topics.label: Ghosts and hauntings
topics.description: Restless spirits, uncanny encounters and places where the dead are said to return.

topics.label: Witches and magic
topics.description: Witchcraft, enchanted books and transformations: stories of powers that rarely come without a condition.

topics.label: Mountain folk and wild people
topics.description: Little mountain dwellers, wild people and the unexpected helpers encountered beyond the village.

topics.label: Dragons, giants and strange beasts
topics.description: Great strength, monstrous visitors and encounters with creatures that leave their mark on the landscape.

topics.label: Treasure and bargains
topics.description: Hidden wealth, promises and uneasy bargains. Read what happens when an opportunity carries an obligation.

topics.label: Mountains, water and weather
topics.description: Storms, glaciers, springs and dangerous crossings, as remembered in the tales of a working landscape.

topics.label: Saints, pilgrims and protection
topics.description: Pilgrimage, prayers, healing and the customs used to seek protection from harm.

topics.label: Village legends and landmarks
topics.description: Stories attached to castles, roads and familiar places, including memories of rulers, disputes and local events.

topics.label: Love, family and home
topics.description: Courtship, marriage, household obligations and the strange visitors who cross a family’s threshold.

topics.label: Wit, courage and good fortune
topics.description: Clever answers, difficult tests and fortunes changed by kindness, courage or a well-timed trick.

topics.label: Animals and the hunt
topics.description: Animal helpers, hunters and creatures whose behaviour gives a warning or conceals another nature.

topics.label: Customs, work and daily life
topics.description: Herding, household work, music and seasonal gatherings: ordinary life at the edge of the extraordinary.

4f92995a49708be40e7ebd81121aaa58deddce90.title: A Bad Nochber
4f92995a49708be40e7ebd81121aaa58deddce90.author: M. Sooder
4f92995a49708be40e7ebd81121aaa58deddce90.summary: An evil roof and a bad Nochber are said to be the worst things one could wish upon a person, people sometimes say.

1fac312781b1b458f19c2c0d7cb993c4c08715ac.title: A Band of Heiden
1fac312781b1b458f19c2c0d7cb993c4c08715ac.author: Josef Müller
1fac312781b1b458f19c2c0d7cb993c4c08715ac.summary: Consisting of four men and three women, the group came one evening to Tresch's house in the Wyler at Gurtnellen and asked for lodging for the night, which was hospitably granted to them according to old custom.

6f7b6f532198677ea0869981469afd061bbabbaa.title: A Battle on the Distelalp
6f7b6f532198677ea0869981469afd061bbabbaa.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
6f7b6f532198677ea0869981469afd061bbabbaa.summary: In Saas, people tell that in very ancient times a band of enemies once intended to invade the country over the Monte Moro.

e87e6d28edc75d924dda0bba1336ad24f635fbbf.title: A Bedsheet as a Sign
e87e6d28edc75d924dda0bba1336ad24f635fbbf.author: M. Sooder
e87e6d28edc75d924dda0bba1336ad24f635fbbf.summary: When the great Sterbet took place, only one man still lived at Ausel and one little woman on the Liemberg. Every day they hung a Lilache outside. It was meant as the sign that they were still alive.

5bdf0c0ae572b8e5b13de03eb17b9a5b8f1eb5d2.title: A Bergmännchen Knows of a Treasure
5bdf0c0ae572b8e5b13de03eb17b9a5b8f1eb5d2.author: Alois Lütolf
5bdf0c0ae572b8e5b13de03eb17b9a5b8f1eb5d2.summary: In Giswil, Canton of Obwalden, a rock called the Giswilerstock rises sheer from an Alp.

a8ddfd3d4952e01718edc436da382f85f8efe366.title: A Bergmännchen Wants to Marry
a8ddfd3d4952e01718edc436da382f85f8efe366.author: Alois Lütolf
a8ddfd3d4952e01718edc436da382f85f8efe366.summary: In the municipality of Menzingen, three farmsteads bear the names Mangeli, meaning want, Sparen, meaning saving, and Hungerhältli.

6f1b1b7482de19a72eb9a55c6c4a419b5aa5bd09.title: A Bergmännlein at Trostburg Castle
6f1b1b7482de19a72eb9a55c6c4a419b5aa5bd09.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
6f1b1b7482de19a72eb9a55c6c4a419b5aa5bd09.summary: About thirty years ago, one evening, boys and girls from the Kulm valley between ten and fourteen years old were playing close below Trostburg Castle near a little bee house.

1aea955e47a2edf1df1d0cc240d712133bd0403b.title: A Bewitched Sow
1aea955e47a2edf1df1d0cc240d712133bd0403b.author: M. Sooder
1aea955e47a2edf1df1d0cc240d712133bd0403b.summary: Rämibabi had a sow with piglets; everything was going well.

80afcd7bdc1ca8ba0c63509807b309a909b809b7.title: A Black Billy Goat in the Stable
80afcd7bdc1ca8ba0c63509807b309a909b809b7.author: M. Sooder
80afcd7bdc1ca8ba0c63509807b309a909b809b7.summary: A Läheme had misfortune in his stable. Sometimes two cows were found in a single Hälslig. Then he brought a black billy goat into the stable. From that time onward, things went well.

869d2578f15a9424f3054fbc6d3553ee353f8fa3.title: A Black Dog
869d2578f15a9424f3054fbc6d3553ee353f8fa3.author: M. Sooder
869d2578f15a9424f3054fbc6d3553ee353f8fa3.summary: In earlier times, people sometimes saw a black Hung in the forest. They said it had been a Bammert, but a spirit in animal form cannot be redeemed.

288bc476ca7cda750b55f59381ca442290b0ced1.title: A Burning Man Lights the Way
288bc476ca7cda750b55f59381ca442290b0ced1.author: Alois Lütolf
288bc476ca7cda750b55f59381ca442290b0ced1.summary: A man from Altbüron had to drive a millstone at night from the Stalten into the village of Altbüron.

f084917f13e98fc178c90e3039a4c012629af323.title: A Capuchin
f084917f13e98fc178c90e3039a4c012629af323.author: Josef Müller
f084917f13e98fc178c90e3039a4c012629af323.summary: A Capuchin from Altdorf wanted to bind a Gespenst in a mountain area of Bürglen.

aac1460f1660bcc9cf24d254b5e0be8e89b365f3.title: A Challenge to Single Combat
aac1460f1660bcc9cf24d254b5e0be8e89b365f3.author: Jakob Kuoni
aac1460f1660bcc9cf24d254b5e0be8e89b365f3.summary: ‘Hujum! Wela chnunt und cheart mi um!’ is the challenge to single combat. It is directed especially at Stubeti-Buben who do not wish to identify themselves upon the road.

a7b19489ddad073288a79cdc84676be68568fb53.title: A Changeling Coin
a7b19489ddad073288a79cdc84676be68568fb53.author: M. Sooder
a7b19489ddad073288a79cdc84676be68568fb53.summary: If one wishes to have a Wächseltaler, one puts a black cat into a sack on Christmas Eve.

037541650f0a38509a533df0e1441f82a3f77b21.title: A Chessi Full of Money
037541650f0a38509a533df0e1441f82a3f77b21.author: Josef Müller
037541650f0a38509a533df0e1441f82a3f77b21.summary: A Chessi full of money is buried in the ground at Bauen in Big Kari's Hostet.

b315840de315c34e061058f633b6a550ec35a931.title: A Child Abducted at Unterschächen
b315840de315c34e061058f633b6a550ec35a931.author: Josef Müller
b315840de315c34e061058f633b6a550ec35a931.summary: The Herger Tonis from Spiringen were spending the grazing season on the Brunni Alp.

43c20d926019f84be8f7f9623f340d7accc138e2.title: A Child Abducted by the Sträggelen
43c20d926019f84be8f7f9623f340d7accc138e2.author: Alois Lütolf

4bce8eab7707833745a9dbce8757b4475083e673.title: A Child Abducted in Surenen
4bce8eab7707833745a9dbce8757b4475083e673.author: Josef Müller
4bce8eab7707833745a9dbce8757b4475083e673.summary: The following story was on everyone’s lips in the eighties of the previous century and was generally held to be true.

7dd453dd65c90b1553fa66bbe1fb579beb7ddc27.title: A Child Follows Its Mother in Death
7dd453dd65c90b1553fa66bbe1fb579beb7ddc27.author: Josef Müller
7dd453dd65c90b1553fa66bbe1fb579beb7ddc27.summary: Nuschi-Hansi in the Winkel at Altdorf had lost his wife.

e92296ee327239a1693fdc66f2873c8a2f26d49e.title: A Child’s Cry
e92296ee327239a1693fdc66f2873c8a2f26d49e.author: Josef Müller
e92296ee327239a1693fdc66f2873c8a2f26d49e.summary: In the mountains around Ursern, people sometimes hear a mournful child’s cry. Bad weather usually sets in, or a misfortune occurs.

084030d65e299d7695befc5340afb65c05520b44.title: A Child’s Vision
084030d65e299d7695befc5340afb65c05520b44.author: Dietrich Jecklin
084030d65e299d7695befc5340afb65c05520b44.summary: A poor man in the Münstertal once tended cattle on the Alpine pastures.

c9b2e46912b377331c3f16c5f997cbfa1b793644.title: A City
c9b2e46912b377331c3f16c5f997cbfa1b793644.author: Jakob Kuoni
c9b2e46912b377331c3f16c5f997cbfa1b793644.summary: According to legend, a city once stood where the little hamlet of Oberrindal lies today, although no trace of it can now be seen.

36a6fd878be510903f632111cbb4dc2580280485.title: A Coffin's Portent
36a6fd878be510903f632111cbb4dc2580280485.author: Josef Müller
36a6fd878be510903f632111cbb4dc2580280485.summary: At Läntergen, Father Imhof was altogether as much at home as in his own house.

3a7d67b9b9b23a75d0ab48b8cf7fafaa244aef88.title: A Cold Bedfellow
3a7d67b9b9b23a75d0ab48b8cf7fafaa244aef88.author: Josef Müller
3a7d67b9b9b23a75d0ab48b8cf7fafaa244aef88.summary: Two men from Gurtnellen—I could give you their names and families—once went crystal hunting in the Fellital.

8609da42a95bb8f33a0093da1825bab86abe5ab8.title: A Corpse Comes to Life
8609da42a95bb8f33a0093da1825bab86abe5ab8.author: Josef Müller
8609da42a95bb8f33a0093da1825bab86abe5ab8.summary: Once, in a farmhouse, a corpse lay in state on a bench in the main room while all the watchers were taking a snack in the adjoining Stübli.

22aa0fca8361f0851a5ed8166b5ca6b22ed132f2.title: A Cowhide Instead of a Witch
22aa0fca8361f0851a5ed8166b5ca6b22ed132f2.author: Alois Lütolf
22aa0fca8361f0851a5ed8166b5ca6b22ed132f2.summary: Just as Zug and Unterwalden have their most notorious witch in Lisi Bossard, so the old land of Schwyz had its own in the Kastenvögtin from the Muotathal, who lived around the middle of the previous century.

b66905d9b93db710a3b77874747f2a4ea8986c06.title: A Dead Man Keeps His Promise
b66905d9b93db710a3b77874747f2a4ea8986c06.author: Josef Müller
b66905d9b93db710a3b77874747f2a4ea8986c06.summary: Within living memory, two brothers or friends lived in the Schmidgasse at Wassen and promised one another that after death they would come and call, ‘I am dead.’ Later one of them emigrated to America.

3cfbb7927e6216570c766e15c047cabe1938ef24.title: A Dead Man Keeps His Word
3cfbb7927e6216570c766e15c047cabe1938ef24.author: Josef Müller

92ef2a72e19a4ad26b1700b2ccf4324498f03673.title: A Dead Mother Fetches Her Children
92ef2a72e19a4ad26b1700b2ccf4324498f03673.author: Josef Müller
92ef2a72e19a4ad26b1700b2ccf4324498f03673.summary: At Törelen in the Schächen Valley, Josefa—the good, caring mother of the household and wife of Councilor Kaspar Herger—had died.

a737654f7d0618dc12f6b9888fd710c745ca06ad.title: A Death Omen at Hohlen Balm
a737654f7d0618dc12f6b9888fd710c745ca06ad.author: Josef Müller
a737654f7d0618dc12f6b9888fd710c745ca06ad.summary: For years old Babä-Sepp of Golzer had spent the grazing season at Hohlen Balm in the Maderanertal.

9f8882a4f0b669941e5536bc052669899543afe0.title: A Deceased Mother's Request
9f8882a4f0b669941e5536bc052669899543afe0.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
9f8882a4f0b669941e5536bc052669899543afe0.summary: It is told from Gasenried in St.

56b63b86b9842fae15112a6274e1b2d716718ed8.title: A Doggelistein
56b63b86b9842fae15112a6274e1b2d716718ed8.author: Alois Lütolf
56b63b86b9842fae15112a6274e1b2d716718ed8.summary: As at Gibelflüh, there was such a Doggelistein—perhaps it still stands—about a quarter of an hour from Winikon beside the forest road to Reiden, near the edge of the woods. It is said to have a pyramidal shape.

367d507de174837649df0a9384f85e0b9b6dc169.title: A Fahriger Banishes Snakes and Dams a Mountain Stream
367d507de174837649df0a9384f85e0b9b6dc169.author: Alois Lütolf
367d507de174837649df0a9384f85e0b9b6dc169.summary: The Schlierenbach in the Wägital region of Schwyz, dangerous in general, had swollen greatly during a terrible storm, but the neighboring landowners made no effort to contain it.

c5456b482426ef2efc8d0351129c6cd46d607d7e.title: A Failed Attempt to Frighten
c5456b482426ef2efc8d0351129c6cd46d607d7e.author: Josef Müller
c5456b482426ef2efc8d0351129c6cd46d607d7e.summary: Wherever Süffibalzi went or stood, he is said to have said a prayer beforehand.

9f91309006e61bd04c18692da2646235b6a2b763.title: A Family of Magicians in Basel
9f91309006e61bd04c18692da2646235b6a2b763.author: C. Kohlrusch
9f91309006e61bd04c18692da2646235b6a2b763.summary: In Basel there was a burgher of an old and distinguished family: Adelbert Meyer.

6a620b8e20d919995d255006d83017c2cdb53389.title: A Farmhand’s Death Omen
6a620b8e20d919995d255006d83017c2cdb53389.author: Josef Müller
6a620b8e20d919995d255006d83017c2cdb53389.summary: Chliser is a small, difficult-to-reach Alp enclosed among rocks on the southwestern slope of the Bristenstock.

adfb37e2eac0be09993157041dce557b6f642be1.title: A Fatal Adventure
adfb37e2eac0be09993157041dce557b6f642be1.author: Josef Müller
adfb37e2eac0be09993157041dce557b6f642be1.summary: More than 100 years ago, a chaplain from Göschenen once stayed much too long with his parish priest in Wassen and did not set out for home until late in the evening.

fd48a798326d5da99bfd9279fcce68c035e0683e.title: A Fiery Apparition
fd48a798326d5da99bfd9279fcce68c035e0683e.author: M. Sooder
fd48a798326d5da99bfd9279fcce68c035e0683e.summary: Once I was fishing in the Langete at night. Then a light followed me as far as the upper smithy. I turned around. It was a life-sized man. Fire flickered out from between his ribs.

18d29d1711de23a417a2d77f840ce81ef6268f7e.title: A Fiery Rider
18d29d1711de23a417a2d77f840ce81ef6268f7e.author: M. Sooder
18d29d1711de23a417a2d77f840ce81ef6268f7e.summary: Mother told me that at twelve o’clock at night, a fiery rider rides around the Altburg on a fiery horse. Then he rides down to the Langete and waters the horse. Afterward he goes back up and disappears.

e1f406eedb37fcfac6ecbef0ede0e340dbdab4c5.title: A Fine Dancer
e1f406eedb37fcfac6ecbef0ede0e340dbdab4c5.author: M. Sooder
e1f406eedb37fcfac6ecbef0ede0e340dbdab4c5.summary: A girl wanted to go dancing.

d27d016a976cacd45734db920e8e6a2c8d0f8907.title: A Fire Announces Itself
d27d016a976cacd45734db920e8e6a2c8d0f8907.author: Josef Müller
d27d016a976cacd45734db920e8e6a2c8d0f8907.summary: In the house in the Hostet (Helgossingen) at Spiringen, a Maitschi often had to gaumen the younger children while the parents were away.

7f390f235b2ad3a00a3071b931634bb2bed08f6d.title: A Footbridge for the Dead Woman
7f390f235b2ad3a00a3071b931634bb2bed08f6d.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
7f390f235b2ad3a00a3071b931634bb2bed08f6d.summary: At Erlinsbach, a Wöchnerin had died and been buried.

ec5936e85612a68f4a6a440ac305698097544d32.title: A Foretelling of the White Death
ec5936e85612a68f4a6a440ac305698097544d32.author: Josef Müller
ec5936e85612a68f4a6a440ac305698097544d32.summary: At nightfall a few decades ago, the Älpler of Gufern in the Maderanertal once saw a forearm bearing a torch float through the darkness.

336ad2a20cc9031d49c8b0386a901a9f6801d274.title: A Ghost (Hospental)
336ad2a20cc9031d49c8b0386a901a9f6801d274.author: Josef Müller
336ad2a20cc9031d49c8b0386a901a9f6801d274.summary: A ghost in a Hospental locksmith’s house takes a child from its cradle and is eventually confined to an alley.

39137f56aa928e1ae1f87e8a3f41c82f49da9e7f.title: A Ghost (Realp)
39137f56aa928e1ae1f87e8a3f41c82f49da9e7f.author: Josef Müller
39137f56aa928e1ae1f87e8a3f41c82f49da9e7f.summary: A brief local record remembers a ghost banished beneath the house steps at Realp.

e6fbfc1293e94e369c943b6fafef2f184b1a3999.title: A Ghost Foretells an Earthquake
e6fbfc1293e94e369c943b6fafef2f184b1a3999.author: C. Kohlrusch
e6fbfc1293e94e369c943b6fafef2f184b1a3999.summary: It was in the years 1701 or 1702, when the land of Glarus was shaken by some 30 or 40 earthquakes, that at midnight an honorable man and citizen in the Linth valley heard an unknown voice call his name.

a92b6e21240a216f92aa39e20b04b9f05bd13e61.title: A Ghost Like a Cowhide
a92b6e21240a216f92aa39e20b04b9f05bd13e61.author: Josef Müller
a92b6e21240a216f92aa39e20b04b9f05bd13e61.summary: On Arni above Silenen, a solitary Manndli lived all winter in an old little house, where a ghost disturbed him.

1a38c193298a1be921944d1421ad82e743516651.title: A Ghost Pursues Fruit Thieves
1a38c193298a1be921944d1421ad82e743516651.author: Alois Lütolf
1a38c193298a1be921944d1421ad82e743516651.summary: In former times, a yarn-boiling hut stood near the village of Grossdietwil.

315849ad378f1864469b088d2134e6dd32b9270c.title: A Ghostly Cat on the Frutt
315849ad378f1864469b088d2134e6dd32b9270c.author: Josef Müller
315849ad378f1864469b088d2134e6dd32b9270c.summary: A ghostly cat on the Frutt near Beroldingen at Seelisberg attracted much attention. Many stories were told about it. (Nineteenth century.)

ca1b2b394aeac78703bc3e01b419cb54b9ccb7ee.title: A Girl Foretells Her Own Death
ca1b2b394aeac78703bc3e01b419cb54b9ccb7ee.author: Josef Müller
ca1b2b394aeac78703bc3e01b419cb54b9ccb7ee.summary: Josef Maria Tresch in Bristen, called ‘schwarz Tresch,’ went to visit his sweetheart one evening.

031a16b28a166adfc76f45bd521e4601d65ba19a.title: A Girl Torments a Woman
031a16b28a166adfc76f45bd521e4601d65ba19a.author: M. Sooder
031a16b28a166adfc76f45bd521e4601d65ba19a.summary: A woman thought that the Doggeli was tormenting her. Then someone told her that she should stick a knife into its cheek. In the morning, the neighbor's girl was lying on the ground; her head had been cut off.

eb0634ac0520f32e73225e47296dda926bfc9fc9.title: A Girl’s Vision
eb0634ac0520f32e73225e47296dda926bfc9fc9.author: Dietrich Jecklin
eb0634ac0520f32e73225e47296dda926bfc9fc9.summary: In former times several houses stood in Tscharina above Untervaz.

09a931c506f54d057900e6b13a31a1d249f478b8.title: A Godchild's Death Omen
09a931c506f54d057900e6b13a31a1d249f478b8.author: Josef Müller
09a931c506f54d057900e6b13a31a1d249f478b8.summary: We were still living at Holzerberg in Bürglen.

c1c22e143a42ed6638551c8c844fca6f90c283f2.title: A Gottvärine as a Mill Hand
c1c22e143a42ed6638551c8c844fca6f90c283f2.author: Theodor Vernaleken
c1c22e143a42ed6638551c8c844fca6f90c283f2.summary: The goblin-like people called ‘Gottvärinen’ or ‘Gottwärinen,’ who sometimes associate with the inhabitants of the valley, are distinguished by their small stature and are kindly and helpful toward humans.

5a6c6cfde22493174f117135c2cf7da53b90f443.title: A Grave Warning (Mels, SG)
5a6c6cfde22493174f117135c2cf7da53b90f443.author: Jakob Kuoni
5a6c6cfde22493174f117135c2cf7da53b90f443.summary: Once a Senn intended no longer to pray the Ave Maria and therefore remained in the hut at the appointed time, where he mocked the prayer with the other farmhands.

9fea325ca7ee0751f6460f4777cfecbd2a9b390c.title: A Gray Cat
9fea325ca7ee0751f6460f4777cfecbd2a9b390c.author: M. Sooder
9fea325ca7ee0751f6460f4777cfecbd2a9b390c.summary: Once, a boy went to visit a girl.

db5d8c031457e6faabc1f6c02dda6f957972c0d8.title: A Great Black Man
db5d8c031457e6faabc1f6c02dda6f957972c0d8.author: Josef Müller
db5d8c031457e6faabc1f6c02dda6f957972c0d8.summary: A great black man without a head encountered my aunt—who lived to be nearly 80 years old—once as she walked from the large Lusser house high in the village along the little path toward the Höfli.

7023c2ee0b25272e2612005c42408d5fa0a24f5d.title: A Hardness in the Scythe
7023c2ee0b25272e2612005c42408d5fa0a24f5d.author: M. Sooder
7023c2ee0b25272e2612005c42408d5fa0a24f5d.summary: The Häulehans suddenly had a Herti in his Sägetze and could no longer mow. Then he took a white-hazel stick and thrashed the Sägetze. After that, it worked again.

7b7d0c66af7f6244b2fbbe23be91a6886505b82e.title: A Hare and Yet No Hare
7b7d0c66af7f6244b2fbbe23be91a6886505b82e.author: M. Sooder
7b7d0c66af7f6244b2fbbe23be91a6886505b82e.summary: In my younger years I was a farmhand.

ff0019b92850c7f6afc17a2254f5a0ae62f7d623.title: A Haunting Defeated by Cursing
ff0019b92850c7f6afc17a2254f5a0ae62f7d623.author: Josef Müller

3b9e0cc70c9bc0c3de26eb2606e4859274469115.summary: When Ahasver first crossed the Alps in his eternal wandering, he chose the Grimsel as his pass.

03696b16d28a24d63dcee57a1fccbf195f50693c.summary: My mother often used to help with the washing.

a8cd20c3170ff492a8f2d684cc3ada33c2af9c2d.summary: Once, I was making my Chehr and approached a farmhouse.

7d14dfb43ff3e8b1252e8678d327c2ebd4f8c2e9.summary: In one place there was a farmer who was nid ganz e sufere—not entirely clean or respectable.

337ba1e4e60add7a346ef0d66c9b94331d339449.title: Antusuhans

337ba1e4e60add7a346ef0d66c9b94331d339449.summary: The late Antusuhans—the Hans belonging to Anton Anthanmatten—was a fine, upright man.

6aa929f545b919128ad7af6c8b00c43c87e21d42.author: Alois Lütolf
6aa929f545b919128ad7af6c8b00c43c87e21d42.summary: A child of noble birth lost her parents at an early age.

49bfa4c5477960842305b394dc02e76e1ba8984c.summary: At Fiechte, a man lay dying.

67eb488f025ceabb89ba544fa8fa0c8cff089b9d.title: At the Biberhoger

3268e2389cf027e2e625ff79b9fb90c6e75771cf.title: At the G'hirmistein

dfeb33a8c44e96b5b5dbe26982ea4a8737c58b07.author: Meinrad Lienert
dfeb33a8c44e96b5b5dbe26982ea4a8737c58b07.summary: One would never guess from the pleasant hills around Bassersdorf how haunted that region is.

b757466b2e0fa345abf9322d0321f13d62418f6d.title: At the Holy Beeches
b757466b2e0fa345abf9322d0321f13d62418f6d.author: Jakob Kuoni
b757466b2e0fa345abf9322d0321f13d62418f6d.summary: Bad Buchen near Oberuzwil was once called ‘at the holy beeches.’ This name undoubtedly points back to a legend that has, however, been lost.

275276858e1bbec4a94652fa5f24d30eb3348644.title: At the Loom
275276858e1bbec4a94652fa5f24d30eb3348644.author: M. Sooder
275276858e1bbec4a94652fa5f24d30eb3348644.summary: In one place, people wove in the evening until twelve.

5de4a4f2fdc45069253a2f68ddadafa2a1393c76.title: At the Lölibrüggli
5de4a4f2fdc45069253a2f68ddadafa2a1393c76.author: M. Sooder
5de4a4f2fdc45069253a2f68ddadafa2a1393c76.summary: Two people were crossing the Lölibrüggli at night.

37cc3c495dce2f12bd4f124efc849b0f717ae0c9.title: At the Pasture Gate
37cc3c495dce2f12bd4f124efc849b0f717ae0c9.author: M. Sooder
37cc3c495dce2f12bd4f124efc849b0f717ae0c9.summary: On a pasture, there was a gate that opened and closed by itself whenever people passed through. The business was not proceeding by natural means.

96d22f069a529aa56f7e7c67a43338acfb4bcdbc.title: At the Road Junction
96d22f069a529aa56f7e7c67a43338acfb4bcdbc.author: Josef Müller
96d22f069a529aa56f7e7c67a43338acfb4bcdbc.summary: At the Dreiangeli estate in Altdorf, perhaps some 30–40 years ago, a woman from the neighborhood often saw a priest walking back and forth at night from 11–12 o’clock with a book under his arm.

1f358e419ae2b9e0776ed5d61ca98cf1a44d3421.title: At the Schreia
1f358e419ae2b9e0776ed5d61ca98cf1a44d3421.author: Jakob Kuoni
1f358e419ae2b9e0776ed5d61ca98cf1a44d3421.summary: Above the Schreia bridge, between Camperneis and Halbmil, before great floods one hears the brook being bailed out and sand being thrown at midnight, a consequence of old disputes over Schöpf-und Wuhrpflicht. J. B. Stoop

e07fa5026b5984c21755657b7a9b3c87e59df65a.title: At the Schutzenbirnbaum
e07fa5026b5984c21755657b7a9b3c87e59df65a.author: Jakob Kuoni
e07fa5026b5984c21755657b7a9b3c87e59df65a.summary: At the Schutzenbirnbaum, between Rebstein and Balgach, a sinister black figure was also seen at night, driving the sweat of fear onto many a person's brow.

34cc430f6d8c903bcbed33abbdcc522c13a6f8a4.title: At the Urnerloch
34cc430f6d8c903bcbed33abbdcc522c13a6f8a4.author: Josef Müller
34cc430f6d8c903bcbed33abbdcc522c13a6f8a4.summary: It was never free of uncanny trouble at the Urnerloch.

8a9268674005ba1bddbf72cfc51db346d5c27a74.title: At the Washing
8a9268674005ba1bddbf72cfc51db346d5c27a74.author: M. Sooder
8a9268674005ba1bddbf72cfc51db346d5c27a74.summary: Once some women were washing on a heilige Obe.

9563b503ff5f6f916c761bb85c8b84a1faf5d67d.title: At Urschebech
9563b503ff5f6f916c761bb85c8b84a1faf5d67d.author: M. Sooder
9563b503ff5f6f916c761bb85c8b84a1faf5d67d.summary: A farmer z’Urschebech also saw such a Lichezug at night. That very night, his hair fell out, and from then onward he bore a completely bald head.

5fb431f29023d0912f4b8856aca1306be5c371ae.title: At Wischenwassern in Guretzmettlen in the Meien Valley
5fb431f29023d0912f4b8856aca1306be5c371ae.author: Josef Müller
5fb431f29023d0912f4b8856aca1306be5c371ae.summary: 1. At Wischenwassern in Guretzmettlen in the Meien Valley, something often threw pebbles at the Älpler. At Färnigen, too, it pelted travelers with stones at night. After dark, a cat crouched upon every fence stake there.

318bba7d7f710d22081cb584a70e0e291e27e26f.title: Atoning Säumerseelen
318bba7d7f710d22081cb584a70e0e291e27e26f.author: Theodor Vernaleken
318bba7d7f710d22081cb584a70e0e291e27e26f.summary: From time to time in Graubünden, on the Furka between Ursern and Upper Valais, and in other places, one encounters patches of snow that look as red as though they had been soaked in red wine.

e64046886666b3b0de9102ca20c83fb4bf924dbb.title: Away through the Air!
e64046886666b3b0de9102ca20c83fb4bf924dbb.author: M. Sooder
e64046886666b3b0de9102ca20c83fb4bf924dbb.summary: By the Galgelöli, the citizens have their fields.

6c3e2589e8bd1669a7096e1d84605d05bca8e70a.title: Away, Away
6c3e2589e8bd1669a7096e1d84605d05bca8e70a.author: Alois Lütolf
6c3e2589e8bd1669a7096e1d84605d05bca8e70a.summary: High on Uri’s Arniberg near Gurtnellen lies the Leutschachalp, a long, gloomy valley.

c13e737ea638ed50eec45b5b9462aeec01297854.title: Banished
c13e737ea638ed50eec45b5b9462aeec01297854.author: Jakob Kuoni
c13e737ea638ed50eec45b5b9462aeec01297854.summary: The Capuchins can banish spirits that become troublesome in inhabited places to a lonely spot.

f7b7d125cc26494e4dddda812639813943549244.title: Baptismal Font of the Church of Rein
f7b7d125cc26494e4dddda812639813943549244.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
f7b7d125cc26494e4dddda812639813943549244.summary: A young lady was banished into it and could be freed with three kisses.

f06dfafcbd7c691859e6096ff10bdcd3983ef158.title: Baron Conrad von Sellenbüren Founds Engelberg Monastery
f06dfafcbd7c691859e6096ff10bdcd3983ef158.author: C. Kohlrusch
f06dfafcbd7c691859e6096ff10bdcd3983ef158.summary: When Conrad, Baron von Sellenbüren, once traveled with his people through the valley where Wolfenschiessen and Grafenort lie and climbed the Hennenberg, the region pleased him so well that he resolved to build a monastery for men there.

ef671b603ff4d0a096ecade27f2ee136211cbaeb.title: Baron Heinrich of Rhäzüns
ef671b603ff4d0a096ecade27f2ee136211cbaeb.author: Dietrich Jecklin
ef671b603ff4d0a096ecade27f2ee136211cbaeb.summary: At Valendas Castle in 1452, the people sat in judgment upon Freiherr Jörg (Brun) von Räzüns.

50ce8a084edc1ae697752ad1fbccd58c3721d6d9.title: Baschi Frech
50ce8a084edc1ae697752ad1fbccd58c3721d6d9.author: Alois Lütolf
50ce8a084edc1ae697752ad1fbccd58c3721d6d9.summary: This happened more than three hundred years ago.

292f10d055d3ba25af403058d469f4b3b9511b29.title: Bean, Bean, I Will Cut You
292f10d055d3ba25af403058d469f4b3b9511b29.author: Dietrich Jecklin
292f10d055d3ba25af403058d469f4b3b9511b29.summary: Three brothers, the children of poor people, went abroad to earn their bread.

67650cdec98d6b139a828d4a65d1d68eca15266e.title: Beating the Water in the Little Pond
67650cdec98d6b139a828d4a65d1d68eca15266e.author: M. Sooder
67650cdec98d6b139a828d4a65d1d68eca15266e.summary: My father's brother Hans once saw, on a night around New Year, how Chasper and Rees, his neighbors, were beating the water in the Weierli.

da38393ed52f3c93c66a243c818585bb4f3ac1de.title: Beatus and the Dwarfs
da38393ed52f3c93c66a243c818585bb4f3ac1de.author: Hermann Hartmann
da38393ed52f3c93c66a243c818585bb4f3ac1de.summary: When Beatus preached the Gospel in the Oberland, there were still little dwarfs, small ‘gesegnete Leutlein,’ or Bergmännchen, who lived in hidden rocky clefts.

ff14b5e6b4e63e4828f20b982aae00e176237ad7.title: Beatus Drives Away the Dragon
ff14b5e6b4e63e4828f20b982aae00e176237ad7.author: Hermann Hartmann
ff14b5e6b4e63e4828f20b982aae00e176237ad7.summary: A visiting preacher promises to drive a dragon from its cave beside the lake.

7ece7fa2b260605c618cb72412a4fab696797c4b.title: Beatus's Wundermantel
7ece7fa2b260605c618cb72412a4fab696797c4b.author: Hermann Hartmann
7ece7fa2b260605c618cb72412a4fab696797c4b.summary: Beatus once traveled from his rock dwelling, before which he had built a chapel for the inhabitants' salvation, to the people in the Üchtland on the opposite shore of Lake Thun.

ad844bf545cd2653a16deaf346bcb5087566049f.summary: a) In spring, when the cattle were let out onto the meadows for the first time, it was still customary in Unterwalden until quite recently to light several pieces of firewood in front of the stable, or at the place through which the…

73bd8b84fbfc13edec35d7a48bd0de72b2a042f8.summary: Johann Jakob Scheuchzer writes in his natural history of Switzerland, published in the year 1746:

2f45860891f8f08c72468dcbcfd5d9f0ca6ca9cc.title: Bergmännli
2f45860891f8f08c72468dcbcfd5d9f0ca6ca9cc.author: Jakob Kuoni
2f45860891f8f08c72468dcbcfd5d9f0ca6ca9cc.summary: White-clad Bergmännli are said once to have lived among the rocks between Ganterschwil and Duferswil.

1e90ecf18f18fa3b30d4db9aee8d2285208bc294.title: Bertha of Baldegg
1e90ecf18f18fa3b30d4db9aee8d2285208bc294.author: Ernst L. Rochholz
1e90ecf18f18fa3b30d4db9aee8d2285208bc294.summary: As fighting reaches the castles near Lake Baldegg, a widow vows to build a chapel if her child survives. Fog and a rising stream turn the attackers aside.

8a572432ab18fbcb3a1cb850b0e743b680de256a.title: Between Two Cliffs
8a572432ab18fbcb3a1cb850b0e743b680de256a.author: Josef Müller
8a572432ab18fbcb3a1cb850b0e743b680de256a.summary: A man from Silenen had paid interest in Erstfeld.

647513e0e05d14d3a53cda1fa56e06f9102a450d.title: Beulentod and the Procession of the Dead
647513e0e05d14d3a53cda1fa56e06f9102a450d.author: Alois Lütolf
647513e0e05d14d3a53cda1fa56e06f9102a450d.summary: From 1610 to 1612 a terrible plague, the Beulentod, raged in Switzerland.

cdf887a24f482e46487389fecaaed4e5318d0378.title: Bewitched
cdf887a24f482e46487389fecaaed4e5318d0378.author: Jakob Kuoni
cdf887a24f482e46487389fecaaed4e5318d0378.summary: On the Wildenberg Alp, an evil spirit once appeared in the middle of the night.

07330c883395693640af415f601c7777ca7f066b.summary: The widow B ...... in Fläsch shared a stable with a neighbor whose wife was a witch.

b71b399006d33e30ee8021fc297a9662c5cf5ccd.title: Binding People
b71b399006d33e30ee8021fc297a9662c5cf5ccd.author: M. Sooder
b71b399006d33e30ee8021fc297a9662c5cf5ccd.summary: Another time, the boys were in the Hoschtert after the apples. Suddenly, they heard something rushing over the paving. What do you give, what do you have—they jumped up and fled!

72406342984e2d8d609c4277c3d2f82685d9162c.title: Binding the Fire
72406342984e2d8d609c4277c3d2f82685d9162c.author: M. Sooder
72406342984e2d8d609c4277c3d2f82685d9162c.summary: In eighteen hundred and thirty-four Huttel burned.

91dc6de03317ac49f084f26bf74b96a0f5f287a6.author: M. Sooder
91dc6de03317ac49f084f26bf74b96a0f5f287a6.summary: Moosjoggi was a passionate Tübeler and once bought some beautifully schwarzgstieleti Tube. He boasted that they were not merely Schopfjoggine that always sat at home.

04cc286a14129c2c113e0a38c77996b19477800f.title: Black Eichmann in Wohlen
04cc286a14129c2c113e0a38c77996b19477800f.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz

ddb0517eae0d5ee053085ac14cea9406ff3e8d23.title: Blatten Castle
ddb0517eae0d5ee053085ac14cea9406ff3e8d23.author: Jakob Kuoni
ddb0517eae0d5ee053085ac14cea9406ff3e8d23.summary: In the time of King Rudolf, Blatten Castle passed to the lords of Ramswag.

bc7f412d36a23943047fd45da24021a605688be0.title: Blazing Skeleton
bc7f412d36a23943047fd45da24021a605688be0.author: Alois Lütolf
bc7f412d36a23943047fd45da24021a605688be0.summary: I have been told by a trustworthy person that once, unexpectedly in the night, a dead body stood upright before her—nothing but bones, in the form in which Death is painted.

16921db7cbb1def96983492317be8bfbf30da062.title: Blikker von Steinach
16921db7cbb1def96983492317be8bfbf30da062.author: C. Kohlrusch
16921db7cbb1def96983492317be8bfbf30da062.summary: A noble family of knights once lived at Steinach Castle, not far from the little town of Arbon.

42e501693cc9964ce84366b92148c8af54a09b7c.title: Blood Vengeance
42e501693cc9964ce84366b92148c8af54a09b7c.author: Jakob Kuoni
42e501693cc9964ce84366b92148c8af54a09b7c.summary: At the time when the Vättnerberg was still inhabited, a house stood in the Spina; its foundation remains visible today.

4fe95e55fc1688678f81e2775fe45d8f07015db8.title: Bläseli from the Black Forest
4fe95e55fc1688678f81e2775fe45d8f07015db8.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
4fe95e55fc1688678f81e2775fe45d8f07015db8.summary: I had stuffed my ears into my fur cap and taken my nose in my hand—that was how I went one winter to spend an evening at an old Freiamt farmer’s Stubete.

8595b2cf211f1dca53f62eb1caf57cbb4df25336.title: Blüemlisalp
8595b2cf211f1dca53f62eb1caf57cbb4df25336.author: Theodor Vernaleken
8595b2cf211f1dca53f62eb1caf57cbb4df25336.summary: Many an Alp that was formerly full of flowers—a Blümelisalp—has preserved the memory of dreadful glaciation that broke over it suddenly.

9f553317bd9389ead525a23ed99677d8cf3e1f13.title: Body and Soul
9f553317bd9389ead525a23ed99677d8cf3e1f13.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9f553317bd9389ead525a23ed99677d8cf3e1f13.summary: It was during the Reformation in Bünden when, in a village in the Engadine, a little beggar man lay near his end.

e7228a4e5c30c3afdb3cc9421add47313c06ad67.title: Bogeys for Children
e7228a4e5c30c3afdb3cc9421add47313c06ad67.author: Alois Lütolf
e7228a4e5c30c3afdb3cc9421add47313c06ad67.summary: a) On the Hundsrügge, a long hill at the aforementioned place between the Rotsee and Buchrain, there once lived a wicked woman.

3655f1276cc259d9e61fc342d0cfd1d135130441.title: Botti’s Grave
3655f1276cc259d9e61fc342d0cfd1d135130441.author: C. Kohlrusch
3655f1276cc259d9e61fc342d0cfd1d135130441.summary: In the Grauholz, not far from the country road to Bern, two age-gray granite pillars stand on the mossy forest floor, with a mound dug over by treasure hunters rising between them.

fced19c4679611293013388b3d35be86f44c5560.title: Bound Fast
fced19c4679611293013388b3d35be86f44c5560.author: Jakob Kuoni
fced19c4679611293013388b3d35be86f44c5560.summary: A farmer came to the Küsterli—the sexton—and complained that someone had stolen the hay from his meadow.

2c0830c40c6ecff668ec3f1b89a1526061cf261f.title: Boundary Spirits
2c0830c40c6ecff668ec3f1b89a1526061cf261f.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
2c0830c40c6ecff668ec3f1b89a1526061cf261f.summary: At a certain house near Uerkheim, a light becomes visible beside a field boundary on stormy nights, and at every turn of the year it becomes a fiery man carrying a shovel.

9fca662c80d55760d2f5845cd6ae7d60b32f586b.title: Bread and Evil Powers
9fca662c80d55760d2f5845cd6ae7d60b32f586b.author: Josef Müller
9fca662c80d55760d2f5845cd6ae7d60b32f586b.summary: When a beggar once spent the night in a Gaden, a ghost came in and said to him, ‘If you did not have a little piece of bread in your sack, I would tear you into rags and shreds.’ A ghost at Rynächt shouted the same thing to an…

40ba39032bb756619559a87f57f1ceeaf0057f0a.title: Bread Given Away
40ba39032bb756619559a87f57f1ceeaf0057f0a.author: M. Sooder
40ba39032bb756619559a87f57f1ceeaf0057f0a.summary: In one place there was a farmer’s wife who begrudged the poor everything; she preferred the pigs. Every day she put large pieces of bread into the pigs’ trough, while twisting charity and greed the wrong way.

fa4e58fd27d2f1b23e7a14d5eac5614e5863ac5f.title: Bringing the Wasting Sickness
fa4e58fd27d2f1b23e7a14d5eac5614e5863ac5f.author: M. Sooder
fa4e58fd27d2f1b23e7a14d5eac5614e5863ac5f.summary: It was more than a hundred years ago.

5fb86b099f719acade372872173376ede9e2188a.title: Bristen Treasures and the Like
5fb86b099f719acade372872173376ede9e2188a.author: Josef Müller
5fb86b099f719acade372872173376ede9e2188a.summary: a) High inside the Bristenstock, a Vynediger revealed, there is a cave. Pure gold drips from its ceiling, and a Chochchessi has been placed beneath it; the kettle has long been full and is running over.

85a78a28d75b34bc6cdf6eed3298b3eeb09c5f9d.title: Brunnenhans on the Giblour in the Canton of Fribourg
85a78a28d75b34bc6cdf6eed3298b3eeb09c5f9d.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
85a78a28d75b34bc6cdf6eed3298b3eeb09c5f9d.summary: While the Sennen on the Giblour fled into the hut before the storm that had broken loose, one of them, Brunnenhans, was still on the path, bringing up from the valley the provisions ordered long before.

1bd227ed2efe056005af1526515d9ff4b72956ac.title: Buchlisberg near Schöftland
1bd227ed2efe056005af1526515d9ff4b72956ac.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
1bd227ed2efe056005af1526515d9ff4b72956ac.summary: There was a forest over whose ownership a nobleman and the municipality of Schöftland quarreled until the outbreak of the French Revolution.

bccf4660466f1049d2d5669b64fe1bd30d8877d4.title: Building the Bridge
bccf4660466f1049d2d5669b64fe1bd30d8877d4.author: Dietrich Jecklin
bccf4660466f1049d2d5669b64fe1bd30d8877d4.summary: The Vetaner once resolved to build a bridge across the Inn below their territory.

29664f63e19671f906d80244f80fef1e41d39e87.title: Bull Heads That Ward Off Lightning
29664f63e19671f906d80244f80fef1e41d39e87.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
29664f63e19671f906d80244f80fef1e41d39e87.summary: Peter Karli’s house at Dottikon in the Freiamt stands on the road to Anglikon, on the left at the turn toward the village of Hägglingen.

c9c7c04d6b0d93234b767dd4e2e557e129ba7cc1.title: Burgfluh in the Frickthal
c9c7c04d6b0d93234b767dd4e2e557e129ba7cc1.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
c9c7c04d6b0d93234b767dd4e2e557e129ba7cc1.summary: If a knight on a white horse is seen below at the Burgfluh, there will be a great war; the same is prophesied by the wild hunter Burkhard, who only recently allowed himself to be seen again in the Frickthal.

d7fdd59f38e4ad89429fab20a930cff8236b223b.title: Buried Alive
d7fdd59f38e4ad89429fab20a930cff8236b223b.author: Josef Müller
d7fdd59f38e4ad89429fab20a930cff8236b223b.summary: People in Altdorf told of a woman who lived in the house formerly belonging to the Crivelli family, now the home of Fürsprech Karl Huber.

8924448694a8b1ca59ae85413dead9452cf67d11.title: Buried in Spreuer
8924448694a8b1ca59ae85413dead9452cf67d11.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
8924448694a8b1ca59ae85413dead9452cf67d11.summary: In the city of Baden there lived a wealthy grain merchant who knew how to force his wares upon poor people at high prices and, during times of famine, often sold them sacks of grain that were as much as half filled with Spreuer.

ccf6530d91548b18f97ab7a7ecb2681d9dddb968.title: Burkhard's Fountain in Beinwil
ccf6530d91548b18f97ab7a7ecb2681d9dddb968.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
ccf6530d91548b18f97ab7a7ecb2681d9dddb968.summary: The parish of Beinwil, with a ruined castle site of the same name, formerly the property of the monastic foundation of Muri, lies near Meienberg in the Freie Ämter of Aargau.

c8c53221edc66ca37ec41ad6f5d63704a56c63ab.title: Burning Mandli and Good Works
c8c53221edc66ca37ec41ad6f5d63704a56c63ab.author: Alois Lütolf
c8c53221edc66ca37ec41ad6f5d63704a56c63ab.summary: a) On a pitch-dark night, a councilor was making his way home from Stans to Ennetbürgen.

3c5628ab0c462aeaeac45bf0dba16199559fbb06.title: Busskirch
3c5628ab0c462aeaeac45bf0dba16199559fbb06.author: Jakob Kuoni
3c5628ab0c462aeaeac45bf0dba16199559fbb06.summary: The church at Busskirch is said to stand on the foundations of a Roman building. According to the legend, even a Roman pagan temple stood here in the time of Gallus.

8670f7bb416f7823e961b464428fa8cc3875598c.title: But Not the Accursed Schimmel
8670f7bb416f7823e961b464428fa8cc3875598c.author: Jakob Kuoni

f9332be644949803f3d1b029cda4784036d68e7e.author: M. Sooder

e4553f4ddee0eab05b0ed44c00fa4554901dea40.author: M. Sooder
e4553f4ddee0eab05b0ed44c00fa4554901dea40.summary: Once I was walking at night with someone toward Eriswil.

ad8077b2c3f4a8b5ae6474f22c9c27a8f2bc934a.summary: On Oberprod, 100 years ago, there lived a man as strong as a tree, Bartholomäus Lutz.

c31c8fe13adf85b99963639a54fc71048cadefa1.author: Josef Müller
c31c8fe13adf85b99963639a54fc71048cadefa1.summary: A rowdy company in an inn at Isental mocked religion and made jokes about it.

a5ddc95d97a39d51a396efcd26eefa5f20cffb8e.summary: One of the many hills called Homberg in the Aargau Jura lies toward Oberfrick, close to the part of the village called In der Gipf.

c32119375cc0e8194904b08574199ce6cbbd8905.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
c32119375cc0e8194904b08574199ce6cbbd8905.summary: Above Botenwil, a village in the Uerkheim valley in the district of Zofingen, lie shrub-covered remains of walls on a hill, once the manor house of a violent Vogt.

957e4389d6138e9bc029125b5a955c7e4e6de9d5.author: Josef Müller
957e4389d6138e9bc029125b5a955c7e4e6de9d5.summary: Shoemaker Zacharias Imholz found a large, coal-black cat highly suspicious when it blocked his way one evening behind Hergerig at Spiringen, beside a marker stone, and stared at him with grass-green, sparkling eyes.

60ad5a5b9327299522d011a6b9a1d98487c25cbc.title: Catillon la Toascha, the Hunchbacked Käthe
60ad5a5b9327299522d011a6b9a1d98487c25cbc.author: C. Kohlrusch
60ad5a5b9327299522d011a6b9a1d98487c25cbc.summary: On the southeastern slope of the Gibloux, an extension of the Jorat range, lie the villages of Vuisternens-en-Ogoz, Villarslod, and Rueyres-Saint-Laurent, on the right of the road from Fribourg to Bulle.

7df51603dfb175fc1347a7b03ddb21f253bf9ed6.title: Cats Are Merry
7df51603dfb175fc1347a7b03ddb21f253bf9ed6.author: M. Sooder
7df51603dfb175fc1347a7b03ddb21f253bf9ed6.summary: Once, late in the evening, a man passed a house that had long stood empty. Suddenly he heard noise inside, went to the little shutter, looked in, and saw a heap of cats upon the stove. Their Maudi was there as well.

1779bf63b2b108891364933f5bf3e9efdd55cbff.author: Jakob Kuoni
1779bf63b2b108891364933f5bf3e9efdd55cbff.summary: On this side of the Rhine lived a physician who had never studied, but who could do many things denied to the others.

832e5581fb640babe4a9bbef79630ab52c47c0f6.title: Chamois Hunters Who Died in Accidents Hunt After Death
832e5581fb640babe4a9bbef79630ab52c47c0f6.author: C. Kohlrusch
832e5581fb640babe4a9bbef79630ab52c47c0f6.summary: High on the Schreckhorn, as in other Alpine regions, sounds like the report of a fired rifle can often be heard among the glaciers.

99d2f2077a667d8bc808a4cfca7ce8ea8f50f4e7.title: Changes in the Alpine Pastures

99d2f2077a667d8bc808a4cfca7ce8ea8f50f4e7.summary: In ancient times our Alp pastures extended much higher and were used far more intensively than they are today. In many places where only sheep and goats now graze, cows were driven up in those days.

8b860ef4f16ddef894ae6af2a6f92f641b99a704.title: Charlemagne and the Serpent
8b860ef4f16ddef894ae6af2a6f92f641b99a704.author: C. Kohlrusch

421260ba88688521897f07c4b32b5fd4c54b5a19.title: Cheap
421260ba88688521897f07c4b32b5fd4c54b5a19.author: Jakob Kuoni
421260ba88688521897f07c4b32b5fd4c54b5a19.summary: The beautiful mountain estates above Brunnadern, on the right side of the Necker, were once sold for three cups full of flour. N. Senn, diary.

b01f09322832912f4004f6a1f721ba9a0520d764.title: Childlessness Incurred and Atoned For

b01f09322832912f4004f6a1f721ba9a0520d764.summary: Long ago there lived a married couple who were childless—through their own fault.

4f3d99e6afc9538a4b7747078ae04cf483965c05.title: Chilier, the Wild Hunter
4f3d99e6afc9538a4b7747078ae04cf483965c05.author: C. Kohlrusch
4f3d99e6afc9538a4b7747078ae04cf483965c05.summary: In the village of Grandvillars there once lived a passionate hunter named Chilier.

fbfd5c1889fabbd5f97ccacc1914f0dca95a787f.summary: There was once a young herdsman who wished to marry and knew three sisters, each as beautiful as the others, so that choosing was difficult for him and he could not decide to give any one of them preference.

2d3a89434e0444051cc393e1f12db74ff0d65a57.summary: A wandering scholar who had learned magic in Salamanca once came during his travels through the world, which he undertook with the Devil’s aid, to Lake Türlen.

7200e3b981d8bcd8f58f1102ab734ea2791f5c4c.summary: This lies on the Türlersee in the Canton of Zurich in the direction of Heferschwil.

5e7e8c5024ef9292fd172103645e568016808e3f.title: Cries as an Omen of Misfortune

5e7e8c5024ef9292fd172103645e568016808e3f.summary: At the Kilchberg near Andermatt, a strange howling and shouting could sometimes be heard, though no one knew who caused it.

ea36d2266c7cd7b9344d7526170afcbb696d84b7.summary: Now crown the bare head of rock. —

ec50a2ff004bcecc9f3a35118c93eef4ac2b689d.summary: At Haldi lived a man who treated his wife with dreadful harshness and cruelty.

f70bd16c8ba80da9dc2088afb721725fa8edf9f6.title: Dancing Fires
f70bd16c8ba80da9dc2088afb721725fa8edf9f6.author: M. Sooder
f70bd16c8ba80da9dc2088afb721725fa8edf9f6.summary: At midnight we stood at the edge of the forest.

b6ab568b47a04bf5c3dbf049ca341bf919970bfe.summary: Death and the Teetälä are said once to have come as far as the Ortflüeh just before Stäg. And a little ring of Näfel is said to have come up out of the ground, and soon afterward the plague came.

b6aac243afd207fdbb4f7eca11d06d4bedb25ede.title: Death Announced by Falling Drops
b6aac243afd207fdbb4f7eca11d06d4bedb25ede.author: Josef Müller

5aa91be9363b527827084af1700a47a03b369369.author: M. Sooder
5aa91be9363b527827084af1700a47a03b369369.summary: Once there were a man and a woman. Whenever the man could put aside a few Batze, he placed them in the cupboard, laughed, and said, “That is something for an old man.” By this he meant that he would use the money when he was old.

04274ce1b1f3b4c168782a5a84c0c3160ed216b3.title: Of Some Peculiar Roots
04274ce1b1f3b4c168782a5a84c0c3160ed216b3.author: M. Sooder
04274ce1b1f3b4c168782a5a84c0c3160ed216b3.summary: Bärgliresli went to irrigate and opened a ditch.

e8b4c86ee3eb454e87b82b6e33b12679c302f226.title: Of Springete
e8b4c86ee3eb454e87b82b6e33b12679c302f226.author: M. Sooder
e8b4c86ee3eb454e87b82b6e33b12679c302f226.summary: Not far from where I was at home, there is a place in the forest called the Springplatz, because many years ago girls and boys held Springete there.

668192265321c9a321c5fe90cd49daab8d77e335.title: Of the Bammert
668192265321c9a321c5fe90cd49daab8d77e335.author: M. Sooder
668192265321c9a321c5fe90cd49daab8d77e335.summary: An old house stands on the Möösli; its roof reaches almost to the ground. People call it Solomon’s House.

583629cd04f8ba1763bcd7166543574b8afb47e5.title: Of the Bammertjöggel
583629cd04f8ba1763bcd7166543574b8afb47e5.author: M. Sooder
583629cd04f8ba1763bcd7166543574b8afb47e5.summary: The Bammertjöggel had all the little animals in his power.

f49959299d067fbc548cdd1283d21c198851177e.title: Of the Beak-People
f49959299d067fbc548cdd1283d21c198851177e.author: M. Sooder
f49959299d067fbc548cdd1283d21c198851177e.summary: When someone makes a deep hole, people ask: “Wosch zu de Schnabellüten abe?” The Schnabellüt live beneath the earth; if one digs far enough down, one can bring them forth.

c88a9e1ecc074074b4298f8ede7a694e1261d16f.title: Of the Black Dog
c88a9e1ecc074074b4298f8ede7a694e1261d16f.author: M. Sooder
c88a9e1ecc074074b4298f8ede7a694e1261d16f.summary: a) In Toggiburg, where the little road branches toward Ungerausel, a terrifyingly large dog with fiery eyes is sometimes seen at night.

bb90a4c1dbea5ec2f0b54428d941dd70d55f11dd.title: Of the Blacksmith and the Doggeli
bb90a4c1dbea5ec2f0b54428d941dd70d55f11dd.author: M. Sooder
bb90a4c1dbea5ec2f0b54428d941dd70d55f11dd.summary: A Doggeli continually tormented a blacksmith.

632174df34ed7c27e4343c2e9fba42928af8dad4.title: Of the Bread and the Three Good Counsels
632174df34ed7c27e4343c2e9fba42928af8dad4.author: Dietrich Jecklin
632174df34ed7c27e4343c2e9fba42928af8dad4.summary: In a large village lived a married couple so poor that the husband had to go abroad to earn his bread.

819850a8cbaa1d6f82918d8873cf783a7959adbc.title: Of the Bületod
819850a8cbaa1d6f82918d8873cf783a7959adbc.author: M. Sooder
819850a8cbaa1d6f82918d8873cf783a7959adbc.summary: Who knows how many years ago, there was a town in the Schmiedwald, and around Madiswil there was neither church nor cemetery.

f8c09e148ee6e19a3e90d78509b4d0f36a58fa07.title: Of the Castle Barn
f8c09e148ee6e19a3e90d78509b4d0f36a58fa07.author: M. Sooder
f8c09e148ee6e19a3e90d78509b4d0f36a58fa07.summary: At Dietel below the forest stands a house that people call the Barn.

6669f31bee2b569a228f9158adbb4adb6ac16ef9.title: Of the Conflagration at Schmidigen
6669f31bee2b569a228f9158adbb4adb6ac16ef9.author: M. Sooder
6669f31bee2b569a228f9158adbb4adb6ac16ef9.summary: You have surely heard people tell of the Brunscht at Schmidigen? No? Well then, people here and there still tell of it, but no version is exactly like another. I shall give it as I received it, adding nothing and taking nothing away.

bb13de5ebc9b2e69b536eaff1a23e2b1c2b4796a.title: Of the Earth Mirror
bb13de5ebc9b2e69b536eaff1a23e2b1c2b4796a.author: M. Sooder
bb13de5ebc9b2e69b536eaff1a23e2b1c2b4796a.summary: At night, a person must bury a mirror at a Chrüzwäg and stand upon it.

9996696b85e9dc18d33e7ebf7f6c466fe91d95ac.title: Of the Erdmännchen or Toggeli
9996696b85e9dc18d33e7ebf7f6c466fe91d95ac.author: C. Kohlrusch
9996696b85e9dc18d33e7ebf7f6c466fe91d95ac.summary: Thus the Toggeli once took charge of all a Senn's lean cows for the entire winter, upon his promise not to call any of them by name when they returned in spring.

b2786556454c455d11fab68091446f4d0ac07f03.title: Of the Fellenen Alp
b2786556454c455d11fab68091446f4d0ac07f03.author: Josef Müller
b2786556454c455d11fab68091446f4d0ac07f03.summary: The upper, southern part of this Alp is today a stone wilderness—Gand—one to three hours long, interrupted by several patches of eternal snow.

6205b4f0fbc10043f060e1e1b5e861b3dda2af28.title: Of the Fire-Breathing Serpent
6205b4f0fbc10043f060e1e1b5e861b3dda2af28.author: Dietrich Jecklin
6205b4f0fbc10043f060e1e1b5e861b3dda2af28.summary: A knight once rode out hunting.

309c226c416f15889ad0748c459614434bf93882.title: Of the Gauliweiblein, Engstlenfräulein, and Geissmaidlein
309c226c416f15889ad0748c459614434bf93882.author: C. Kohlrusch
309c226c416f15889ad0748c459614434bf93882.summary: A Swiss man from the Bernese Oberland was once traveling abroad, a considerable time ago, and one evening stopped at an isolated hut, where an old man received him hospitably.

6395223e817b2d82620066ca73e7521826f5d17f.title: Of the Hanischulmeischterbueb
6395223e817b2d82620066ca73e7521826f5d17f.author: M. Sooder
6395223e817b2d82620066ca73e7521826f5d17f.summary: The Hanischulmeischterbueb could do many things that other people would not have known how to set about.

609abc39b189e91f84226fed0822ab1f79d9cdc6.title: Of the Little Bird That Tells the Truth
609abc39b189e91f84226fed0822ab1f79d9cdc6.author: Dietrich Jecklin
609abc39b189e91f84226fed0822ab1f79d9cdc6.summary: One fine morning, a rich miller awoke because the great millwheel had stopped.

1730545db601dab7cfe7f68d4e0f075adbe560ff.title: Of the Little Black Spider
1730545db601dab7cfe7f68d4e0f075adbe560ff.author: M. Sooder
1730545db601dab7cfe7f68d4e0f075adbe560ff.summary: a) A hideous tyrant had a great castle built on Bärhegen.

d6c87364ff56e906cb10309017aff57f81b8c380.title: Of the Miller's Daughter
d6c87364ff56e906cb10309017aff57f81b8c380.author: M. Sooder
d6c87364ff56e906cb10309017aff57f81b8c380.summary: A poor boy was in the forest. Then he suddenly saw something beneath the trees. From fear, he climbed up a fir. There he hid as well as he could and prayed silently that the Lord God would protect him from all evil.

83907de13169c857e14753a5de2377f724e82484.title: Of the Old Fire Bell
83907de13169c857e14753a5de2377f724e82484.author: M. Sooder
83907de13169c857e14753a5de2377f724e82484.summary: Many things are said about the Füürglöggli; whether they are true, I do not know. At the very beginning, it is said to have been at Sant Urbe. Then it came to Gumiswil.

10c1fd626efbb3efdee0a89a0598c3672efd86f1.title: Of the Penitents, or Fiery Men, Who Are Seen at Night
10c1fd626efbb3efdee0a89a0598c3672efd86f1.author: Alois Lütolf
10c1fd626efbb3efdee0a89a0598c3672efd86f1.summary: Of this matter there would indeed be much to write and say.

bc46df5a11e6234fe756b213c0f18815e2b2301a.title: Of the Poor Boy
bc46df5a11e6234fe756b213c0f18815e2b2301a.author: M. Sooder
bc46df5a11e6234fe756b213c0f18815e2b2301a.summary: A man once came home from America. Then a poor boy went to him and said he had no work; the man should give him something to do.

c948853867d77f479c0219a55ec5a5f7a1c7362b.title: Of the Rütschele Tailor
c948853867d77f479c0219a55ec5a5f7a1c7362b.author: M. Sooder
c948853867d77f479c0219a55ec5a5f7a1c7362b.summary: The Rütscheleschnieder, a poor little Taunermanndli, spent the winter gwedelet—making bundles of brushwood—in a small forest.

a5e6d24a6827a8e7362ad49de60badc7a115551e.title: Of the Strong Martin Schelbert
a5e6d24a6827a8e7362ad49de60badc7a115551e.author: Josef Müller
a5e6d24a6827a8e7362ad49de60badc7a115551e.summary: He was actually a man of Schwyz, but for many summers he stayed ennet der Märcht on the Urnerboden.

90342d0b7fb6d23d42d6158fafd0e4d40187f598.title: Of the Stumper and Markenrücker
90342d0b7fb6d23d42d6158fafd0e4d40187f598.author: Jakob Kuoni
90342d0b7fb6d23d42d6158fafd0e4d40187f598.summary: Because landholdings in the Werdenberg region are greatly subdivided, in autumn cattle usually cannot be grazed freely but only gestumpet.

afb91b91447bd277c589c5fdf821fc1e9bb135d3.title: Of the Three Men in the Little Cliff
afb91b91447bd277c589c5fdf821fc1e9bb135d3.author: M. Sooder
afb91b91447bd277c589c5fdf821fc1e9bb135d3.summary: My father once went bathing in the stream with other boys. It was a Sunday, near the Altburg, where the Flüehli comes right down to the stream. Then something gruchset—grunted or groaned. He looked around but saw no one.

c4f2de9632a419a77f25c0818b754010b5b5174c.title: Of the Treasure in the Judsfad in the Meiental
c4f2de9632a419a77f25c0818b754010b5b5174c.author: Josef Müller
c4f2de9632a419a77f25c0818b754010b5b5174c.summary: Of the treasure in the Judsfad in the Meiental, it is said that in ancient times a Jewish man mined ore there, smelted it, and refined it.

32777594f244b1de7d7964a2c921cded53440de8.title: Of the Türsten-Gjäg
32777594f244b1de7d7964a2c921cded53440de8.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
32777594f244b1de7d7964a2c921cded53440de8.summary: The following is told in the Simmental about the Türsten-Gjäg.

84744d1f9fa06ddfb15aced9cab04a6dffb6dfc6.title: Of the Wasedokter
84744d1f9fa06ddfb15aced9cab04a6dffb6dfc6.author: M. Sooder
84744d1f9fa06ddfb15aced9cab04a6dffb6dfc6.summary: a) Our father said that he once had a little cow, a very good one; it gave a whole bucketful of milk.

9d3264e8b5e09d2d601cf7ea0b73bf154016d4e7.title: Of the Wild People
9d3264e8b5e09d2d601cf7ea0b73bf154016d4e7.author: Jakob Kuoni
9d3264e8b5e09d2d601cf7ea0b73bf154016d4e7.summary: In the Untertal, the pre-glacial valley of the Schilz, beneath the great Gufel, wild people once lived.

c632d204e406329b275f6d51aeee29ec48ee8d6d.title: Of Treasures
c632d204e406329b275f6d51aeee29ec48ee8d6d.author: Josef Müller
c632d204e406329b275f6d51aeee29ec48ee8d6d.summary: 1. A great treasure is hidden on the Flüeli (Zwing-Uri) near Amsteg; if it were found, the whole canton of Uri would be rich enough.

b8e16e83a00340d1b14804b5fe338bb0d2c93126.title: Of Tyrannical Lords
b8e16e83a00340d1b14804b5fe338bb0d2c93126.author: Josef Müller
b8e16e83a00340d1b14804b5fe338bb0d2c93126.summary: a) On the tower in the Dörfli at Silenen, according to the tradition attested by several people, there formerly stood a wooden house, which is certainly correct.

92dc6f46483373f27385e0ebecba20956499d322.title: Ofengüpf — The Oven Crest
92dc6f46483373f27385e0ebecba20956499d322.author: Theodor Vernaleken
92dc6f46483373f27385e0ebecba20956499d322.summary: The hill on which the castle of the lords of Sellenbüren once stood is called the Ofengüpf by the farmers in the village of Sellenbüren near Zürich. Treasures are said to be guarded inside this hill by a black dog.

32e3777d57ed423b0d44c16a4d0a7c43430cdd44.title: Oh, If She Came!
32e3777d57ed423b0d44c16a4d0a7c43430cdd44.author: M. Sooder
32e3777d57ed423b0d44c16a4d0a7c43430cdd44.summary: Many years ago, the boys from Möhreweid went sledding down the Esel.

4cc8433c6496573e876eb7af4abf74f431a5a2d7.title: Oh, You Poor Little Fox, Where Are You?
4cc8433c6496573e876eb7af4abf74f431a5a2d7.author: Josef Müller
4cc8433c6496573e876eb7af4abf74f431a5a2d7.summary: a) In the woods near Geezig above Seedorf, a hunter had shot a fox and put it in his rucksack.

3c9abbade989df7fe862daef7ac717059bfef526.title: Old Customs (Funeral Customs)
3c9abbade989df7fe862daef7ac717059bfef526.author: M. Sooder
3c9abbade989df7fe862daef7ac717059bfef526.summary: When a sick person is rapidly declining, a pot full of water is prepared in the kitchen so that the soul can still wash before it departs.

51396dd495765348c51f5002ec36686ce8ebd4cd.title: Old Customs (Livestock Customs)
51396dd495765348c51f5002ec36686ce8ebd4cd.author: M. Sooder
51396dd495765348c51f5002ec36686ce8ebd4cd.summary: A calf born on a Wednesday will not prosper. But one can prevent this: cut a little from its ear, throw it away, and say, “There, take your due!”

fa8a04c74fe4e0d0ee1c1f639ac976a4cca31578.title: Old Maids
fa8a04c74fe4e0d0ee1c1f639ac976a4cca31578.author: Jakob Kuoni
fa8a04c74fe4e0d0ee1c1f639ac976a4cca31578.summary: According to an old legend of the people of Sargans, girls who through their own fault become old maids must assemble after death at the great marsh near Schaan in Liechtenstein.

116ea4e51b187642b7ed47249c3a7d8c21a569ab.title: Old Maids Condemned in the Rottal Glacier
116ea4e51b187642b7ed47249c3a7d8c21a569ab.author: C. Kohlrusch
116ea4e51b187642b7ed47249c3a7d8c21a569ab.summary: Few girls in the Bernese Oberland die as old maids.

6e6f2729b78f28855a34c3f654d5867996a24ef9.title: Omen
6e6f2729b78f28855a34c3f654d5867996a24ef9.author: M. Sooder
6e6f2729b78f28855a34c3f654d5867996a24ef9.summary: On the day before Huttwil burned, the Chilezit kept stuttering. The people mocked that a Heidesiegerischt must be behind it. The following night lightning struck.

473a04f72727e5057fdbeab323e06918512f31a4.title: On an Ember Day
473a04f72727e5057fdbeab323e06918512f31a4.author: Josef Müller
473a04f72727e5057fdbeab323e06918512f31a4.summary: That is, on a Wednesday, Friday, or Saturday in one of the Fronfasten weeks, people always said that one should not go out with a gun.

6a56c64aa966828fa1899655ddd1ecb0adfff1f4.title: On Brodässe
6a56c64aa966828fa1899655ddd1ecb0adfff1f4.author: Otto Sutermeister
6a56c64aa966828fa1899655ddd1ecb0adfff1f4.summary: Hansli had a Fraueli named Bethli, and Bethli had a husband named Hansli.

c38fc853d9ea72ee31b342476e4453e2b801de04.title: On Castle Hill
c38fc853d9ea72ee31b342476e4453e2b801de04.author: Theodor Vernaleken
c38fc853d9ea72ee31b342476e4453e2b801de04.summary: On Castle Hill near Rohrbach, before every thunderstorm one hears howling, cracking whips, and a rattling wagon at the very spot where the former lord of the castle wished to build an enormous bridge.

62632ca42e420e1fd5cdc23d10c35fce4fce4bfe.title: On Saint Georgenberg
62632ca42e420e1fd5cdc23d10c35fce4fce4bfe.author: Jakob Kuoni
62632ca42e420e1fd5cdc23d10c35fce4fce4bfe.summary: Fahrende Schüler looked through the Bergspiegel into the rock wall and discovered immeasurable treasures of gold and silver there, as they did at the higher Steienwand and in the Goldloch of nearby Alp Sennis.

35a5036556840927eb524df0cbbe62ef30f574a0.title: On St. Andrew’s Night
35a5036556840927eb524df0cbbe62ef30f574a0.author: M. Sooder
35a5036556840927eb524df0cbbe62ef30f574a0.summary: My mistress was a miller’s daughter from the region of Bern.

d3c6c8147f1ef890f0518c1829c80b0a9f2a85e3.title: On the Alp Culma
d3c6c8147f1ef890f0518c1829c80b0a9f2a85e3.author: Josef Müller
d3c6c8147f1ef890f0518c1829c80b0a9f2a85e3.summary: On the Alp Culma in the Etzlital, something used to drive the livestock out with stones on the final evening before the Alpabfahrt.

5ce0ebe016572328f5f81d4e03cdb3bacf2a7eba.title: On the Arni
5ce0ebe016572328f5f81d4e03cdb3bacf2a7eba.author: M. Sooder
5ce0ebe016572328f5f81d4e03cdb3bacf2a7eba.summary: It was always haunted in an Arnihütte, but only when the War was no longer on the pasture and the hut too stood empty. Once in autumn a hunter passed by. He heard someone turning the cheese and handling the milk vessels.

fab053652195ce60786c88b660c8927310c78554.title: On the Casting of a Bell
fab053652195ce60786c88b660c8927310c78554.author: Josef Müller
fab053652195ce60786c88b660c8927310c78554.summary: The first bells at Silenen—the great bell at Spiringen—were cast in the Streissrütti, on the Achern.

ef9b754d13172234de1a69f4d62ada5c8f558f08.title: On the Chaltenegg
ef9b754d13172234de1a69f4d62ada5c8f558f08.author: M. Sooder
ef9b754d13172234de1a69f4d62ada5c8f558f08.summary: My sister was on her way home at nightfall. She had come from Chabisberg and wanted to go toward Flückigen. Everything was still.

4f986da36aef139595f602d745f75364d48bfea9.title: On the Clothing and Food of the Erdmännchen
4f986da36aef139595f602d745f75364d48bfea9.author: Alois Lütolf
4f986da36aef139595f602d745f75364d48bfea9.summary: a) In Gibelflüh, people hung little red coats and cloaks on the door as gifts for the Erdmännchen. They took them away but did not put them on.

412f14f7d3032fdabc26ea60a52c797468394638.title: On the Feast of the Ten Thousand Knights
412f14f7d3032fdabc26ea60a52c797468394638.author: M. Sooder
412f14f7d3032fdabc26ea60a52c797468394638.summary: On zähetusig Rittertag, Grandmother said, a long procession always goes from the Altburg up toward Hänseli. One hears chains rattling, but sees nothing more.

d7e85527eae59ec7ffcbfd70d141719ddea93162.title: On the Fursch Alp
d7e85527eae59ec7ffcbfd70d141719ddea93162.author: Jakob Kuoni
d7e85527eae59ec7ffcbfd70d141719ddea93162.summary: Before the railway was built, livestock leased out for Sömmerung in the Glarus Alps was driven from Flums over the passes at Schönbühl and Wissmil.

5a22a73f8a352010a5e249fd8d8ab9276a294034.title: On the Hingerarni
5a22a73f8a352010a5e249fd8d8ab9276a294034.author: M. Sooder
5a22a73f8a352010a5e249fd8d8ab9276a294034.summary: A herdsman named Röthlisbärger lived on the Hingerarni. He came from Trachsel and in his youth had been a Verdingbueb. He had scarcely enough to live on and was always close to the fence line. One night he had a dream. A voice called:

51688bd5c90084868d369d7847f0bbb0f90d5285.title: On the Holy Night
51688bd5c90084868d369d7847f0bbb0f90d5285.author: M. Sooder
51688bd5c90084868d369d7847f0bbb0f90d5285.summary: On the Holy Night, animals can speak.

3bda2ce37f6b2f7d57c1d091dc6455383e11c0ec.title: On the Oberplegi Alp at the Glärnisch
3bda2ce37f6b2f7d57c1d091dc6455383e11c0ec.author: Theodor Vernaleken
3bda2ce37f6b2f7d57c1d091dc6455383e11c0ec.summary: On the Oberplegi Alp at the Glärnisch, which is now covered by glacier ice, there once lived an alpine dairyman who had sinned with a maiden named Kathrin.

5f9459cc481f2839588fe1961a068f19d10eff91.title: On the Schatzbödeli
5f9459cc481f2839588fe1961a068f19d10eff91.author: Josef Müller
5f9459cc481f2839588fe1961a068f19d10eff91.summary: A treasure is buried on the Schatzbödeli, or Burgli, in the Ysleren at Attinghausen.

b526435f571d2aa7dc4277f4b3f7870164b89fc7.title: On the Steihufe and Around It
b526435f571d2aa7dc4277f4b3f7870164b89fc7.author: M. Sooder
b526435f571d2aa7dc4277f4b3f7870164b89fc7.summary: When one goes from the Bisig up along the Längwäg toward the Steihufe, one passes two Wolfsgruebe.

83277e1049f9e96214564346261f7246a36e4356.title: On the Surenen Alps
83277e1049f9e96214564346261f7246a36e4356.author: Theodor Vernaleken
83277e1049f9e96214564346261f7246a36e4356.summary: On the Surenen Alps between Engelberg and Uri, there is a curious tradition that attributes the mountain pasture's reversion to wilderness to a different sacrilege.

9fa15ab0ab317e7faf12094e26a1c0a2d1a81bfd.title: On the Wanneli Alp
9fa15ab0ab317e7faf12094e26a1c0a2d1a81bfd.author: Josef Müller
9fa15ab0ab317e7faf12094e26a1c0a2d1a81bfd.summary: In the municipality of Erstfeld, a subterranean lake is hidden beneath the Wanneli Alp, and if it ever breaks out, all of Ripshausen will perish. This was revealed by a fahrender Schüler.
