69d7c5cb99718bba2db27caa09977a27637112bf.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
69d7c5cb99718bba2db27caa09977a27637112bf.summary: The holy bishop Nicholas gave his name to the village and region where he is now venerated in a beautiful house of God; before that, the place may have been called “Gasen” (Chauson).

91f8de0de7a8d9591699275e20c88b0220af44b3.title: The Church of Blumenstein and the Wandering Jew
91f8de0de7a8d9591699275e20c88b0220af44b3.author: Theodor Vernaleken
91f8de0de7a8d9591699275e20c88b0220af44b3.summary: The little church of Blumenstein stands apart from the village.

396f8d608e4c08f622d7aa23627047719a75eb7f.title: The Church of Isérables
396f8d608e4c08f622d7aa23627047719a75eb7f.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
396f8d608e4c08f622d7aa23627047719a75eb7f.summary: The inhabitants of the municipality of Isérables are said to have been rather simple-minded people in earlier times, and amusing Schildbürgerstücklein are told about them.

1e0a2085cd38fd01e838f67b8f84f9c47897580a.title: The Church Tower, Bells, and Church in Naters
1e0a2085cd38fd01e838f67b8f84f9c47897580a.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
1e0a2085cd38fd01e838f67b8f84f9c47897580a.summary: It is related that the church tower of Naters is very old, that it was built by the pagans and only centuries later fitted out for Catholic worship.

7f5c36a99266bc09873452d1b6662716359c3a2b.title: The Churchyard at Sellenbüren
7f5c36a99266bc09873452d1b6662716359c3a2b.author: Meinrad Lienert
7f5c36a99266bc09873452d1b6662716359c3a2b.summary: One day, a little boy strolled singing toward the cozy village of Sellenbüren. He meant to go into the nearby forest and search for strawberries in the undergrowth.

28585910ceed2d875c0d003e1591f49a7aaec4ac.title: The Chüeiher in the Chaltenegg
28585910ceed2d875c0d003e1591f49a7aaec4ac.author: M. Sooder
28585910ceed2d875c0d003e1591f49a7aaec4ac.summary: At Unzit, a Chüeiher drives through the Chaltenegg. No one sees anything. But people hear bells and Treichle and the Chüeiher calling, ‘Hoop, hoop.’

7a660f7b0dcd5806df38d9cb754d46de4c438f62.title: The City of Wolfsnest
7a660f7b0dcd5806df38d9cb754d46de4c438f62.author: Dietrich Jecklin
7a660f7b0dcd5806df38d9cb754d46de4c438f62.summary: According to the legend, on the site of the present Steigwaid above Mayenfeld there once stood the great city of Wolfsnest.

2d4f17f4145af7dadc0910c6a53cc0d60a87021a.title: The Clariden
2d4f17f4145af7dadc0910c6a53cc0d60a87021a.author: Theodor Vernaleken
2d4f17f4145af7dadc0910c6a53cc0d60a87021a.summary: The Clariden in the land of Glarus and several Blüemlisalp pastures in the Bernese Oberland are principal homes of this legend.

66adaeabec912f0182fb0db19127d3fe4cae5ad0.title: The Clean Shirt
66adaeabec912f0182fb0db19127d3fe4cae5ad0.author: Josef Müller
66adaeabec912f0182fb0db19127d3fe4cae5ad0.summary: In the municipality of Gurtnellen lived a man who knew and could do more than other people.

116032c240ae3347dd0152fe3f1b21e000fb4c22.title: The Clerk
116032c240ae3347dd0152fe3f1b21e000fb4c22.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
116032c240ae3347dd0152fe3f1b21e000fb4c22.summary: The people of Lötschental also wanted a clerk.

4c5ae4c6cf1976d7e87f151495f01dc597bcb2ad.title: The Clever Beggar
4c5ae4c6cf1976d7e87f151495f01dc597bcb2ad.author: Dietrich Jecklin
4c5ae4c6cf1976d7e87f151495f01dc597bcb2ad.summary: There was once a beggar in Scarl who lost his way in the forest and came to a cave.

8132671a4baab04fc5585d63e903f24ea6a62af5.title: The Clever Beggar and the Man-Eater
8132671a4baab04fc5585d63e903f24ea6a62af5.author: Otto Sutermeister
8132671a4baab04fc5585d63e903f24ea6a62af5.summary: Once there was a beggar who lost his way in the forest and came to a cave.

19c39d3db3d9aca3b42d4006a08938f3f25ff645.title: The Clever King’s Son
19c39d3db3d9aca3b42d4006a08938f3f25ff645.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
19c39d3db3d9aca3b42d4006a08938f3f25ff645.summary: A young king’s son sought a wife at the neighboring courts.

ce787cefb8da8363056cf868ecaa33b9354de359.title: The Clever Villagers
ce787cefb8da8363056cf868ecaa33b9354de359.author: Meinrad Lienert
ce787cefb8da8363056cf868ecaa33b9354de359.summary: The people of Filisur in Graubünden could not understand why the Lord God had placed such a high mountain directly in front of their sun.

56288a00b34b6457755c3dba60fba41b86109fff.title: The Clever Waldfängge
56288a00b34b6457755c3dba60fba41b86109fff.author: Dietrich Jecklin
56288a00b34b6457755c3dba60fba41b86109fff.summary: Another Waldfängge near Conters once herded all the village goats for an entire summer.

97a35d92276a2b8f0a9e7df49d86786a4b99fa19.title: The Cloth Full of Wheat
97a35d92276a2b8f0a9e7df49d86786a4b99fa19.author: Jakob Kuoni
97a35d92276a2b8f0a9e7df49d86786a4b99fa19.summary: South of Wartau Castle, a path runs beneath the wall and around the castle hill.

ea0d136a19c245c04a76ce1e79d8ca27b32bb33c.title: The Coals
ea0d136a19c245c04a76ce1e79d8ca27b32bb33c.author: J. J. Jakob
ea0d136a19c245c04a76ce1e79d8ca27b32bb33c.summary: It appears that the Erdmännchen were not skilled in every art and science but needed human help in certain matters.

aa112cf329e5455f23e041d2517b85325374c62a.title: The Coals Turned into Gold
aa112cf329e5455f23e041d2517b85325374c62a.author: Dietrich Jecklin
aa112cf329e5455f23e041d2517b85325374c62a.summary: A Fänggenmannli who lived at the far end of Savien on the Valätscher-Alpe in a ‘Balma’ once came by night to the Bühel farm.

1c3c0333ff8bfa6c23ea75757f3a0d2a26b79f7b.title: The Coat of Arms of the Anderhalten Family in Sachseln
1c3c0333ff8bfa6c23ea75757f3a0d2a26b79f7b.author: Alois Lütolf
1c3c0333ff8bfa6c23ea75757f3a0d2a26b79f7b.summary: My legend goes back a mere 1466 years and arrives at the year 398, when Pope Anastasius and Emperor Honorius requested and received help from the 3 Lands.

6eaa1733faee5398d66f21d2ff7369a719c1d5e5.title: The Cock's Egg
6eaa1733faee5398d66f21d2ff7369a719c1d5e5.author: Dietrich Jecklin
6eaa1733faee5398d66f21d2ff7369a719c1d5e5.summary: Around the year 1730, Jann Fausch, who lived on the Stutz near Seewis in the Prätigau, had a large, coal-black cock.

986ade41a4f1248cf71b21250c488c40837ce1c6.title: The Cold Hand (Uri)
986ade41a4f1248cf71b21250c488c40837ce1c6.author: Josef Müller
986ade41a4f1248cf71b21250c488c40837ce1c6.summary: A herder in Ursern feels an unseen hand and is asked to arrange a Mass for a troubled soul.

ce8c1fafabe1c22277c7f754448338b73d1bf39d.title: The Cold Hand (Valais)
ce8c1fafabe1c22277c7f754448338b73d1bf39d.author: J. Siegen
ce8c1fafabe1c22277c7f754448338b73d1bf39d.summary: A remote holding in the Lötschental becomes the setting for a cold hand, a winter ordeal, and prayers for the dead.

bdbf8a5612d73ef065d895a1d194296f61c3ce60.title: The Colors and Garb of Spirits
bdbf8a5612d73ef065d895a1d194296f61c3ce60.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
bdbf8a5612d73ef065d895a1d194296f61c3ce60.summary: In Upper Aargau, he is called Rotthaler and Rothenburger.

58b25a1771f00b4616fd0938fa04270bc4a54aa9.title: The Conjured Teacher on the Reppisch
58b25a1771f00b4616fd0938fa04270bc4a54aa9.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
58b25a1771f00b4616fd0938fa04270bc4a54aa9.summary: There once lived on the Reppisch, a border stream between Aargau and Zürich territory, a teacher whose home and name shall remain unmentioned here because legal proceedings concerning him and his present fate took place only recently.

79fe2017e7c3b1e3ad04cd2bd6ac73ff4a781b21.title: The Conversion
79fe2017e7c3b1e3ad04cd2bd6ac73ff4a781b21.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
79fe2017e7c3b1e3ad04cd2bd6ac73ff4a781b21.summary: In the Val d'Illiez lived a poor family that called nothing its own but a black, dilapidated hut through which the wind whistled and a patch of meadow in front of it where a small mountain cow and two goats found their scanty fodder.

5e4ed485f9c6505488935a32654ad225d62477d1.title: The Cooper of Lucerne in the Dragon Cave
5e4ed485f9c6505488935a32654ad225d62477d1.author: C. Kohlrusch
5e4ed485f9c6505488935a32654ad225d62477d1.summary: In the city of Lucerne there once lived a cooper who often wandered through the dense forests and clefts of Mount Pilatus in search of wood for making wine barrels.

a1e4ff9cfcd45178de6a30bf54883dad18ab0f3b.title: The Costly Hotzdecke
a1e4ff9cfcd45178de6a30bf54883dad18ab0f3b.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
a1e4ff9cfcd45178de6a30bf54883dad18ab0f3b.summary: There are people in the world who cannot live among their fellow human beings without dispute and quarrel and must forever argue with one person or another.

9c1784b3ee1de2a0dee4d9836c9784fcb02a03af.title: The Councillors at Santaburg
9c1784b3ee1de2a0dee4d9836c9784fcb02a03af.author: Alois Lütolf
9c1784b3ee1de2a0dee4d9836c9784fcb02a03af.summary: a) Santaburg once stood upon a bright hill between Nebikon and Dagmersellen, where nothing but desolate woodland is now found.

a9d2171885cad8b6f6d31be8d76975fde2fdb5a3.title: The Councilors
a9d2171885cad8b6f6d31be8d76975fde2fdb5a3.author: Josef Müller
a9d2171885cad8b6f6d31be8d76975fde2fdb5a3.summary: Folk tradition says that council meetings were held from time to time in Kaspar Gisler’s house in Schattdorf.

f6c23dbe08742e8fe5c7c048c2f3d789c274ece8.title: The Countess at Schwarzsee
f6c23dbe08742e8fe5c7c048c2f3d789c274ece8.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
f6c23dbe08742e8fe5c7c048c2f3d789c274ece8.summary: In ancient times a road led from Milan to Brig, then across the Beichtgrat into the Lötschental, and from there across the Lötschen Pass—where paving stones can still be seen—to Kandersteg.

81217633f72e91e773857d4e26330aacfb66dd25.title: The Countess at Z'en-Tischen
81217633f72e91e773857d4e26330aacfb66dd25.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
81217633f72e91e773857d4e26330aacfb66dd25.summary: High in the Naters Alp called Lusgen, on the boundary of the Aletsch Valley, one finds a deeply fissured rock that is partly split into large Blatten, or broad stone slabs.

cecf63fe3faba166561f87c52f48d0fb940c8c0a.title: The Countess on the Lusgen
cecf63fe3faba166561f87c52f48d0fb940c8c0a.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
cecf63fe3faba166561f87c52f48d0fb940c8c0a.summary: The Alp called Lusgen lies on the Gletscherbord of the upper Aletschgletscher.

882e3db984a0c7bb7a9fabbbe626d900bbc94d9c.title: The Courageous Women of Lenk
882e3db984a0c7bb7a9fabbbe626d900bbc94d9c.author: Hermann Hartmann
882e3db984a0c7bb7a9fabbbe626d900bbc94d9c.summary: Many years ago, during wartime, men from Valais raided the Alpen belonging to the people of Lenk in the upper Simmental and drove away a large number of stolen cattle.

f792fff8daa2246adc72f5ac3d00eafcec05f4f7.title: The Cows’ Mysterious Departure
f792fff8daa2246adc72f5ac3d00eafcec05f4f7.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
f792fff8daa2246adc72f5ac3d00eafcec05f4f7.summary: Storms and sudden snowfall on Alpine pastures, the proximity of wild animals, or swarms of stinging insects sometimes make a herd of cows on an alp so confused and wild that it takes flight and, no longer heeding the herder’s calls…

f24d3eb39fabaecd81133330413fafbaa69d1897.title: The Cows’ Mysterious Departure (Hartmann)
f24d3eb39fabaecd81133330413fafbaa69d1897.author: Hermann Hartmann
f24d3eb39fabaecd81133330413fafbaa69d1897.summary: On the Wergistalalp and Bussalp in the Grindelwald valley, it happens that the cows rücken.

d9c1596b711ac776b3c699413ca08184edb2508e.title: The Cradle Child Carried Off
d9c1596b711ac776b3c699413ca08184edb2508e.author: Josef Müller
d9c1596b711ac776b3c699413ca08184edb2508e.summary: One day, when the mother at Klosterberg in Isental returned to the house from her fieldwork and meant to tend to the child in the cradle, the child had vanished.

fa23bdca840efeeec31d44000164bcf1ac552c5d.title: The Cradle Spirit
fa23bdca840efeeec31d44000164bcf1ac552c5d.author: Meinrad Lienert
fa23bdca840efeeec31d44000164bcf1ac552c5d.summary: A haunted cradle at Yberg draws a mother into a mountain encounter and leaves a gift of fragrant flowers.

d9cb736886046f91b66e89ce4ee79dc813380ca3.title: The Cream Witch
d9cb736886046f91b66e89ce4ee79dc813380ca3.author: Josef Müller
d9cb736886046f91b66e89ce4ee79dc813380ca3.summary: a) In a Heimkuhalpeli, entirely apart from the other people, lived a Wybervölchli who seldom went out, never fetched provisions, and yet lived well.

9c81e4afa3f0e3cfa5fdf5e95b9b0acbb7a6de01.title: The Cross on le petit vanni
9c81e4afa3f0e3cfa5fdf5e95b9b0acbb7a6de01.author: C. Kohlrusch
9c81e4afa3f0e3cfa5fdf5e95b9b0acbb7a6de01.summary: On the summit of the Eccojalaz rises a steep rocky pinnacle called the little rock, le petit vanni.

3dd235b004624995549d76bc64128775bcf44a1e.title: The Crow on the Britschelade
3dd235b004624995549d76bc64128775bcf44a1e.author: M. Sooder
3dd235b004624995549d76bc64128775bcf44a1e.summary: When the weather is about to turn and bring rain, a crow sometimes flies onto a Britschelade and caws as loudly as its throat allows.

4eaab2f144f48b52424de2f91c26b0a122505c19.title: The Crowned Snake
4eaab2f144f48b52424de2f91c26b0a122505c19.author: Alois Lütolf
4eaab2f144f48b52424de2f91c26b0a122505c19.summary: Every afternoon, a girl went behind her parents’ house with her little bowl of warm milk containing bread and would eat nowhere else.

13b28d7e06ad5bef7dcfb4b921f3d4ec00af7826.title: The Crowned Snake of Niederlenz
13b28d7e06ad5bef7dcfb4b921f3d4ec00af7826.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
13b28d7e06ad5bef7dcfb4b921f3d4ec00af7826.summary: Southwest of the village of Niederlenz, in the level grain fields, lies a charming hill richly overgrown with tall grass and planted with many cherry and apple trees.

41699098cbec4f27de62c52a4cc003c15246dcb3.title: The Cry of Agnes
41699098cbec4f27de62c52a4cc003c15246dcb3.author: C. Kohlrusch
41699098cbec4f27de62c52a4cc003c15246dcb3.summary: Toward Sarmenstorf, in a forest, lie the last remains of Fahrwangen Castle.

1456415dd8b5a2591102f1f47fe4c3304b52442d.title: The Cry on the Alpine Pasture
1456415dd8b5a2591102f1f47fe4c3304b52442d.author: Alois Lütolf
1456415dd8b5a2591102f1f47fe4c3304b52442d.summary: A hunter follows a cry across an alpine pasture in Uri as the sound repeatedly changes direction.

0920489a0594f44f99174686b1539b6488869bce.title: The Crystal Cave
0920489a0594f44f99174686b1539b6488869bce.author: Jakob Kuoni
0920489a0594f44f99174686b1539b6488869bce.summary: The crystal cave at Kobelwies must have a hidden exit. A fox ran in through the front and later emerged again at Freienbach. Oral

5066a19740d392a6bdf641ef3058d6b6707aa781.title: The Crystal Cave in the Hinterbirg
5066a19740d392a6bdf641ef3058d6b6707aa781.author: Hermann Hartmann
5066a19740d392a6bdf641ef3058d6b6707aa781.summary: Long ago, one evening, a herder on Alp Tschingelfeld at the Faulhorn was gathering his strayed goats far from the hut.

3849f135097fc3d774dbcdb60788b0879ddacc5e.title: The Crystal Diggers
3849f135097fc3d774dbcdb60788b0879ddacc5e.author: C. Kohlrusch
3849f135097fc3d774dbcdb60788b0879ddacc5e.summary: The most skillful crystal diggers were the Capuchin fathers.

f5161d7d9eadcb885482435ad0e62267ed64128c.title: The Cunning Fox
f5161d7d9eadcb885482435ad0e62267ed64128c.author: Josef Müller
f5161d7d9eadcb885482435ad0e62267ed64128c.summary: Yes, foxes are cunning; they watch a person to see whether he is lotze—lying in wait for them.

8edb7f91b541887896e0761fc5d0effa9bc03fea.title: The Cunning Habsburger (Aargau)
8edb7f91b541887896e0761fc5d0effa9bc03fea.author: Meinrad Lienert, Schweiz
8edb7f91b541887896e0761fc5d0effa9bc03fea.summary: Lienert tells how Rudolf of Habsburg combines military cunning with an unexpected act of humility.

9c3ebc4f3e1a1b14034c65a04a72aa64dd1928e6.title: The Cunning Habsburger (Zürich)
9c3ebc4f3e1a1b14034c65a04a72aa64dd1928e6.author: Meinrad Lienert
9c3ebc4f3e1a1b14034c65a04a72aa64dd1928e6.summary: Lienert’s Zürich version pits Rudolf of Habsburg against the power of the Regensberg family.

44859e1cd81cbc92be3e09a203fb4e2281e490a3.title: The Cunning Smith
44859e1cd81cbc92be3e09a203fb4e2281e490a3.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
44859e1cd81cbc92be3e09a203fb4e2281e490a3.summary: In ancient times there lived a capable smith who enjoyed a large clientele.

5c49e214fc1041eb9bd2406c0854fc7ed8a2d26d.title: The Cunning Wildleutchen
5c49e214fc1041eb9bd2406c0854fc7ed8a2d26d.author: Meinrad Lienert
5c49e214fc1041eb9bd2406c0854fc7ed8a2d26d.summary: In the village of Tenna in Graubünden, where the remarkable Bluter live, there once lived the Geschworene Valentin Suter.

9887fae519f2e9cb6196bf1671dd36e7668b439c.title: The Curious Fox
9887fae519f2e9cb6196bf1671dd36e7668b439c.author: Josef Müller
9887fae519f2e9cb6196bf1671dd36e7668b439c.summary: Two men lay in wait inside a small, two-man Tatschihüsli on the Göscheneralp.

784bce32826fdb9aac12fc586aa7497eb022c5ba.title: The Curse in the Butter
784bce32826fdb9aac12fc586aa7497eb022c5ba.author: Dietrich Jecklin
784bce32826fdb9aac12fc586aa7497eb022c5ba.summary: On an Alp in Schanvigg, a little beggar man wrapped in ragged clothes once approached a woman who was just boiling butter.

85896fac6098b56b996406382fe4b0cc71b027d8.title: The Cursed Allmend
85896fac6098b56b996406382fe4b0cc71b027d8.author: Alois Lütolf
85896fac6098b56b996406382fe4b0cc71b027d8.summary: Once, a wrongdoer was whipped in Zug and driven out of the country with his back raw.

f382c32214cb0c0fa2da686606de04f840365f20.title: The Cursed Herb
f382c32214cb0c0fa2da686606de04f840365f20.author: Alois Lütolf
f382c32214cb0c0fa2da686606de04f840365f20.summary: It grows on the Blümlisalp in Uri and is cursed by God because of the sins of the Sennen. Formerly it was an especially blessed plant that caused the cows to give much milk.

e0101f0dddb0c24d2b4fb83e4d9f0c22d29e9ef2.title: The Dance Ground on Alp Tardona
e0101f0dddb0c24d2b4fb83e4d9f0c22d29e9ef2.author: Jakob Kuoni
e0101f0dddb0c24d2b4fb83e4d9f0c22d29e9ef2.summary: At the far end of the Calfeisen Valley lies Alp Zarduna, which provides summer pasture for more than 290 head of cattle. On this Alp is a large level place called the Dance Ground.

0063fea33e222968033f3b2f048e047a8ec1ce00.title: The Dance of Death
0063fea33e222968033f3b2f048e047a8ec1ce00.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
0063fea33e222968033f3b2f048e047a8ec1ce00.summary: I owe the following legend to an earlier and a later account, which did not entirely agree; I have tried to reconcile them as well as possible.

8f2e4c04f3780fe61f71587a035ddb8b7695f09e.title: The Dance on Palfries
8f2e4c04f3780fe61f71587a035ddb8b7695f09e.author: Jakob Kuoni
8f2e4c04f3780fe61f71587a035ddb8b7695f09e.summary: The farmhands on the Bäschneralp had decided to have a merry day and for this purpose summoned two fiddlers and several young women from the village of Bärschis to the Alp.

6c0c398acee49be78206b3c2ba58d41cf7b36c63.title: The Dancer
6c0c398acee49be78206b3c2ba58d41cf7b36c63.author: Jakob Kuoni
6c0c398acee49be78206b3c2ba58d41cf7b36c63.summary: At Portels on the Flumser Kleinberg, in the Harzloch, stands a house that, like many very old houses, has a large chamber or hall.

60259d69ea8230ccad2ebadf8efca909f62110ac.title: The Dancing Couple
60259d69ea8230ccad2ebadf8efca909f62110ac.author: Hermann Hartmann
60259d69ea8230ccad2ebadf8efca909f62110ac.summary: Near the Giessbach lies an open promontory toward Lake Brienz, covered with splendid grass and called the Tanzplatz in local speech.

fad4b1199eafb60f7291b135de7cd843e2abb3af.title: The Dancing Places

ad98b4877c7014e66151645f04f11fe58aad7a96.author: Josef Müller
ad98b4877c7014e66151645f04f11fe58aad7a96.summary: About 60 years ago, the Bernese brought a tremendous giant on a chain up through the land of Glarus as far as Linthal and challenged the people of Glarus to a Schwinget.

d07f64211701ed812c610cff872519f75f1a88a0.title: The Giant Eishexe
d07f64211701ed812c610cff872519f75f1a88a0.author: Jakob Kuoni
d07f64211701ed812c610cff872519f75f1a88a0.summary: In the Thur valley lived a giant named Eishexe, meaning ‘terrible.’ He needed no bridge across the Thur, no matter how greatly it swelled or how fiercely even his enormous horse resisted the current.

7f1a11ef54f600e5e0efc880aa3ca85d11252f50.title: The Giant Gargantua
7f1a11ef54f600e5e0efc880aa3ca85d11252f50.author: C. Kohlrusch
7f1a11ef54f600e5e0efc880aa3ca85d11252f50.summary: Before Saint Donatus, Archbishop of Besançon, converted the Gruyère region to Christianity, an enormous giant had made his home there whom the people of that region, in their pagan blindness, revered and worshiped as an idol.

342f9bb6d57c9ff19c20497e99e39e1a8a0cd82d.title: The Giant Gross Hans Rotzer
342f9bb6d57c9ff19c20497e99e39e1a8a0cd82d.author: Alois Lütolf
342f9bb6d57c9ff19c20497e99e39e1a8a0cd82d.summary: This gigantic man from the Melchtal is said to have donated the site for the chapel built there, and this is also said to have been the reason he was saved after an unhappy death.

41d20a645fede84a809100869202ff87682d1264.title: The Giant in the Gadmental
41d20a645fede84a809100869202ff87682d1264.author: Hermann Hartmann
41d20a645fede84a809100869202ff87682d1264.summary: In the Gadmental there is a footbridge from rock to rock called the Heidenweg.

dcf7db50ff35510bb88b1d33dd1545577ade71b5.author: C. Kohlrusch
dcf7db50ff35510bb88b1d33dd1545577ade71b5.summary: The Geissberg near the village of Villigen extends eastward into a cone-shaped projection. Old masonry still stands upon its summit, for which reason it is called simply the ‘Burg.’

d22f14a86e643ae29361f310fca3ce62169060a2.title: The Giant Turned to Stone
d22f14a86e643ae29361f310fca3ce62169060a2.author: C. Kohlrusch
d22f14a86e643ae29361f310fca3ce62169060a2.summary: Near the Bründlenalp lies the Dominikhöhle.

17e52b16dd42a0070ca7dcfc04c394898e6a59d7.title: The Giants in Iberg
17e52b16dd42a0070ca7dcfc04c394898e6a59d7.author: Alois Lütolf
17e52b16dd42a0070ca7dcfc04c394898e6a59d7.summary: There in the canton of Schwyz lived two giant siblings, a brother and a sister.

422e5567407a5154ed0c28594c9abc6a18eb638b.title: The Giants of Iseltwald (Hartmann)

ab89983f1ccab4e7b22af14aeba95af01280b83e.summary: Kohlrusch’s giants from Iseltwald turn military service into a claim to an eagle banner and three turnips.

040c17531f84dbd6b955c0a9490cc8521be499fc.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
040c17531f84dbd6b955c0a9490cc8521be499fc.summary: A father and son were plowing.

8cf420a48828e5825c9a280b219b77677359741d.summary: The Buzen are thoroughly uncanny, malicious night goblins who wish human beings no good.

abe05897d2ab9b2b77c4a3a08fca19a2acd798f5.summary: As Gerig Heiri of Spiringen traveled home from military service, one evening he accompanied a young, pretty, and, as he thought, respectable girl along the open country road.

f14bf8e67268f272f8df7eda81178a71934fbe0b.title: The Girl from the Schratten

47da9c14070bc94edca03c3a886bbf190f433463.summary: Above Flims in Graubünden lay a green alp belonging to a widow.

323e16f823c2794e7445517dcbd494df1088725d.summary: In the Küpfen above Langwies, a poor man of Langwies owned a mountain meadow and wanted to build a house there.

c753a3fb1e09f694ccea582f98558b008e4124df.author: Meinrad Lienert
c753a3fb1e09f694ccea582f98558b008e4124df.summary: There was once a farmer at Irgenhausen, a hamlet beside the Pfäffikersee.

f64253b8fadafd20a46b088b92e7dff964e2a488.summary: The old miller near the little town of Zofingen in the canton of Aargau had lost an elderly cousin.

36d0885d7734b7ba36e788ae174521b0edcaa48e.title: The Golden Cowbell

36d0885d7734b7ba36e788ae174521b0edcaa48e.summary: In Bern’s Simme Valley, where the cleanest and prettiest little wooden houses in the world stand, there once lived a young farm lad.

f4bc69c800d99cead09d3ad30bc4d831d27be9e6.summary: A golden game of ninepins is said to lie near the Martinsbrücke.

07b70390f0ba9e5e99ad0ff598b6e2cd211be061.summary: In ancient times, a castle containing unbelievable riches stood on Gasterholz hill.
