867cc9c32b447799dca939a386830a5c9e08385a.summary: Treacherous spirits and Bozen are also said once to have existed in our Valais.

8b3c0b39e2d553713df229e917b0108940ebf53f.title: The Lazy Little Goat Herd
8b3c0b39e2d553713df229e917b0108940ebf53f.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
8b3c0b39e2d553713df229e917b0108940ebf53f.summary: Once a woman hired a little goat herd and told him that he should come at a proper time to eat breakfast, so that he could let the goats out before it grew so late.

85b703ee18645d7e377d7bd4257c96b61645adbb.title: The Lazy Senn
85b703ee18645d7e377d7bd4257c96b61645adbb.author: Jakob Kuoni
85b703ee18645d7e377d7bd4257c96b61645adbb.summary: Reindeer lichen was once the herb richest in milk upon our Alps.

8f84ebb59f022c46b4dd3a052727448b943189eb.title: The Leap Ordeal
8f84ebb59f022c46b4dd3a052727448b943189eb.author: Alois Lütolf
8f84ebb59f022c46b4dd3a052727448b943189eb.summary: On the Gotthard road, where it crosses the Gornernbach above a fine bridge protected by railings to the left bank of the Reuss, lies the Pfaffensprung.

3a09f705d4fe9f3026b51ac64086a92b89f18cb7.title: The Lease Payment
3a09f705d4fe9f3026b51ac64086a92b89f18cb7.author: Meinrad Lienert
3a09f705d4fe9f3026b51ac64086a92b89f18cb7.summary: Beneath the gloomy Giswiler Stock in the land of Unterwalden lies a beautiful farmstead called the Iwi.

26656d4e7fde3d056312feb79b4319fd57353a48.title: The Leather Bridge and Silenen Castle
26656d4e7fde3d056312feb79b4319fd57353a48.author: Josef Müller
26656d4e7fde3d056312feb79b4319fd57353a48.summary: In former times, the Zwingherren tower in the village of Silenen and the tower on the Flüeli near Amsteg are said to have been connected by a leather bridge.

72ace180baf4c2328be44d37bfa44e6c0342b696.title: The Leather-Pounding Spirit
72ace180baf4c2328be44d37bfa44e6c0342b696.author: Josef Müller
72ace180baf4c2328be44d37bfa44e6c0342b696.summary: A little below the Alpliger Lücke, the pass between the Gescheneralp and Realp, a man had hidden a stolen roll of leather in a Gand. After the man’s death, however, a goatherd boy often heard him pounding leather there.

2f42271f2db313cc6af3d12d9a9b4be08c7b1553.title: The Legend of Pilatus
2f42271f2db313cc6af3d12d9a9b4be08c7b1553.author: Meinrad Lienert
2f42271f2db313cc6af3d12d9a9b4be08c7b1553.summary: Above the beautifully situated city of Lucerne on Lake Lucerne stands a mighty, jagged mountain formerly called Frakmunt. But ever since the governor Pilate has dwelt on the rugged mountain, people have called it Pilatus.

290ae5eeba9ae166c5cce14408c21a848bfb1a4b.title: The Legend of Queen Bertha
290ae5eeba9ae166c5cce14408c21a848bfb1a4b.author: C. Kohlrusch
290ae5eeba9ae166c5cce14408c21a848bfb1a4b.summary: In the tenth century, a queen named Bertha ruled the Kingdom of Burgundy, which at that time also included the land of Vaud.

0fed31ea53c701e67052301a5c1f6ad531b0265e.title: The Legend of Reifenstein
0fed31ea53c701e67052301a5c1f6ad531b0265e.author: C. Kohlrusch
0fed31ea53c701e67052301a5c1f6ad531b0265e.summary: Beside the church path that leads from Titterten to Reigoldswil, the ruins of Reifenstein Castle rise on a jagged, almost freestanding rock where a side valley opens into the broad and beautiful Reigoldswil valley.

de6b343c533271934d7b730c4a0e08263de61dbf.title: The Legend of the Blümlisalp
de6b343c533271934d7b730c4a0e08263de61dbf.author: Hermann Hartmann
de6b343c533271934d7b730c4a0e08263de61dbf.summary: A series of legends relates the destruction of the most beautiful Alpen of the Oberland.

f8c5370a8c74b0f12990375b4cb5f44ff1707fb5.title: The Legend of the Glärnisch
f8c5370a8c74b0f12990375b4cb5f44ff1707fb5.author: Theodor Vernaleken
f8c5370a8c74b0f12990375b4cb5f44ff1707fb5.summary: On the Glärnisch, there was once a magnificent Alp.

dd49d97930a992b7bebf1888ca888ff77b4d4e7c.title: The Leithund
dd49d97930a992b7bebf1888ca888ff77b4d4e7c.author: Josef Müller
dd49d97930a992b7bebf1888ca888ff77b4d4e7c.summary: a) In the ‘hohlä Gässli’ at Lucerne—or, according to others, at Brunnen—a shoemaker lived in a tiny Tatschihüsäli.

c776b17996d225ccd8d599ad8b279403085058f8.title: The Lesser Evil
c776b17996d225ccd8d599ad8b279403085058f8.author: Josef Müller
c776b17996d225ccd8d599ad8b279403085058f8.summary: Long ago, when a man was to be hanged or executed by the sword and a maiden came forward and offered to marry him, his life was spared provided that he consented to the marriage.

3219acd6a0d82d09193f2ec5a262120b38ae5fca.title: The Liberation of the Three Lands
3219acd6a0d82d09193f2ec5a262120b38ae5fca.author: Meinrad Lienert
3219acd6a0d82d09193f2ec5a262120b38ae5fca.summary: When the Landvögte of the three lands of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden learned of Gessler’s death at the hands of the marksman Tell, they took fright.

95338069e589e3578d55df630b8bb8945e2ab718.title: The Liberties around the Homburg
95338069e589e3578d55df630b8bb8945e2ab718.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
95338069e589e3578d55df630b8bb8945e2ab718.summary: Northwest of the village of Oberfrick, the Homberg and the Thiersteinberg face one another.

6906ae590f8ccd017c5384ae06746014fe58def9.title: The Lichtensteiner-Bödeli
6906ae590f8ccd017c5384ae06746014fe58def9.author: Dietrich Jecklin
6906ae590f8ccd017c5384ae06746014fe58def9.summary: A man from Haldenstein was once standing watch while serving in the Dutch forces, and a powerful longing for his dear homeland came over him.

e71781273a60659f140d14a68cc8263bc9f25ec5.title: The Light in the Lohäule
e71781273a60659f140d14a68cc8263bc9f25ec5.author: M. Sooder
e71781273a60659f140d14a68cc8263bc9f25ec5.summary: A light always comes from the Chüehweid, forward through the Lohäule as far as the Altburg. There it suddenly flares up as high as a room and disappears.

02a9ccbdf6f438e2f25a3b966bb0d58ddc4e2722.title: The Lilies
02a9ccbdf6f438e2f25a3b966bb0d58ddc4e2722.author: Jakob Kuoni
02a9ccbdf6f438e2f25a3b966bb0d58ddc4e2722.summary: Two men who could not get along down in the valley could not do so up on the alpine pasture either, where one day they unexpectedly met.

cb041c40f8dc40d8b558960439aea8550f2f3c98.title: The Limping Kostkuh
cb041c40f8dc40d8b558960439aea8550f2f3c98.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
cb041c40f8dc40d8b558960439aea8550f2f3c98.summary: Whenever an Emmental Senn left his Alp in autumn and wished to go home, he had to leave a Kostkuh standing up in the stable; otherwise, he could never reach the valley safely.

354ecb522f4a6ecf5bdae7ba6e58b9829d94cfce.title: The Lindegiger on the Ruckfeld
354ecb522f4a6ecf5bdae7ba6e58b9829d94cfce.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
354ecb522f4a6ecf5bdae7ba6e58b9829d94cfce.summary: Anyone going from the little town of Brugg to Zurzach encounters an old linden tree at the crossroads on the broad Ruckfeld, with benches built around its trunk.

5b5d24e2cf989c265a1493f9586693e439413241.title: The Linden of Linn
5b5d24e2cf989c265a1493f9586693e439413241.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
5b5d24e2cf989c265a1493f9586693e439413241.summary: One of the largest and oldest trees in Aargau is the linden on the Bötzberg, which gave the nearby little village of Linn its name.

e8e0be7724ead73ce4d919945935f23a1849ab96.title: The Linden Tree and the Miller’s Servant
e8e0be7724ead73ce4d919945935f23a1849ab96.author: Alois Lütolf
e8e0be7724ead73ce4d919945935f23a1849ab96.summary: In former times, a mighty tall linden tree stood by the front mill at Hergiswil.

d2082f1e909656f73d516d389720eb2d50f8a156.title: The Lindwurm
d2082f1e909656f73d516d389720eb2d50f8a156.author: Jakob Kuoni
d2082f1e909656f73d516d389720eb2d50f8a156.summary: On the Grabser Alpen there once lived a terrible Lindwurm.

fb46a2351d85c5a13654a63040fcfe11366e3ed9.title: The Lirenkind
fb46a2351d85c5a13654a63040fcfe11366e3ed9.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
fb46a2351d85c5a13654a63040fcfe11366e3ed9.summary: Between the villages of Ober-Siggingen and Unter-Siggingen, on the slope of the Siggingerberg, lies the little wood called Lirenhölzli, surrounded on the east and west by vineyards.

754b82b1e4f03f513068e824e34a6466656935dc.title: The Little Alp Mother (Mels, St. Gallen)
754b82b1e4f03f513068e824e34a6466656935dc.author: Jakob Kuoni
754b82b1e4f03f513068e824e34a6466656935dc.summary: A maiden was once clearing a piece of ground at Tödigerhütte on the Flumser Grossberg in order to plant potatoes.

06702fc9fe3990b79b7f66b893041b6d8f405206.title: The Little Bell and the Rübi
06702fc9fe3990b79b7f66b893041b6d8f405206.author: Josef Müller
06702fc9fe3990b79b7f66b893041b6d8f405206.summary: In one place, a Rübi rushed down the valley and caused damage.

0381891b514baa052bc19fc030e7ca6d96fc9346.title: The Little Bird That Laid Golden Eggs
0381891b514baa052bc19fc030e7ca6d96fc9346.author: Dietrich Jecklin
0381891b514baa052bc19fc030e7ca6d96fc9346.summary: Not far from a large city lived a broom maker who could barely manage to feed his wife and two boys.

8b869dc983b9546066854bf777fbe5890309c757.title: The Little Black Dog
8b869dc983b9546066854bf777fbe5890309c757.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
8b869dc983b9546066854bf777fbe5890309c757.summary: Between Vernamiége and Mâse, in a ravine bounded by the two crossed ridges Charchilly and Terreyssy, it is said to be haunted and uncanny even today, from the Borgne up to the crest.

c04449f1a0e19507c14ed4fd5ce58087aa480a01.title: The Little Bone
c04449f1a0e19507c14ed4fd5ce58087aa480a01.author: C. Kohlrusch
c04449f1a0e19507c14ed4fd5ce58087aa480a01.summary: Many years ago, on the Sandalp, which extends into the farthest corner of the Linth valley at the foot of the highest Glarus mountains, an evil man from Linthal had his Alpine dairy hut and, like the other herdsmen, spent the summer there with his cattle.

70b98c82e6038e9de25d9eacd3f8fdf94e6a0c32.title: The Little Brother’s Hut on the Wiedereck near Effingen
70b98c82e6038e9de25d9eacd3f8fdf94e6a0c32.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
70b98c82e6038e9de25d9eacd3f8fdf94e6a0c32.summary: The Wiedereck is a mountain covered with vines from foot to crown, beside the village of Effingen in the Fricktal.

1ca53a024b89f7ff8090e675738b31a3178995c6.title: The Little Cat
1ca53a024b89f7ff8090e675738b31a3178995c6.author: Meinrad Lienert
1ca53a024b89f7ff8090e675738b31a3178995c6.summary: Many hundreds of years ago, the Pestleutchen once brought the Great Death from foreign lands into the mountains of Valais.

cd7d24730dbbcc4dab3ebcf1bd940b4055b767a5.title: The Little Chamois Cheese
cd7d24730dbbcc4dab3ebcf1bd940b4055b767a5.author: Meinrad Lienert
cd7d24730dbbcc4dab3ebcf1bd940b4055b767a5.summary: In Graubünden, above Camana in the middle of the Safien valley, there once lived a wild Fänggenmännlein.

90eaeed458bec22402dbb19094fdf858a7e0e4f7.title: The Little Church at Freibach
90eaeed458bec22402dbb19094fdf858a7e0e4f7.author: M. Sooder
90eaeed458bec22402dbb19094fdf858a7e0e4f7.summary: The little church at Freibach stood below the Rain, where the path goes down toward the Moos.

9bc65cbf7463c7c2f02842055b5f1feb61981f2b.title: The Little Cross Among the Dancing Folk
9bc65cbf7463c7c2f02842055b5f1feb61981f2b.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
9bc65cbf7463c7c2f02842055b5f1feb61981f2b.summary: In the Voralpe of Rouaz in the Sanetsch Valley, so it is told, a merry nighttime dance was once arranged.

3ed5b668d5aaa29b6e050ab3f612181ec4b00d96.title: The Little Crumbs on the Table
3ed5b668d5aaa29b6e050ab3f612181ec4b00d96.author: Otto Sutermeister
3ed5b668d5aaa29b6e050ab3f612181ec4b00d96.summary: A rooster once said to his little hens, “Come quickly up into the room and peck together the bread crumbs on the table. Our mistress has gone out to make a visit.”

ab0242f9652a48ec5ec3677bbaa3e0789e12055f.title: The Little Dwarf Woman of Fontanix
ab0242f9652a48ec5ec3677bbaa3e0789e12055f.author: Jakob Kuoni
ab0242f9652a48ec5ec3677bbaa3e0789e12055f.summary: Many dwarfs once lived at Fontanix on the Wangs mountain.

d6a6a3eade7a19c58ad4823cdc35d66b19b7b55d.title: The Little Earth Men on the Ramsflue
d6a6a3eade7a19c58ad4823cdc35d66b19b7b55d.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
d6a6a3eade7a19c58ad4823cdc35d66b19b7b55d.summary: Behind the Aerlisbacher-Egg, between the little village of Hard and the old Lawrence Kapällele, there stands all alone in a valley a terribly overgrown Flue called the Ramsflue.

57cac5c4b2287f18cc2b2849c0707eb6b85f33e6.title: The Little Farmer and the Alraune
57cac5c4b2287f18cc2b2849c0707eb6b85f33e6.author: Josef Müller
57cac5c4b2287f18cc2b2849c0707eb6b85f33e6.summary: a) A poor wretch with a large brood of children was in great need.

4ed35c3af415b2f208e30e8ec3f327a4be2b416e.title: The Little Feed Hand
4ed35c3af415b2f208e30e8ec3f327a4be2b416e.author: Theodor Vernaleken
4ed35c3af415b2f208e30e8ec3f327a4be2b416e.summary: One evening, a little man came to a farmer in the canton of Bern who fed his hay to livestock at a remote place and offered his services as a feed hand.

4860918f45bcff073e2ed874ef33e1813076a69f.title: The Little Fox and the Innkeeper’s Daughter
4860918f45bcff073e2ed874ef33e1813076a69f.author: Josef Müller
4860918f45bcff073e2ed874ef33e1813076a69f.summary: An innkeeper’s son was hunting foxes.

571ffe13d65ffc9fec16195198d043f0f445d7eb.title: The Little Fox in the Ebnet
571ffe13d65ffc9fec16195198d043f0f445d7eb.author: Josef Müller
571ffe13d65ffc9fec16195198d043f0f445d7eb.summary: A fox stole the finest lambs and kids from the owner of the Ebnet at Sisikon.

386e9ca9a4ad2e8e83125a1a68d8fe0b3d39e9d6.title: The Little Fox on the Glattalp
386e9ca9a4ad2e8e83125a1a68d8fe0b3d39e9d6.author: Josef Müller
386e9ca9a4ad2e8e83125a1a68d8fe0b3d39e9d6.summary: a) Two men from Uri, one married and the other a handsome bachelor, went hunting on the Glattalp in the canton of Schwyz.

fd62921e4d6267e53c6b17a0b3d1bcbbd04549bd.title: The Little Frog with the Red Collar
fd62921e4d6267e53c6b17a0b3d1bcbbd04549bd.author: Arthur Rossat
fd62921e4d6267e53c6b17a0b3d1bcbbd04549bd.summary: Once there was a poor, hunchbacked woman who was always ailing.

6775750fb2d208168cd6a6384b92764810478cc9.title: The Little Gold Man
6775750fb2d208168cd6a6384b92764810478cc9.author: Dietrich Jecklin
6775750fb2d208168cd6a6384b92764810478cc9.summary: A quarter of an hour outside Sculms rises a high rock wall.

364dc22dcd538715eef06da65de61fd33b54eaf6.title: The Little Gray Man
364dc22dcd538715eef06da65de61fd33b54eaf6.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
364dc22dcd538715eef06da65de61fd33b54eaf6.summary: An alp in Goms is said often to have been very uncanny.

184a529f380d52065328c2c8daedeb5d705fa06e.title: The Little Green Frog
184a529f380d52065328c2c8daedeb5d705fa06e.author: Josef Müller
184a529f380d52065328c2c8daedeb5d705fa06e.summary: Once every year, a man from Bürglen drove cattle “across into the Italian-speaking country” to the Italian autumn markets.

1e9696ad9cc07ccc49eb28ec58328cc7518a086f.title: The Little Green Man
1e9696ad9cc07ccc49eb28ec58328cc7518a086f.author: M. Sooder
1e9696ad9cc07ccc49eb28ec58328cc7518a086f.summary: a) In earlier times people used to tell many stories about the grüene Manndli.

0367816f4e473561673e89af1434d60687f97e57.title: The Little Green Man in Theel, near Leuk
0367816f4e473561673e89af1434d60687f97e57.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
0367816f4e473561673e89af1434d60687f97e57.summary: Near the Riset barn, about half an hour below Guttet, a green man is said to have been seen often, and he played many a wicked trick on passersby.

1271e1d194059f769e59a514cf3d3b14b7098ab2.title: The Little Herb of Wisdom
1271e1d194059f769e59a514cf3d3b14b7098ab2.author: Dietrich Jecklin
1271e1d194059f769e59a514cf3d3b14b7098ab2.summary: After wisdom was no longer lacking in any other community up and down the land, only the Senter (Sinser) still lacked it.

13c75cd31bad85379f72c77705b63c6a99881f3d.title: The Little Leather Cap
13c75cd31bad85379f72c77705b63c6a99881f3d.author: Meinrad Lienert
13c75cd31bad85379f72c77705b63c6a99881f3d.summary: A woman making cheese in the Safien Valley is offered weather advice by a small man in a leather cap.

edefb0510394c9b6168166e4c671e6326db9f904.title: The Little Light on the Langete
edefb0510394c9b6168166e4c671e6326db9f904.author: M. Sooder
edefb0510394c9b6168166e4c671e6326db9f904.summary: Once, late in the evening, I was walking home from Dietel.

b12e25a5da5453c6e99008b819ea1e5ce9351448.title: The Little Man from Tuf
b12e25a5da5453c6e99008b819ea1e5ce9351448.author: Jakob Kuoni
b12e25a5da5453c6e99008b819ea1e5ce9351448.summary: Schaan (Oberschan) is far and wide the oldest village.

e51d4540fb0cb945a2579b52b666f3726cb09b11.title: The Little Man in the Gülle at Tegerfelden
e51d4540fb0cb945a2579b52b666f3726cb09b11.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
e51d4540fb0cb945a2579b52b666f3726cb09b11.summary: Long ago, before the old trade road to and from the Zurzach fair passed through Tegerfelden, a wondrous married couple lived in this village.

02e84af4068ab59f4b99828a0f501b66002c14b3.title: The Little Man in the Riverbed
02e84af4068ab59f4b99828a0f501b66002c14b3.author: C. Kohlrusch
02e84af4068ab59f4b99828a0f501b66002c14b3.summary: Whenever the forest stream called the Lombach, which flows through the wild and narrow valley of Habkern, threatens to fill with water and overflow, a little man comes striding along its bed before the waters surge.

d875765a78c0c9956e37968d9f8ba0d267907b19.title: The Little Man of Grünenfeld
d875765a78c0c9956e37968d9f8ba0d267907b19.author: Jakob Kuoni
d875765a78c0c9956e37968d9f8ba0d267907b19.summary: The clock on the tower of the Mels church struck eleven.

c675ef10e19af27aa19ef499f65aaabcc79b82ef.title: The Little Man of the Harder
c675ef10e19af27aa19ef499f65aaabcc79b82ef.author: Hermann Hartmann
c675ef10e19af27aa19ef499f65aaabcc79b82ef.summary: When the religious house of Interlaken stood at the height of its power and clever provosts had managed to extend its possessions far beyond the gates of Bern and concentrate the finest Alp holdings all around in their own hands—when…

03e75954452689070e83cab9d0cb71a3e0bfc3f1.title: The Little Man on the Withered Branch
03e75954452689070e83cab9d0cb71a3e0bfc3f1.author: M. Sooder
03e75954452689070e83cab9d0cb71a3e0bfc3f1.summary: In his younger years, my father was a Charer out in the villages. Later, while we children were eating, he sometimes told us a little story that he declared to be true.

b8b6600c32dbdb74100486aaf4726b753719a5f9.title: The Little Man Who Would Not Brush Against Anyone
b8b6600c32dbdb74100486aaf4726b753719a5f9.author: Alois Lütolf
b8b6600c32dbdb74100486aaf4726b753719a5f9.summary: There were also Erdleutle in Uri's Jsenthal.

63e42f37d12eb3ad584c3bbc6c8206e5e44d6a42.title: The Little Peasant in Heaven
63e42f37d12eb3ad584c3bbc6c8206e5e44d6a42.author: Otto Sutermeister
63e42f37d12eb3ad584c3bbc6c8206e5e44d6a42.summary: Once a poor, pious Bürli died and came to the gate of heaven.

967d74b2183fc32a7484ff97eb171907ffbf338e.title: The Little Plague People
967d74b2183fc32a7484ff97eb171907ffbf338e.author: Hermann Hartmann
967d74b2183fc32a7484ff97eb171907ffbf338e.summary: In the fourteenth century there was a great Sterbet in the Bernese country.

fd16bbdc583db890a4f3586e4e75c298169c2976.title: The Little Red Cloth near Castelen
fd16bbdc583db890a4f3586e4e75c298169c2976.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
fd16bbdc583db890a4f3586e4e75c298169c2976.summary: A fugitive from distant lands came to Thalheim in the Jura and bought Castelen Castle behind the Gislifluh, where he lived in complete seclusion with only a manservant and a maid.

79c170f0a4ccf23a35d7c45f479b29654e13d972.title: The Little Red Lady
79c170f0a4ccf23a35d7c45f479b29654e13d972.author: Dietrich Jecklin
79c170f0a4ccf23a35d7c45f479b29654e13d972.summary: Near the larger lake on the Curer Alp stand several “gestrickte” houses and stables, joined from smoothly hewn beams or logs. On the site of one of these houses there formerly stood another in which things were “not right.”

d09829985ef3a6427d35b0b5f3e4439b5fdee97d.title: The Little Snow Man
d09829985ef3a6427d35b0b5f3e4439b5fdee97d.author: Jakob Kuoni
d09829985ef3a6427d35b0b5f3e4439b5fdee97d.summary: Lukas Manhart, a herder of many years, relates: ‘On evenings before snowstorms break in during late autumn and force the herders to descend from the Alp with the herd, I often saw a little man in a white cloak who called very strangely but entered nowhere.

3e4added6501677e38ccd13e0c5ba32fa957a27a.title: The Little Swineherd
3e4added6501677e38ccd13e0c5ba32fa957a27a.author: Meinrad Lienert
3e4added6501677e38ccd13e0c5ba32fa957a27a.summary: At the outlet of the beautiful and great Lake Geneva, in which the snow-covered mountains of Savoy are reflected, lies the proud Swiss city of Geneva, which even today likes to call itself the Republic of Geneva.

ce1af143b95b2e07b80579980359f11d02b1ced3.title: The Little Venediger Man
ce1af143b95b2e07b80579980359f11d02b1ced3.author: Meinrad Lienert
ce1af143b95b2e07b80579980359f11d02b1ced3.summary: In olden times, very strange, dark-haired people from the Welschland often climbed up onto the Swiss Alps.

57283da24c99598b83a5c79455a8a137eb827895.title: The Little Wild Man at Conters
57283da24c99598b83a5c79455a8a137eb827895.author: Theodor Vernaleken
57283da24c99598b83a5c79455a8a137eb827895.summary: At Conters, too, a wildes Männlein tended the cows for a long time. Then, when people once gave it a suit of clothes and it had put them on, it likewise grew proud, tossed the herding staff high into the air, and sang:

65a8552aca287913c5634f8ddb2007c676064f6c.title: The Little Wild Man’s Advice
65a8552aca287913c5634f8ddb2007c676064f6c.author: Jakob Kuoni
65a8552aca287913c5634f8ddb2007c676064f6c.summary: The dwarfs went barefoot and often looked enviously at the shoes worn by other human children.

536fefb093a27439b8f5a9318693ad3fc4fa6560.title: The Little Wild Men in Maladers
536fefb093a27439b8f5a9318693ad3fc4fa6560.author: Theodor Vernaleken
536fefb093a27439b8f5a9318693ad3fc4fa6560.summary: In various places, wilden Männlein have tended people’s cattle, driving them to pasture and home again. They never accepted any payment for their services other than milk and other food.

be4d982c65b41b6d3ac91cbb2bb010fbf9e68f01.title: The Little Wild Men’s Gratitude
be4d982c65b41b6d3ac91cbb2bb010fbf9e68f01.author: Jakob Kuoni
be4d982c65b41b6d3ac91cbb2bb010fbf9e68f01.summary: On the Feuscha, a mountain farm at the front of the roughly 500-meter-high Krachenwand, in the middle of which lies a large inaccessible cave, there once lived a married couple frequently visited by the wilden Mannli who inhabited the cave just mentioned.

5e937490fef704cac7309db28e09f5a5bd6569ce.title: The Little Woman by the Lushütte
5e937490fef704cac7309db28e09f5a5bd6569ce.author: M. Sooder
5e937490fef704cac7309db28e09f5a5bd6569ce.summary: It was a fine day; the cattle were grazing, and the carpenters were doing some work around the Lushütte.

bee4704e40cf8a82abd13273f516c745971480c4.title: The Little Woman Makes Fritters
bee4704e40cf8a82abd13273f516c745971480c4.author: M. Sooder
bee4704e40cf8a82abd13273f516c745971480c4.summary: A farmwife rarely went to church, but every Sunday, she told all the servants to go. When the Prediglüt came home, every platter and every basin stood full of Chüechli.

9c82b7abd3e1c3b9ea05424e5c9e86dca1e4509e.title: The Little Woman of St. Gall
9c82b7abd3e1c3b9ea05424e5c9e86dca1e4509e.author: Jakob Kuoni
9c82b7abd3e1c3b9ea05424e5c9e86dca1e4509e.summary: In the village of Schänis stands the old Heidenturm; the church belonging to it burned down in 1824. The grassy area before it is the old churchyard. The St. Gall-Weibchen is seen there during the Fronfastenzeit.

6c8fe4f5b15a194bcfbf0c187bce5101a7a4de95.title: The Little Woman of Steckborn
6c8fe4f5b15a194bcfbf0c187bce5101a7a4de95.author: Jakob Kuoni
6c8fe4f5b15a194bcfbf0c187bce5101a7a4de95.summary: In olden times, the so-called ’s Wibli vo Steckbore came to church every year to celebrate Christmas there.

e2647e4898969f5c9d04d45f02e9bf404e8a4fc2.title: The Little Woman on Sossau Lane
e2647e4898969f5c9d04d45f02e9bf404e8a4fc2.author: M. Sooder
e2647e4898969f5c9d04d45f02e9bf404e8a4fc2.summary: When it is about to strübere—to turn rough and squally—an ugly little woman stands on Sossaugass where the path climbs toward Holzacher; her face is full of wrinkles and gray to look at like Spinnhuppele.

75fa8dcd78c81c0a567fc25ca261403a9e024862.title: The Little Woman with the Little Rake
75fa8dcd78c81c0a567fc25ca261403a9e024862.author: M. Sooder
75fa8dcd78c81c0a567fc25ca261403a9e024862.summary: When one comes up the hill at Ausel by the Chappeli, a path leads back toward Sali. A hollow tree formerly stood there. A Fraueli was sometimes said to come out of the hollow. She carried a wooden Rächeli.

15653614ddb7913f5ad3b3f61007548aec0ba604.title: The Little-Child Tree
15653614ddb7913f5ad3b3f61007548aec0ba604.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
15653614ddb7913f5ad3b3f61007548aec0ba604.summary: Among the rent-paying properties of the village of Koblenz, the 1664 rent roll of the Klingnau provostry lists, on page 192b, the Söthenzelge field section, whose boundary on the reed meadow is marked by the Little-Child Pear Tree.

29bb6b2b6c2c4d979a493cabf16b3eb19e712257.title: The Lochluegenjäger
29bb6b2b6c2c4d979a493cabf16b3eb19e712257.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
29bb6b2b6c2c4d979a493cabf16b3eb19e712257.summary: On the road from the village of Leerau to Staffelbach lies the Grossstein to the west and, to the east, a basin-shaped depression in the valley called the Lochluege.

1a6cd29c1fb1876374def708afb66aab4789d567.title: The Locusts on the Glacier
1a6cd29c1fb1876374def708afb66aab4789d567.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
1a6cd29c1fb1876374def708afb66aab4789d567.summary: What a plague of locusts is — or rather, what damage these tiny creatures can cause — is now, unfortunately, known from experience in the Upper Valais, especially around Visp.

55e841c9cb06c629313e7bd73af20183a7b13d8d.title: The Lohhäwle Buck
55e841c9cb06c629313e7bd73af20183a7b13d8d.author: M. Sooder
55e841c9cb06c629313e7bd73af20183a7b13d8d.summary: The Lohhäwle used to be uncanny too. There, the Lohhäwlebock would suddenly spring onto a person's back. When we were children, people made him into a Bölima to frighten us.

6cd08ceaf09f871bb0037b994e357a25688de7d5.title: The Long Bridge
6cd08ceaf09f871bb0037b994e357a25688de7d5.author: Jakob Kuoni
6cd08ceaf09f871bb0037b994e357a25688de7d5.summary: Not far from Magdenau Abbey, Allenschwanden Castle stood on a Gütsch; and across the valley, likewise on a mountain ridge, stood another castle.

5a42ec941cf67751c57263a01946f575c977edf1.title: The Lords of Mangipani Castle
5a42ec941cf67751c57263a01946f575c977edf1.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
5a42ec941cf67751c57263a01946f575c977edf1.summary: Two hours above Brig, where the Rhone foams like a mountain torrent through its narrow bed of rock, lies the little village of Moerel.

5a50e9f533aecc65d0d348a3731dc82e861db04c.title: The Lords of Rotental
5a50e9f533aecc65d0d348a3731dc82e861db04c.author: C. Kohlrusch
5a50e9f533aecc65d0d348a3731dc82e861db04c.summary: On the southwest side of the Jungfrau, high above its foot, lies a fearsomely glaciated valley, the Rotental or Rottal.

68dd31dfa61f9dada2542dd49cdf2412d0d214d7.title: The Lords of Rottal
68dd31dfa61f9dada2542dd49cdf2412d0d214d7.author: M. Sooder
68dd31dfa61f9dada2542dd49cdf2412d0d214d7.summary: When the Rottalhere shoot, the old people said, bad weather follows.

8aebaf7376eaecf78715f17159ce30739ee8b661.title: The Losplatte in the Kiental
8aebaf7376eaecf78715f17159ce30739ee8b661.author: Hermann Hartmann
8aebaf7376eaecf78715f17159ce30739ee8b661.summary: The first people to set foot in the Kiental were two brothers.

99bd216c7e6efcc90d386481ce19e9e7df3263b9.title: The Lost Child
99bd216c7e6efcc90d386481ce19e9e7df3263b9.author: C. Kohlrusch
99bd216c7e6efcc90d386481ce19e9e7df3263b9.summary: On one of the branches of the Jura above the village of Ettingen lie the remains of Fürstenstein Castle, once the fortified residence of the Lords of Rothberg.

f17821fcfec1d1430b68064ddf5883881c72706b.title: The Lost Cows
f17821fcfec1d1430b68064ddf5883881c72706b.author: Theodor Vernaleken
f17821fcfec1d1430b68064ddf5883881c72706b.summary: A farmer named Oswald at Itramen in the Grindelwald Valley had 7 magnificent cows.

b4c1ecd8259b364d01720185e556e0ab9320c7cf.title: The Lost Mine
b4c1ecd8259b364d01720185e556e0ab9320c7cf.author: Dietrich Jecklin
b4c1ecd8259b364d01720185e556e0ab9320c7cf.summary: In former times mining was also attempted at several places in the Stürviser-Tal, but without substantial success.

f68374dc5fa2b43110baa7cc10473f4c343e6ff4.title: The Lost Voralpe
f68374dc5fa2b43110baa7cc10473f4c343e6ff4.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
f68374dc5fa2b43110baa7cc10473f4c343e6ff4.summary: In the foothills of the Sanetsch valley, between Garey and Malonnaz, loose stone rubble shows the traces of an ancient landslide.

06764089fa0953feaf8606c3529f89ca6e99b8fc.title: The Lost Zytgeissli
06764089fa0953feaf8606c3529f89ca6e99b8fc.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
06764089fa0953feaf8606c3529f89ca6e99b8fc.summary: A hunter had lost his beloved Zytgeissli, as young goats are called in Valais, and this grieved him deeply.

9eb7239edac80fb2572d2f43d874c891d355a03e.title: The Lovers' Death
9eb7239edac80fb2572d2f43d874c891d355a03e.author: Jakob Kuoni
9eb7239edac80fb2572d2f43d874c891d355a03e.summary: An Austrian knight was captured by the Swiss in war and confined in the tower at Wallenstadt.

c1f712a984a41e178fcc86d8ba563ad8c3d98f54.title: The Lucky Hunter
c1f712a984a41e178fcc86d8ba563ad8c3d98f54.author: Dietrich Jecklin
c1f712a984a41e178fcc86d8ba563ad8c3d98f54.summary: Years ago there lived in Ruis a very skillful hunter who, during the chamois-hunting season, brought home a chamois every day.

bfa130033fe4fb167f696104793db5c813908b27.title: The Lusgen Boze
bfa130033fe4fb167f696104793db5c813908b27.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
bfa130033fe4fb167f696104793db5c813908b27.summary: The high pasture of Lusgen lies at Aletschbort and belongs to Belalp.

4cf8cfe35228c2056ea88260e70bf0fff9c5cf68.title: The Lädeligugger-Faveri of Tägerig
4cf8cfe35228c2056ea88260e70bf0fff9c5cf68.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
4cf8cfe35228c2056ea88260e70bf0fff9c5cf68.summary: More than a generation ago, a very poor man lived in Tägerig among the last houses on the country road toward Mellingen.

3c91b4ace5710156fec180c4b96ca4e25838c019.title: The Läheme’s Boy
3c91b4ace5710156fec180c4b96ca4e25838c019.author: M. Sooder
3c91b4ace5710156fec180c4b96ca4e25838c019.summary: Humorous narratives travel up and down the country as ‘little samples’ or ‘little pieces.’ Almost every village in our region bears a nickname hung upon it by the teasing of friendly neighbors, but none stands out in particular.

68fd3a9be5bdea8d2dace21ebec8e8f3d5175060.title: The Lälle of Rheinfelden
68fd3a9be5bdea8d2dace21ebec8e8f3d5175060.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
68fd3a9be5bdea8d2dace21ebec8e8f3d5175060.summary: At the time when the Swedes were besieging the town of Rheinfelden, they bribed a rich and violent citizen inside with a large sum of money to deliver the fortress into their hands.

6369302b609e8c9223c3b3902bdd61a3343b8998.title: The Lämmli Hole near Wegenstetten
6369302b609e8c9223c3b3902bdd61a3343b8998.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
6369302b609e8c9223c3b3902bdd61a3343b8998.summary: On the side facing the village of Wegenstetten, high in the cliffs of the Fricktal Jura mountain called Homberg—or, to distinguish it from others of the same name, Thiersteinberg—lies a cave with a stone bench and baking trough hewn out on both sides.

8f15a77f19c6e313e80cc98a9cfc42970c7c8235.title: The Läuwitiär
8f15a77f19c6e313e80cc98a9cfc42970c7c8235.author: Josef Müller
8f15a77f19c6e313e80cc98a9cfc42970c7c8235.summary: Every year in spring, the Wylerplangg avalanche thunders down into the valley from the heights of the Rienzenberg chain.

434e1c6212cefb2c179cebaefb73d062fb021de8.title: The Magic Book
434e1c6212cefb2c179cebaefb73d062fb021de8.author: Josef Müller
434e1c6212cefb2c179cebaefb73d062fb021de8.summary: A goatherd reads a book aloud and finds a bottle of wine on the table. A Capuchin hears his story and says where the wine came from.

f508b90728a107a8368062b8de332c2121721425.title: The Magic Book and the Geissbuben
f508b90728a107a8368062b8de332c2121721425.author: Josef Müller
f508b90728a107a8368062b8de332c2121721425.summary: Two Geissbuben in Isental, who preferred stretching out in the cool shade to running after the goats, were seized by a farmer by their hair and ears because the goats had grazed the tastiest herbs from his land.

fdc9c4d4b54b6d0a8c3c3e2dff7f0c8a2d9b3a5f.title: The Magic Book Helps in Time of Need
fdc9c4d4b54b6d0a8c3c3e2dff7f0c8a2d9b3a5f.author: Josef Müller
fdc9c4d4b54b6d0a8c3c3e2dff7f0c8a2d9b3a5f.summary: A priest refuses to absolve a man who keeps a magic book. The two later take shelter together in a hut, where the book unexpectedly protects them.

6fb9e2c043f7401c2d7f52051c8b1b2b4c7b0f6a.title: The Magic Book of the Three Poor Boys
6fb9e2c043f7401c2d7f52051c8b1b2b4c7b0f6a.author: Josef Müller
6fb9e2c043f7401c2d7f52051c8b1b2b4c7b0f6a.summary: Three hungry boys use a book to go unseen into the priest’s barn for milk foam. Their mother and the collector have different views about what the boys should have done.

0faaae2fa41dacf33fcd277224457ec838067799.title: The Magic Nail
0faaae2fa41dacf33fcd277224457ec838067799.author: Josef Müller
0faaae2fa41dacf33fcd277224457ec838067799.summary: Feld-Baschi's family in Gurtnellen had “a fine row” of smoked meat hanging in the chimney when a Romani woman entered the house, looked at it, and praised it.

ff0b3aab0d2c528175a33457e64f32fc0a155158.title: The Magic Ride
ff0b3aab0d2c528175a33457e64f32fc0a155158.author: Dietrich Jecklin
ff0b3aab0d2c528175a33457e64f32fc0a155158.summary: An Oberländer was serving as a sentry before the royal palace in Paris.

49b1ff80432c377f0a666ec29bfc7a4de9a766c8.title: The Magic Rock
49b1ff80432c377f0a666ec29bfc7a4de9a766c8.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
49b1ff80432c377f0a666ec29bfc7a4de9a766c8.summary: Three hours above Spitzegg, a bare head of rock rises from the brown of the Alpwiesen.

85f6ac50238de314414984df38db767c091ede7a.title: The Magical Apparatus
85f6ac50238de314414984df38db767c091ede7a.author: Alois Lütolf
85f6ac50238de314414984df38db767c091ede7a.summary: a) Among the apparatus belonging to Hans Blattmann of Ägeri, who had to answer charges of sorcery in Lucerne around 1597, were the following objects: a fire mirror, keys, a Krampfring, a silver sign, small consecrated wax candles…

ebdcfa2b5b0d64fd8db71dc9bcab8b80dd3c8d2c.title: The Magnanimous People of Nidwalden
ebdcfa2b5b0d64fd8db71dc9bcab8b80dd3c8d2c.author: Meinrad Lienert
ebdcfa2b5b0d64fd8db71dc9bcab8b80dd3c8d2c.summary: Once, the citizens of the good city of Lucerne had a bitter dispute with the country people of the valleys of Unterwalden nid dem Kernwald over a right on the lofty Bürgenberg.

7003552f9dae435c8184484f3f4078295c86eb06.title: The Magpie’s Cry
7003552f9dae435c8184484f3f4078295c86eb06.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
7003552f9dae435c8184484f3f4078295c86eb06.summary: When magpies repeatedly chatter around a person, that person must pray, for each time something bad lies ahead.

ddb92aab5cb7a977c11212f784202b2ffc2e33e7.title: The Maiden at Birr
ddb92aab5cb7a977c11212f784202b2ffc2e33e7.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
ddb92aab5cb7a977c11212f784202b2ffc2e33e7.summary: In former times, a white maiden was often seen near the rectory at Birr in the Birrfeld, standing beside a cauldron full of gold.

2a92dc3b2eb15f012cbc8de8bf01e3e2bd698c4b.title: The Maiden at the Neuacher Fire Pond
2a92dc3b2eb15f012cbc8de8bf01e3e2bd698c4b.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
2a92dc3b2eb15f012cbc8de8bf01e3e2bd698c4b.summary: Late one evening, a man from the Hohlenweg near Reinach was gathering brushwood in the forest in the region where the so-called fire pond lies.

23f1400d4291726d854570c552753ff0a202d09e.title: The Maiden in the Schilztobel
23f1400d4291726d854570c552753ff0a202d09e.author: Jakob Kuoni
23f1400d4291726d854570c552753ff0a202d09e.summary: In earlier times, the young people gathered on Sunday afternoons at a level place above the little village of Portels to dance and play.

9bdee78473a6e246f6408c43c6bbcb941160561e.title: The Maiden of Forsteck
9bdee78473a6e246f6408c43c6bbcb941160561e.author: Jakob Kuoni
9bdee78473a6e246f6408c43c6bbcb941160561e.summary: In the castle forest near Forsteck, a woman was gathering leaves.

8c471277e64f022fe2195ada5ed3ff2c629cbb92.title: The Maiden of Morteratsch (Jecklin)
8c471277e64f022fe2195ada5ed3ff2c629cbb92.author: Dietrich Jecklin
8c471277e64f022fe2195ada5ed3ff2c629cbb92.summary: In former times, on the Alp where the colossal Morteratsch Glacier now lies behind Pontresina, a young Senn named Aratsch summered the village cows.

9a35de23f146b674d12fa7888aeedc50860747a5.title: The Maiden of Morteratsch (Lechner)
9a35de23f146b674d12fa7888aeedc50860747a5.author: Ernst Lechner
9a35de23f146b674d12fa7888aeedc50860747a5.summary: Between the jagged masses of ice of the Pers and Morteratsch glaciers rises a solitary fairy island called Isla persa, the lost island.

97062b54571f1331da3d1511d08e4cc71cce6c1e.title: The Maiden on the Laubsberg near Seon
97062b54571f1331da3d1511d08e4cc71cce6c1e.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
97062b54571f1331da3d1511d08e4cc71cce6c1e.summary: The Laubsberg lies north of the village of Seon in the Hallwil lake valley.

217f2afa4496a3b1ec89005a064402f051a6b93d.title: The Maiden with the Gold
217f2afa4496a3b1ec89005a064402f051a6b93d.author: Dietrich Jecklin
217f2afa4496a3b1ec89005a064402f051a6b93d.summary: On the high Russein Alp, a Senn worked vigorously with his assistants.

ace368a507fcd65953185d601d43c96d6adcbca9.title: The Maiden Without Arms
ace368a507fcd65953185d601d43c96d6adcbca9.author: Dietrich Jecklin
ace368a507fcd65953185d601d43c96d6adcbca9.summary: In a little house outside the village there once lived a desperately poor married couple who could scarcely feed themselves and their only little daughter.

882cae524cff3c6d23bed4c28837b206c50e8b92.title: The Malicious Dwarf in the Grosse Riedera
882cae524cff3c6d23bed4c28837b206c50e8b92.author: C. Kohlrusch
882cae524cff3c6d23bed4c28837b206c50e8b92.summary: A little more than half a century ago, a cooper named Dietrich lived in the Grosse Riedera.

0f3a8ac70a7d23dc7a2eeee2d4cc9665ea2b309d.title: The Malicious Little Dwarf
0f3a8ac70a7d23dc7a2eeee2d4cc9665ea2b309d.author: Hermann Hartmann
0f3a8ac70a7d23dc7a2eeee2d4cc9665ea2b309d.summary: Above Erlenbach in the Simmental, there once lived a miserly man.

24e7046a0e022019325acce897573335787b0ddc.title: The Malicious White Woman
24e7046a0e022019325acce897573335787b0ddc.author: Dietrich Jecklin
24e7046a0e022019325acce897573335787b0ddc.summary: Not far from the village of Präz lies a broad, beautiful slope, a place favored by the village youth for ‘Schlittlen’ in winter.

3774152572a8d3d872f97b7a37de975b1d3f8bb8.title: The Man at the Hearth
3774152572a8d3d872f97b7a37de975b1d3f8bb8.author: Josef Müller
3774152572a8d3d872f97b7a37de975b1d3f8bb8.summary: “One day,” relates a sixty-year-old man from Schattdorf, “I was sitting behind our little table in the room when, all at once, through the open door I saw a man in shirtsleeves standing at the hearth in the kitchen.

d4dbedd3f56e4a08879ef16d3386fef5784c4a9b.title: The Man from Ingenbohl in Vienna
d4dbedd3f56e4a08879ef16d3386fef5784c4a9b.author: Alois Lütolf
d4dbedd3f56e4a08879ef16d3386fef5784c4a9b.summary: A man still living heard it from the son of the person to whom this happened.

f7ad57abe4078998cd25c2e96f01676ce4a381e9.title: The Man from the Schächental and the Giant
f7ad57abe4078998cd25c2e96f01676ce4a381e9.author: Josef Müller
f7ad57abe4078998cd25c2e96f01676ce4a381e9.summary: Once an extraordinarily strong man from Schwyz came into the little canton of Uri, flaunted his strength there, and challenged every Urner to a contest.

42971d63ce8e0995ca3de96f5c93111235cac93c.title: The Man in the Moon
42971d63ce8e0995ca3de96f5c93111235cac93c.author: Dietrich Jecklin
42971d63ce8e0995ca3de96f5c93111235cac93c.summary: A Senn on the Waltensburg Alp was once asked by a poor woman for a drink of milk. With harsh words, however, the coarse dairyman refused her modest request. She then cursed him to the coldest place in the world.—

4b80c9d87e028c1ec204e791e73eb1204fb70335.title: The Man of Muntclü
4b80c9d87e028c1ec204e791e73eb1204fb70335.author: C. Kohlrusch
4b80c9d87e028c1ec204e791e73eb1204fb70335.summary: In a forest called Muntclü, between the municipalities of Scuol and Ftan, a man appears at the witching hour.

3730841ae6c34c99b37163ab069fa5b8d70c8d41.title: The Man Peening the Scythe
3730841ae6c34c99b37163ab069fa5b8d70c8d41.author: Josef Müller
3730841ae6c34c99b37163ab069fa5b8d70c8d41.summary: One day up in the Lammatt at Flüelen, my mother saw an old Grittschimanndeli—that is, a poorly dressed, old, shriveled man.

daa4ef60c5006499b1bbbddd653a61b79259065a.title: The Man Who Went to the Devil
daa4ef60c5006499b1bbbddd653a61b79259065a.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
daa4ef60c5006499b1bbbddd653a61b79259065a.summary: In former times, a powerful lord named Montacuay lived in a castle in Valais.

1ac4c4a74e1f858dfc83221c5341ca892f4fbf8e.title: The Mandlene Hunter Around Villnachern
1ac4c4a74e1f858dfc83221c5341ca892f4fbf8e.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
1ac4c4a74e1f858dfc83221c5341ca892f4fbf8e.summary: Below Villnachern, on a low rise, are the remains of a castle that vague legend calls Lichtenau.

659572ede5025e8757d0824dce55a718ebb017bd.title: The Manndli That Foretold Snow
659572ede5025e8757d0824dce55a718ebb017bd.author: Josef Müller
659572ede5025e8757d0824dce55a718ebb017bd.summary: An 80-year-old Älpler from Gurtnellen, who had worked as a Senn for more than 50 years on the Alp Gornern, draws from the well of his memories: It was the 8th of Herbstmonat, late in the evening, when I sat together in the hut at…

39d418a2ead6e147b60e9c72683ef727bea63f24.title: The Manndli with the Wetterhut
39d418a2ead6e147b60e9c72683ef727bea63f24.author: Josef Müller
39d418a2ead6e147b60e9c72683ef727bea63f24.summary: When they went up to Alp Hinterfeld in the Meien Valley, it happened now and then that a little Manndli wearing a pointed, broad-brimmed Wetterhut and carrying a stick was seen on the Alp, although it never came near the hut.

9dc82148f001530615a3096ee212bcbe414afbb1.title: The March Ghost on Seelisberg
9dc82148f001530615a3096ee212bcbe414afbb1.author: Josef Müller
9dc82148f001530615a3096ee212bcbe414afbb1.summary: It was in the famine year 1816 when my husband’s grandmother, then 16 years old, and her 11-year-old sister went with their mother on pilgrimage to the Schmärzächäppäli at Emmetten.

f8149c65579a48b4feedf5ce8a619e80f15fb849.title: The March of the Laueli
f8149c65579a48b4feedf5ce8a619e80f15fb849.author: Josef Müller
f8149c65579a48b4feedf5ce8a619e80f15fb849.summary: On the Laueli Berggut adjoining the Alp of Bolgen, two farmhands were occupied in erecting the Hag.

ef30b30d14e9e2d52dc660730d917c29e26bd503.title: The Marchen-Setzer
ef30b30d14e9e2d52dc660730d917c29e26bd503.author: Dietrich Jecklin
ef30b30d14e9e2d52dc660730d917c29e26bd503.summary: One evening a man walked from Closters to Montbiel to feed the cattle. There beside the road, at the place called Bündelti, he noticed a stranger tampering with a Marchstein.

05c73ea633ef17418588beb63a8c74cbca7e288a.title: The Marchen-Verfälscher
05c73ea633ef17418588beb63a8c74cbca7e288a.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
05c73ea633ef17418588beb63a8c74cbca7e288a.summary: In former times, a black man carrying a fiery piece of hewn timber is said to have been seen at night in many places, pacing up and down across open meadows.

38393f70f8f83600c4eafd14f1fee8684cf7edfb.title: The Marchenrücker of Putz
38393f70f8f83600c4eafd14f1fee8684cf7edfb.author: Dietrich Jecklin
38393f70f8f83600c4eafd14f1fee8684cf7edfb.summary: A shoemaker from Putz once took the footpath toward Buchen.

cdf04d020626fe6d4eae25b220fb82b85101fb43.title: The Marchstein-Geist of Buffalora
cdf04d020626fe6d4eae25b220fb82b85101fb43.author: Dietrich Jecklin
cdf04d020626fe6d4eae25b220fb82b85101fb43.summary: In the previous century, the municipality of Cernez is said to have appropriated the beautiful Alp of Buffalora from the municipality of Cierfs in a highly dubious manner.

6786b2f7899333a71e516c839ef9e024563ebfce.title: The Marchsteine on Hutt-Egg
6786b2f7899333a71e516c839ef9e024563ebfce.author: Josef Müller
6786b2f7899333a71e516c839ef9e024563ebfce.summary: At Hutt-Egg in Bauen, something had often torn the Marchsteine from beneath the woods at night and carried them some distance farther down into the private property.

b9a0c53603848d837bf8afe3af76cde445837465.title: The Marchversetzer of Reinach
b9a0c53603848d837bf8afe3af76cde445837465.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
b9a0c53603848d837bf8afe3af76cde445837465.summary: Once, up by the castle at Reinach, a farmhand was driving a plow in the field with his master.

efcb5e65ab7ea9badfe1ecdb81f6f518437f626a.title: The Markenrücker (Jonschwil, SG)
efcb5e65ab7ea9badfe1ecdb81f6f518437f626a.author: Jakob Kuoni
efcb5e65ab7ea9badfe1ecdb81f6f518437f626a.summary: On the holy night, people from Schwarzenbach crossed the bridge by the Töbeli and saw two headless men who looked like Fenersäulen; a large black dog with a fiery eye was there too.

e926e55e6fbf060682cf6c635b22d1798ad5ad09.title: The Markenrücker above Grub
e926e55e6fbf060682cf6c635b22d1798ad5ad09.author: Jakob Kuoni
e926e55e6fbf060682cf6c635b22d1798ad5ad09.summary: During his lifetime, he was a respected man.

6d785037b387f75586a4b2c5de781f223d7d159d.title: The Markenrücker on Gaplon
6d785037b387f75586a4b2c5de781f223d7d159d.author: Jakob Kuoni
6d785037b387f75586a4b2c5de781f223d7d159d.summary: A man in the Kreuzgässli near Oberschan was awakened in the middle of the night by loud knocking, as though someone wished to stop for shelter.

55820a4cb5f4d7d104e40f9fa12577d2a594d5fe.title: The Marksman
55820a4cb5f4d7d104e40f9fa12577d2a594d5fe.author: Jakob Kuoni
55820a4cb5f4d7d104e40f9fa12577d2a594d5fe.summary: In the forest by the so-called Weihwasserplatte on the road from Pfäfers to Vättis, a fiery man is said sometimes to have appeared at night and shot glowing bullets at those passing after 12 o’clock.

7ceafc127002ddbca3396d5ecd6e256a7220a29a.title: The Marmots of the Saas Valley
7ceafc127002ddbca3396d5ecd6e256a7220a29a.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
7ceafc127002ddbca3396d5ecd6e256a7220a29a.summary: In ancient times, the marmots in the Saaseralpen belonged to the Blandrati counts in Visp, who possessed them not as public authorities but as Alpeigentümer.

e126d3e611c90b4d800ddf728601e7cd73c3d729.title: The Martisloch
e126d3e611c90b4d800ddf728601e7cd73c3d729.author: C. Kohlrusch
e126d3e611c90b4d800ddf728601e7cd73c3d729.summary: In the high rock wall of the nearer Eiger is a large opening. This opening bears the name Heiterloch but is also called the Martisloch.

270a29811fbaec89bc31d68dfb8e621c692cac2a.title: The Marvelous Barge
270a29811fbaec89bc31d68dfb8e621c692cac2a.author: Walter Keller
270a29811fbaec89bc31d68dfb8e621c692cac2a.summary: A farmer’s son builds a barge that travels over land and water, then asks a king to keep his promise.

aaaa9e7d34a9b52ee7bfdace64b0697996ac2790.title: The Master Appears to a Maiden
aaaa9e7d34a9b52ee7bfdace64b0697996ac2790.author: M. Sooder
aaaa9e7d34a9b52ee7bfdace64b0697996ac2790.summary: A farmwife, Müetti told me, also instructed a Jumpfere in how to angereesle. She had to sweep the room with the Hemlistock and carry out the Ghüder, walking backward the entire time.

0aeeeed613f51d98f7e0b0f2166b7e7511e517bc.title: The Master of a Thousand Arts
0aeeeed613f51d98f7e0b0f2166b7e7511e517bc.author: Alois Lütolf
0aeeeed613f51d98f7e0b0f2166b7e7511e517bc.summary: Until recently there lived in Lungern a man—God rest his soul—who wanted to be capable of more than eating bread.

720d4d7ee7e09e93d70191b2d93018c42efc1157.title: The Master of Witchcraft
720d4d7ee7e09e93d70191b2d93018c42efc1157.author: Meinrad Lienert
720d4d7ee7e09e93d70191b2d93018c42efc1157.summary: A wonder-working doctor once lived by the Devil’s Bridge near Einsiedeln in the Canton of Schwyz.

21702e8eefcdcb30a761c586a4398ef8f438950e.title: The Matthisethier in Reinach
21702e8eefcdcb30a761c586a4398ef8f438950e.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
21702e8eefcdcb30a761c586a4398ef8f438950e.summary: On Christmas Eve, a young stray kitten lay down before the window of a house in Reinach whose inhabitants were called the Matthise.

389e7d6b5f0883eded03ed14ee85dbb7521a7b2b.title: The Mattisee and the Schwedenhaus near Hettenschwil
389e7d6b5f0883eded03ed14ee85dbb7521a7b2b.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
389e7d6b5f0883eded03ed14ee85dbb7521a7b2b.summary: When the Swedes besieged the little Rhine towns of Laufenburg and Rheinfelden, they devastated all the surrounding country in the neighboring Jura and behaved with particular inhumanity in the valleys of Mandach and Hottwil.

d52c74f2848cf9606bbd78d52332fec93da6556d.title: The Mauerhubel near Zetzwil
d52c74f2848cf9606bbd78d52332fec93da6556d.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
d52c74f2848cf9606bbd78d52332fec93da6556d.summary: When the grain all around is still green in July, on the Mauerhubel it can already be seen standing in completely yellow strips as wide as a Heerstrasse.

63e6f0524fad1dd09a0e90c699fefa116615fce8.title: The Meerenschwanden Dorfloos
63e6f0524fad1dd09a0e90c699fefa116615fce8.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
63e6f0524fad1dd09a0e90c699fefa116615fce8.summary: The night ghost of the Freiamt village of Meerenschwanden is a pig that is indeed called the Dorfloos, but is just as often generally called the Dorfhund, because the latter name is the customary regional term for any familiar local ghost.

b0d3e1fd969375a5a87b5089ac9565d94d0d2e22.title: The Meerfräulein
b0d3e1fd969375a5a87b5089ac9565d94d0d2e22.author: Jakob Kuoni
b0d3e1fd969375a5a87b5089ac9565d94d0d2e22.summary: At Wintersberg there still stands a little house where three men wished to win a treasure.

49f6df8b47b4840bcec96bddcb59412e6d1d24b9.title: The Meistersfrau as a Witch
49f6df8b47b4840bcec96bddcb59412e6d1d24b9.author: Dietrich Jecklin
49f6df8b47b4840bcec96bddcb59412e6d1d24b9.summary: A boy from Bonaduz, having returned from Swabia, told his parents, among other things, that he could dance on a thread.

727661673c5ccf1eed020ef796e403c633195beb.title: The Melkfassalpe
727661673c5ccf1eed020ef796e403c633195beb.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
727661673c5ccf1eed020ef796e403c633195beb.summary: Where the great Ferpekle Glacier now lies, there were once beautiful meadows and villages.

a402a1eb9c5781b7be6f5df093776f85c4d7740d.title: The Merciful King
a402a1eb9c5781b7be6f5df093776f85c4d7740d.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
a402a1eb9c5781b7be6f5df093776f85c4d7740d.summary: In Naters I heard it told that once, up on the Belalp, a Chinig lived with his young daughter.

e6d267d1815cc744bd7b756f28d3e25a51db24bf.title: The Merzenstein
e6d267d1815cc744bd7b756f28d3e25a51db24bf.author: Josef Müller
e6d267d1815cc744bd7b756f28d3e25a51db24bf.summary: With the Merzenstein, an exposed boulder on a mountain terrace at Wyssig above Bauen, a witch intended to destroy the church of Bauen.

905c81b734107504f73da5409f91bfbf845255ce.title: The Messamt on the Hungerlialp
905c81b734107504f73da5409f91bfbf845255ce.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
905c81b734107504f73da5409f91bfbf845255ce.summary: The parish priest down in the valley had long noticed that the Sennenfamilie of the Hungerlialp never appeared at Mass.

2d6242f622c69615259cb31807d7089eeb8f2989.title: The Midnight Banquet
2d6242f622c69615259cb31807d7089eeb8f2989.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
2d6242f622c69615259cb31807d7089eeb8f2989.summary: The old and original "Felliser Josi" of Brig, a true child of temperament, was known as a seer of spirits.

c2a775549ab84c51e9ef7c949ac7cc131dacfd25.title: The Milchisbach-Hund
c2a775549ab84c51e9ef7c949ac7cc131dacfd25.author: Theodor Vernaleken
c2a775549ab84c51e9ef7c949ac7cc131dacfd25.summary: On the right bank of Lake Brienz are two places almost two hours apart, one above Ringgenberg and the other below Brienz.

3d5850b90a7c5848b463200f252d8c4235aafc16.title: The Milk Horn
3d5850b90a7c5848b463200f252d8c4235aafc16.author: Theodor Vernaleken
3d5850b90a7c5848b463200f252d8c4235aafc16.summary: North of Unterseen lies the Habkern valley.

7e445c8711acfdd90563d696cd23575175d6ca24.title: The Milk in the Herdsman's Staff
7e445c8711acfdd90563d696cd23575175d6ca24.author: Jakob Kuoni
7e445c8711acfdd90563d696cd23575175d6ca24.summary: The Geissler ‘Köbi,’ Jakob, and ‘Seppen-Lihert,’ Joseph's Leonhard, tended goats together on the Langwiese.

71d3e67d00c0fbffa2d4f1c5c91cc841664d8327.title: The Milk Soup of Kappel
71d3e67d00c0fbffa2d4f1c5c91cc841664d8327.author: Meinrad Lienert
71d3e67d00c0fbffa2d4f1c5c91cc841664d8327.summary: Once, many centuries ago, there was a very evil time.

29b7971263182db57ea7b1d0fac21417b069b74e.title: The Milk Strap (Nidelgret)
29b7971263182db57ea7b1d0fac21417b069b74e.author: Hermann Hartmann
29b7971263182db57ea7b1d0fac21417b069b74e.summary: In ancient times, a woman lived at Hasle im Grund of whom the people said that she could draw milk from a strap.

e097a8baf275b78124b63f233e27b9ff8e416159.title: The Milk Thieves
e097a8baf275b78124b63f233e27b9ff8e416159.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
e097a8baf275b78124b63f233e27b9ff8e416159.summary: Many stories are also told in Zermatt about the Godverjinen—dwarfs—little earth men.

6d10753811da9744417e9cf390bc1092d6734435.title: The Milk-Eating Nachtvolk
6d10753811da9744417e9cf390bc1092d6734435.author: Alois Lütolf
6d10753811da9744417e9cf390bc1092d6734435.summary: Hans Sager wished to go home to Willisau in the depths of night—this happened 300 years ago.

740af7bf8cdb3d9d18d09badf40c01881c74176e.title: The Milking Stool (Graubünden)
740af7bf8cdb3d9d18d09badf40c01881c74176e.author: D. Jecklin
740af7bf8cdb3d9d18d09badf40c01881c74176e.summary: A herder promises a cow to the worker who will fetch a forgotten milking stool from an abandoned alpine hut.

9bb1b60602cfaf7552890e6037f29297ffcc4e5e.title: The Milking Stool (St. Gallen)
9bb1b60602cfaf7552890e6037f29297ffcc4e5e.author: C. Kohlrusch
9bb1b60602cfaf7552890e6037f29297ffcc4e5e.summary: A wager over a forgotten milking stool sends a herder into a hut guarded by mountain spirits.

d20e0b74b84aa335e729172b2162afd05757927d.title: The Mill on the Alchbach
d20e0b74b84aa335e729172b2162afd05757927d.author: Hermann Hartmann
d20e0b74b84aa335e729172b2162afd05757927d.summary: In the municipality of Oberwil in the Simmental, a mill once stood in the Alchbachgraben.

ea3fa4e9b880b6408b27e326c94f62a053de1420.title: The Miller with His Daughters
ea3fa4e9b880b6408b27e326c94f62a053de1420.author: M. Sooder
ea3fa4e9b880b6408b27e326c94f62a053de1420.summary: A miller had three daughters who were not exactly the cleverest.

680d8920bd0d814de519e024a6177ae28f282d02.title: The Miller's Wife as a Cat
680d8920bd0d814de519e024a6177ae28f282d02.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
680d8920bd0d814de519e024a6177ae28f282d02.summary: A miller is long plagued by a wife who has given herself over to witchcraft, but he cannot prove it against her.

2ba2173aac927067a57549ea0efd8fe7ea5b963f.title: The Miller’s Wife
2ba2173aac927067a57549ea0efd8fe7ea5b963f.author: Alois Lütolf
2ba2173aac927067a57549ea0efd8fe7ea5b963f.summary: At the mill in Brisecken, one mill hand after another mysteriously disappeared at night, so that the position acquired a bad reputation and no one wished to take it.

7d2f5640517345c44eafb207547fe61516a3ecd5.title: The Mine Devil
7d2f5640517345c44eafb207547fe61516a3ecd5.author: C. Kohlrusch
7d2f5640517345c44eafb207547fe61516a3ecd5.summary: Some time ago, a pious and learned man wrote to Lavater that in the Graubünden mountains there was a silver mine upon which the head of that place, Landammann Peter Buol, had spent great sums in recent years but from which he had gathered no small wealth.

87c4999507767d5fb4c99e23c8fe4a49fd12b5bd.title: The Mine on the Knapperkopf
87c4999507767d5fb4c99e23c8fe4a49fd12b5bd.author: Jakob Kuoni
87c4999507767d5fb4c99e23c8fe4a49fd12b5bd.summary: The gold veins on the Knapperkopf were discovered and secretly exploited by two brothers.

53f69d06627288ff5db6547ba86e72fedf9f5d02.title: The Miracle Doctor
53f69d06627288ff5db6547ba86e72fedf9f5d02.author: Hermann Hartmann
53f69d06627288ff5db6547ba86e72fedf9f5d02.summary: Near Grindelwald lived a little man known to the valley people only as the miracle doctor because of his arts.

4525bf90f629cf4c5fa1b4ccf9771030f5e34f98.title: The Miracle in the Grainfield
4525bf90f629cf4c5fa1b4ccf9771030f5e34f98.author: Dietrich Jecklin
4525bf90f629cf4c5fa1b4ccf9771030f5e34f98.summary: There in the path lies a lovely child,

2e7b6c995b294356661d01777f1320c2afd8ccd1.title: The Miracle of the Ring
2e7b6c995b294356661d01777f1320c2afd8ccd1.author: Alois Lütolf
2e7b6c995b294356661d01777f1320c2afd8ccd1.summary: Among the many votive tokens left by the faithful, one can see a ring hanging from a chain on the left in the center of the Maria Sonnenberg chapel on Seelisberg.

52935a5e4a421a7747143f62284b0dc9c3cbe89b.title: The Miracles of the Holy Night
52935a5e4a421a7747143f62284b0dc9c3cbe89b.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
52935a5e4a421a7747143f62284b0dc9c3cbe89b.summary: In Valais, people are also said once to have held it true that on Christmas night, while the clock strikes twelve and for as long as it continues striking, all livestock can speak human language.

692ab039d98b674a09ee5c0a887428ebd18ab873.title: The Miraculous Church
692ab039d98b674a09ee5c0a887428ebd18ab873.author: Hermann Hartmann
692ab039d98b674a09ee5c0a887428ebd18ab873.summary: High among the ice fields of the Bernese Oberland, in the middle of a glacier, there is a wondrous vault of ice that perfectly resembles the interior of a church.

81d40b1758e3b176d3951a3923988c122186d9ae.title: The Miraculous Image of Unterseen
81d40b1758e3b176d3951a3923988c122186d9ae.author: Hermann Hartmann
81d40b1758e3b176d3951a3923988c122186d9ae.summary: A magnificent painting depicting the Savior upon the cross once hung in the church at Unterseen and greatly adorned that house of God.

da3206d11866be0e4f47e9a6a9b23f0461b7a4ed.title: The Miraculous Lily from the Corpse
da3206d11866be0e4f47e9a6a9b23f0461b7a4ed.author: Alois Lütolf
da3206d11866be0e4f47e9a6a9b23f0461b7a4ed.summary: Around 1430, a strange event occurred in Hildisrieden.

cc8f17678b1c70ce93c188139823dac16529bb34.title: The Miraculous Ointment
cc8f17678b1c70ce93c188139823dac16529bb34.author: Jakob Kuoni
cc8f17678b1c70ce93c188139823dac16529bb34.summary: Old Fluri Manhart in the Fäsch at Flums was a widely renowned ‘doctor’ whose Kundsame extended across the Rhine as far as Tyrol.

31a61d0e3198c742fa5fb94b6fe7c97cc8009023.title: The Miraculous Rescue
31a61d0e3198c742fa5fb94b6fe7c97cc8009023.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
31a61d0e3198c742fa5fb94b6fe7c97cc8009023.summary: It is told of a priest in Törbel that he stole the church treasure.

45be78f020a1fea97ddf9ab297684cd2923beb38.title: The Miraculous Snow

1e37c9361924cd3374f68a6b6a6f502c382a4a1d.summary: Not long ago, Castelen Castle in the Aargau Jura was still a state estate productive in grain and wine.

97fbdf2c5345362930e898b015e940c41f03ad5d.title: The Schalbet Glacier

5a2040f358c4c4054e2264281c8a94a717140885.title: The Schatzjungfrau in Romooser-Enzi

5a2040f358c4c4054e2264281c8a94a717140885.summary: In Romoos in the Entlebuch, an old man told it to his sons, and I have it from one of them.

6ba740463555edcc6eb5054c183b2e83c027dbf3.title: The Schlachthäusi of Bern
