7a6a10455c9b6f232764626c31644416b3c959b4.summary: Near Strahlegg Castle, the hoof of a packhorse once happened to strike a gleaming gold coin from the earth, and the Säumer walking behind it found a considerable treasure there.

7964d51f4bd3af88b9d1a672c924fffb1747ce36.title: The Treasure of the Blüemlisalp
7964d51f4bd3af88b9d1a672c924fffb1747ce36.author: Josef Müller
7964d51f4bd3af88b9d1a672c924fffb1747ce36.summary: A little shepherd boy was tending sheep on the Blüemlisalp.

455d91f37fc331a71ecc193b7f65438d764eecab.title: The Treasure of the Church at Closters
455d91f37fc331a71ecc193b7f65438d764eecab.author: Dietrich Jecklin
455d91f37fc331a71ecc193b7f65438d764eecab.summary: It was around the end of the 18th century when a man who lived near the church in Closters came home late from work one evening.

8eb990f8b8f5ce0495d571b679edf69083d5acd5.title: The Treasure on Kaiserstock
8eb990f8b8f5ce0495d571b679edf69083d5acd5.author: Josef Müller
8eb990f8b8f5ce0495d571b679edf69083d5acd5.summary: a) The learned Uri Landammann Dr. K. Lusser recounts the following legend in a manuscript of 1833, published in Urner Wochenblatt 1921, no. 44:

d508994c0446e5e02644e6b91842d932b030558c.title: The Treasure on the Alp
d508994c0446e5e02644e6b91842d932b030558c.author: Josef Müller
d508994c0446e5e02644e6b91842d932b030558c.summary: A rich lord owned a large, beautiful Alp.

f2ab1e026acbb133e69c25c2ad83cb1a0a87fea1.title: The Treasure on the Flums Alp
f2ab1e026acbb133e69c25c2ad83cb1a0a87fea1.author: Jakob Kuoni
f2ab1e026acbb133e69c25c2ad83cb1a0a87fea1.summary: In olden times, a road is said to have led from Flums over the Flums Alp to Glarus, and where the herds of Flums now frolic in summer there stood a flourishing settlement.

8b51a539195471be4fc50764c441500443a9de54.title: The Treasure on the Linen Cloth
8b51a539195471be4fc50764c441500443a9de54.author: Josef Müller
8b51a539195471be4fc50764c441500443a9de54.summary: In one of the so-called charcoal gardens opposite Amsteg, which have now partly been converted into meadowland and bear their name because charcoal was formerly burned there, a treasure had lain buried since the time of the French.

697846cc30e7d38beb05e8befb21ea2e3acd197f.title: The Treasure on the Lungenstutz
697846cc30e7d38beb05e8befb21ea2e3acd197f.author: Josef Müller
697846cc30e7d38beb05e8befb21ea2e3acd197f.summary: a) According to the revelation of a fahrender Schüler, there are three gold mines on the upper Lungenstutz in the Maderanertal, near the place where the great wooden cross stood only a few decades ago.

b68f45d8d132673cb22e57b6330bf26e1d2b3dca.title: The Treasure on the Siwiboden
b68f45d8d132673cb22e57b6330bf26e1d2b3dca.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
b68f45d8d132673cb22e57b6330bf26e1d2b3dca.summary: The Siwiboden lies in the north of the Saas valley on the eastern mountainside.

875541637bc1f36cca41671b4c9d4c9a5d7e8efe.title: The Treasure Toad
875541637bc1f36cca41671b4c9d4c9a5d7e8efe.author: Alois Lütolf
875541637bc1f36cca41671b4c9d4c9a5d7e8efe.summary: At Hirnisbühl, near the notorious Galgenhölzli by Nebikon, Philip Lünz was once clearing land when his Karst struck a pot shaped like one of our bronze cooking pots.

0ef98d543a7db65343c6cb2d860c94428920fe03.title: The Treasure Toad in Kirchdorf
0ef98d543a7db65343c6cb2d860c94428920fe03.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
0ef98d543a7db65343c6cb2d860c94428920fe03.summary: A farmer from Kirchdorf in the Siggen Valley had suddenly become astonishingly rich without being able to give any clear reason for it, thereby arousing his neighbors' suspicion.

0ff773c91cd737d7eb047ac5d76fddf1b06d7391.title: The Treasure-Bringing Shot
0ff773c91cd737d7eb047ac5d76fddf1b06d7391.author: Alois Lütolf
0ff773c91cd737d7eb047ac5d76fddf1b06d7391.summary: A fahriger Schüler came to a hunter in Gurtnellen and said that he would go for a time to the Nidersee on the Leutschachalp, whereupon the lake would begin to roar tremendously.

384226e63ccf7813eccd9c25a272cb6c25c174ba.title: The Treasure-Guarding Dragon
384226e63ccf7813eccd9c25a272cb6c25c174ba.author: Alois Lütolf
384226e63ccf7813eccd9c25a272cb6c25c174ba.summary: On Tannen, a high and wild Alp in Obwalden belonging to the Kilcher of Kerns, there is a cave whose end no one has ever been able to reach.

95372c429cdbeac087a6395fe483230b89ed7cb7.title: The Treasure-Guarding Nun of Schönbrunn
95372c429cdbeac087a6395fe483230b89ed7cb7.author: Alois Lütolf
95372c429cdbeac087a6395fe483230b89ed7cb7.summary: A convent once stood on the “Chiteboden” below the chapel at Schönbrunn in the canton of Zug. Everything has now vanished, and only a legend has sunk its roots into this ground.

d887b5ca8af3e6c3f0bed845240d40c6bc7dfdf0.title: The Treasure-Guarding Toad near Laufenburg
d887b5ca8af3e6c3f0bed845240d40c6bc7dfdf0.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
d887b5ca8af3e6c3f0bed845240d40c6bc7dfdf0.summary: On the right bank of the Rhine between Laufenburg and Bünzgen, in the rocky valley of the Antlesbach, hammer works are said to have stood until the Thirty Years' War, and ruins of walls and slag in the ground still speak for it.

024089f9c9453243a8921306dbd491f57110fe91.title: The Treasure-Keeper of Fracstein
024089f9c9453243a8921306dbd491f57110fe91.author: Dietrich Jecklin
024089f9c9453243a8921306dbd491f57110fe91.summary: Not far from the Felsenbach, where a little road branches from the Prätigau highway toward Malans, a citizen of Malans was once walking along that road toward his home village on a dark evening.

81397d36c6d3a3cb7ff38d16ffd3d7ddb31c5137.title: The Tree Stump and the Witch
81397d36c6d3a3cb7ff38d16ffd3d7ddb31c5137.author: Josef Müller
81397d36c6d3a3cb7ff38d16ffd3d7ddb31c5137.summary: On an Alp in the Reuss valley, the cattle were never left in peace.

4321a9d375763bd547a7f5335392d76bd597b7a7.title: The Tree-Strong Riedbub
4321a9d375763bd547a7f5335392d76bd597b7a7.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
4321a9d375763bd547a7f5335392d76bd597b7a7.summary: A man at Ried had a son who was as healthy as a chamois and had cheeks as red as dry cherry leaves.

52d86720add81974f88f4c24a9d80fce945f579f.title: The Trostburg Castle Dog
52d86720add81974f88f4c24a9d80fce945f579f.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
52d86720add81974f88f4c24a9d80fce945f579f.summary: At every new moon, a black dog and a butcher appear in the ruins of Trostburg Castle, accompanied by loud clamor and shouting.

ac267d9c3091fa3d056cec0b8a91e98ee476d86f.title: The Trottengeist at Gebisdorf
ac267d9c3091fa3d056cec0b8a91e98ee476d86f.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
ac267d9c3091fa3d056cec0b8a91e98ee476d86f.summary: Between the villages of Gebisdorf and Birmensdorf, not far to the right of the Baden highway, stands the Gebisdorf Weintrotte in a meadow, an old, half-ruined building.

9033d9ffe61df5b9cb09a59c234305d209a23a3d.title: The Trottengeist in Frick
9033d9ffe61df5b9cb09a59c234305d209a23a3d.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
9033d9ffe61df5b9cb09a59c234305d209a23a3d.summary: In former times, no citizen dared press grapes at night in the Frick Gemeindstrotte.

ee4db8ebf2af0cbcc2b3a90c96792ff6e5004b5a.title: The Trottentier of Oberflachs
ee4db8ebf2af0cbcc2b3a90c96792ff6e5004b5a.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
ee4db8ebf2af0cbcc2b3a90c96792ff6e5004b5a.summary: The wine-rich village of Oberflachs has several Trotten, all of which stand deserted outside the autumn season except for one; for as long as the people of Oberflachs can remember, this one has always been inhabited by the Trottentier.

5345b2dcbc0f1e48d19f0361bd923d64337649e7.title: The Troublesome Little Pitcher
5345b2dcbc0f1e48d19f0361bd923d64337649e7.author: Meinrad Lienert
5345b2dcbc0f1e48d19f0361bd923d64337649e7.summary: On the ruins of the great Roman city of Vindonissa [Windisch] in Aargau, near today’s little town of prophets, Brugg, there once lived a holy hermit named Teutbert.

22047250906161d5fd9c423996226ae0a8824fd7.title: The Tränen-Tobel
22047250906161d5fd9c423996226ae0a8824fd7.author: Dietrich Jecklin
22047250906161d5fd9c423996226ae0a8824fd7.summary: Between the municipalities of Tersnaus and Camuns lies a steep, desolate Tobel called the Tränen-Tobel.

33fca10186b7b6509654290c6d57e37fef159997.title: The Turtmann Glacier in Valais
33fca10186b7b6509654290c6d57e37fef159997.author: Theodor Vernaleken
33fca10186b7b6509654290c6d57e37fef159997.summary: On the spot where the Turtmann Glacier now spreads its blue burdens of ice, there once lay the loveliest alp in the valley, called Blüemlisalp.

0c53f54b9624c3e6cfadf268098482ac0ebdabc7.title: The Tuutier
0c53f54b9624c3e6cfadf268098482ac0ebdabc7.author: Jakob Kuoni
0c53f54b9624c3e6cfadf268098482ac0ebdabc7.summary: It seems to me as though it were yesterday that old Nef, our neighbor, told us about the Tuutier.

c7969574be3316e32b0f20946335a2bff19be521.title: The Two Brothers
c7969574be3316e32b0f20946335a2bff19be521.author: M. Sooder
c7969574be3316e32b0f20946335a2bff19be521.summary: Two brothers once lived at Altburg who did not get along, as happens in a household where one pulls “hüscht” and the other “hott”—each in a different direction. Not a day passed when they did not quarrel and wrangle together.

7800f8fc12d3922e4cbd7d0febc1346bb6cf1aee.title: The Two Brothers and the Four Giants
7800f8fc12d3922e4cbd7d0febc1346bb6cf1aee.author: Dietrich Jecklin
7800f8fc12d3922e4cbd7d0febc1346bb6cf1aee.summary: Many hundreds of years ago, when giants still existed, there were once two brothers in Scarl.

516c16c38ff616b2973abdbf9673f854c1a1c2b4.title: The Two Friends
516c16c38ff616b2973abdbf9673f854c1a1c2b4.author: Dietrich Jecklin
516c16c38ff616b2973abdbf9673f854c1a1c2b4.summary: There once was a king who had two wondrously beautiful daughters.

e8a3666ca58a4ce8db2c725d0f91f559fce35da4.title: The Two Herders
e8a3666ca58a4ce8db2c725d0f91f559fce35da4.author: Otto Sutermeister
e8a3666ca58a4ce8db2c725d0f91f559fce35da4.summary: Once there were two herders who drove their herds onto unlike pastures.

7789e358737b8edee35538b428ecc4ede00ba46f.title: The Two Lights of Life
7789e358737b8edee35538b428ecc4ede00ba46f.author: Ernst L. Rochholz
7789e358737b8edee35538b428ecc4ede00ba46f.summary: Two bedside lights go out around the time an old woman dies. When messengers cross the region to fetch her sister, they discover the second death.

1b787b9aee86f258356d17548dba137201155157.title: The Two Old Men
1b787b9aee86f258356d17548dba137201155157.author: Josef Müller
1b787b9aee86f258356d17548dba137201155157.summary: At nightfall, a weary traveler reached a lonely hut.

333660841e624977bd9c7263e4c27e53c345e493.title: The Two Treasure Guardians
333660841e624977bd9c7263e4c27e53c345e493.author: Dietrich Jecklin
333660841e624977bd9c7263e4c27e53c345e493.summary: Near Ortenstein Castle, on the summit of a hill, in a quiet grove above a fearsome abyss, stands the Church of St.

85df3e1fc2c358a10fd9607f6b4dbe7ef25fe70c.title: The Two Wartburgs
85df3e1fc2c358a10fd9607f6b4dbe7ef25fe70c.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
85df3e1fc2c358a10fd9607f6b4dbe7ef25fe70c.summary: The two Wartburg castles in Aargau stand near the little town of Aarburg on two neighboring, graceful mountain peaks and can be seen from far away through the Winen and Aare valleys.

035407a62892eaa7befeeb5b538fd34d4ff56d4c.title: The Two Weather Witches in Meien
035407a62892eaa7befeeb5b538fd34d4ff56d4c.author: Josef Müller
035407a62892eaa7befeeb5b538fd34d4ff56d4c.summary: “Two of us half-grown girls were tending goats in the Meiental.

970f8aebb701a55edfbcfab1d0461debd4057a93.title: The Tyfelisieder
970f8aebb701a55edfbcfab1d0461debd4057a93.author: Josef Müller
970f8aebb701a55edfbcfab1d0461debd4057a93.summary: a) There was once a man who never had enough money.

e6fb1a99b41b6e06599a308be21dcb4b9c1adce3.title: The Tyrant at the Altburg
e6fb1a99b41b6e06599a308be21dcb4b9c1adce3.author: M. Sooder
e6fb1a99b41b6e06599a308be21dcb4b9c1adce3.summary: Legends must not be treated as historical sources, or only with caution.

94a3ae300cb06052e4e46dd1c35cef401ac5f04a.title: The Tyrant at the Schlössli
94a3ae300cb06052e4e46dd1c35cef401ac5f04a.author: M. Sooder
94a3ae300cb06052e4e46dd1c35cef401ac5f04a.summary: The lord in the Schlössli wished to force the farmers to build a leather bridge from the Schlössli to the Altburg. So that people would not know where he was, whenever he rode away he had his horse's shoes nailed on backward.

9f23d5e71aff937a5fd264e1f9b685ee74b650f1.title: The Täli-Giger
9f23d5e71aff937a5fd264e1f9b685ee74b650f1.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9f23d5e71aff937a5fd264e1f9b685ee74b650f1.summary: On the Tschiertschen Alp of Farur lies a little valley called the Täli.

73bd8c34a0e3120d48ba49b335ef40f72c572bb9.title: The Töberhund
73bd8c34a0e3120d48ba49b335ef40f72c572bb9.author: Jakob Kuoni
73bd8c34a0e3120d48ba49b335ef40f72c572bb9.summary: From the Töber to the Weinburg, the Töberhund can be seen at night, a most unwelcome companion that constantly moans and growls and looks about terribly with its fiery eyes.

6b6c64a14b2df531e41a97982a0948e1851f7d3f.title: The Töst on the Childberg near Brittnau
6b6c64a14b2df531e41a97982a0948e1851f7d3f.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
6b6c64a14b2df531e41a97982a0948e1851f7d3f.summary: The highest hill on the left side of the Aargau Wigger valley, situated between the villages of Brittnau and Strengelbach, is called the Childberg.

7089cf4dd9d3018d591e33b578bc13c9cef0cd60.title: The Türrlidokter
7089cf4dd9d3018d591e33b578bc13c9cef0cd60.author: Josef Müller
7089cf4dd9d3018d591e33b578bc13c9cef0cd60.summary: The Türrlidokter was a wonder-working physician in Unterwalden.[1] A man from Uri’s Isental from whom a thief had stolen a substantial quantity of meat once sought his help and asked him to show him the thief.

2f909f02a6e4251e50c45a29f6c028117540fecd.title: The Türst (Lienert)
2f909f02a6e4251e50c45a29f6c028117540fecd.author: Meinrad Lienert, Schweiz
2f909f02a6e4251e50c45a29f6c028117540fecd.summary: Lienert follows a proud hunter into the company of the Türst and the storm-driven supernatural hunt.

464626346ab047cfe9553afc7bbb8c954cfcd70a.title: The Türst (Lütolf)
464626346ab047cfe9553afc7bbb8c954cfcd70a.author: Alois Lütolf
464626346ab047cfe9553afc7bbb8c954cfcd70a.summary: Lütolf links the Türst and Sträggele to forbidden hunting, uncanny animals, and the dangers of their pursuit.

c59df335458afbc78cdf9fc2e067332322898f56.title: The Uncanny Fox in Bristen
c59df335458afbc78cdf9fc2e067332322898f56.author: Josef Müller
c59df335458afbc78cdf9fc2e067332322898f56.summary: Several people in Bristen—for this was only a few decades ago—saw a fox at night for a time in the Paradiesli and elsewhere around the church; it often came across as far as Frentschenberg.

09ffec7ee5db738db691b7692227d30feb467b85.title: The Uncanny Ox Butcher
09ffec7ee5db738db691b7692227d30feb467b85.author: Alois Lütolf
09ffec7ee5db738db691b7692227d30feb467b85.summary: It is often related of the Nachtvolk that they stopped in cattle sheds, cut meat from one head of cattle, and ate it, although afterward nothing could be noticed amiss with the animal—unless, through some clumsiness, a little bone had gone missing.

705c5948675cbdc5743bbb3d4d6157734c029bb9.title: The Uncanny Raven
705c5948675cbdc5743bbb3d4d6157734c029bb9.author: Josef Müller
705c5948675cbdc5743bbb3d4d6157734c029bb9.summary: A man from Schattdorf was reading from a book.

e5032da2daee774f6dd96c05cf62a90b23595509.title: The Uncanny Ride
e5032da2daee774f6dd96c05cf62a90b23595509.author: Dietrich Jecklin
e5032da2daee774f6dd96c05cf62a90b23595509.summary: Late one evening, a “Frohnfastenkind” was riding from the village of Grüsch toward his home at Malans.

3e760d0720077cd87cd8dba70de96d38fb8d6b3d.title: The Uncanny Rider
3e760d0720077cd87cd8dba70de96d38fb8d6b3d.author: Jakob Kuoni
3e760d0720077cd87cd8dba70de96d38fb8d6b3d.summary: A teamster from Diepoldsau often collected his last load from the quarry at Monstein late in the evening.

c3738505519e2131791eb91ead5b96648c4a810a.title: The Underground Passages
c3738505519e2131791eb91ead5b96648c4a810a.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
c3738505519e2131791eb91ead5b96648c4a810a.summary: People formerly spoke a great deal about underground passages.

0c0230f4079c838934dbd2a5af3049622e6f8e00.title: The Unfaithful Herdsman (Dialect)
0c0230f4079c838934dbd2a5af3049622e6f8e00.author: Jakob Kuoni
0c0230f4079c838934dbd2a5af3049622e6f8e00.summary: That same herdsman who, up on Tamunz, deliberately let a small herd of cattle plunge to its death must carry it up through the Boggries to the very top amid sighs and gasps, and then, with a shuddering laugh, let it roll back down again.

f7b3c3ea9e5ce34c6d87f1d9908820f073793314.title: The Unfaithful Maid of Laufenburg
f7b3c3ea9e5ce34c6d87f1d9908820f073793314.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
f7b3c3ea9e5ce34c6d87f1d9908820f073793314.summary: Long ago in Laufenburg, a hardworking maid served a wealthy widow.

014ae23276af543903ddc317a0669e021194c2e0.title: The Unfortunate Alpine Cauldron Thief
014ae23276af543903ddc317a0669e021194c2e0.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
014ae23276af543903ddc317a0669e021194c2e0.summary: Among the arts of magic and witchcraft, as the people generally believe, are also the skill and power of g'stellen, that is, holding thieves fast with the stolen goods until either the owner or the person who performed g'stellen releases them again.

cda30055fb57f0ad06c73bdcc41019ff9d89a62f.title: The Unfulfilled Dream (Kohlrusch)
cda30055fb57f0ad06c73bdcc41019ff9d89a62f.author: C. Kohlrusch
cda30055fb57f0ad06c73bdcc41019ff9d89a62f.summary: A woman’s recurring Good Friday dream leads her to treasure in a Laufenburg ruin, but doubt intervenes.

0f8bbb607399bc8ace4c2d1efa83f385feb3d96c.title: The Unfulfilled Dream (Rochholz)
0f8bbb607399bc8ace4c2d1efa83f385feb3d96c.author: Ernst L. Rochholz
0f8bbb607399bc8ace4c2d1efa83f385feb3d96c.summary: Rochholz connects a woman’s treasure dream with Laufenburg’s ruin and the religious obligations of its dead.

76ed6a61b553c3361e72a49aad5172c9fc0093eb.title: The Ungeheuerlein in the Plasselbschlund
76ed6a61b553c3361e72a49aad5172c9fc0093eb.author: C. Kohlrusch
76ed6a61b553c3361e72a49aad5172c9fc0093eb.summary: At that time, people also spoke of a spirit that occasionally made its presence known in the Plasselbschlund.

d6cb636113d0524e4320b0d87949f45f01194f6e.title: The Unholde on Scheidegg
d6cb636113d0524e4320b0d87949f45f01194f6e.author: Alois Lütolf
d6cb636113d0524e4320b0d87949f45f01194f6e.summary: Ask in Luthern for the shortest way to Sumiswald, and you will be told to go over Scheidegg. On the Alp there, you can refresh yourself with milk and butter.

0f0498570b98dfea956d56778dd835e6922fada4.title: The Unnatural Son
0f0498570b98dfea956d56778dd835e6922fada4.author: C. Kohlrusch
0f0498570b98dfea956d56778dd835e6922fada4.summary: A father’s final encounter with his son ends in punishment that continues among the glaciers.

cdef0dcafd049ba78706c62de54189c2e5649b50.title: The Uristier on the Reuss
cdef0dcafd049ba78706c62de54189c2e5649b50.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
cdef0dcafd049ba78706c62de54189c2e5649b50.summary: Along the upper course of the Reuss, shepherd boys drove goats into the mountains.

ff5735aaaf72b521db1c11360d37bb3e1881e44e.title: The Urtel
ff5735aaaf72b521db1c11360d37bb3e1881e44e.author: Jakob Kuoni
ff5735aaaf72b521db1c11360d37bb3e1881e44e.summary: Not far from the little town of Sargans, on the Rieter toward the railway station, lies a large spring hole called the Urtel.

5d934d94e44a36bc30b4209e52c1cbf0607b556f.title: The Uzystein in Monbiel
5d934d94e44a36bc30b4209e52c1cbf0607b556f.author: Theodor Vernaleken
5d934d94e44a36bc30b4209e52c1cbf0607b556f.summary: In Monbiel, a wildes Männlein likewise tended the household cows for years.

081fe8522cedac96e5c95b00dc40905f65cfad3c.title: The Valeis Dog
081fe8522cedac96e5c95b00dc40905f65cfad3c.author: C. Kohlrusch
081fe8522cedac96e5c95b00dc40905f65cfad3c.summary: At night, a large black dog can often be seen shambling through the streets of Mels with a rattling noise. It usually runs as far as the town hall, where it vanishes with a howl.

8a1df0157e937268762c0748e916179fff0f8ee4.title: The Valeishund
8a1df0157e937268762c0748e916179fff0f8ee4.author: Jakob Kuoni
8a1df0157e937268762c0748e916179fff0f8ee4.summary: For many years Vilters and Wangs were embroiled in a boundary dispute over pasture and forest in the Valeistobel.

74aa79c5feaac03a6d3474f887f3dca359f9b9c3.title: The Value of Innocence
74aa79c5feaac03a6d3474f887f3dca359f9b9c3.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
74aa79c5feaac03a6d3474f887f3dca359f9b9c3.summary: Devoutly believing people place a high value on the innocence of baptized children and readily attribute supernatural power to it.

0505155a7e6d16214ec7781f68e35baa8d557fde.title: The Vanished Duke
0505155a7e6d16214ec7781f68e35baa8d557fde.author: Meinrad Lienert
0505155a7e6d16214ec7781f68e35baa8d557fde.summary: On a hill between the villages of Grandson and Montagny, in the wine-rich land of Vaud, there stands amid somber fir trees an old oak said to have been planted by the Confederates when they defeated the Duke of Burgundy there.

5e148075c98de79962c3c3a2843ca40c1a3c867f.title: The Vanished Forest
5e148075c98de79962c3c3a2843ca40c1a3c867f.author: Theodor Vernaleken
5e148075c98de79962c3c3a2843ca40c1a3c867f.summary: In Thurgau, close to the Zürich border, lies Lake Bichelsee beside the village of the same name.

99b26fff77270da712161bb8d2ef505dcb825ccb.title: The Vanished Treasure at Castellum
99b26fff77270da712161bb8d2ef505dcb825ccb.author: Dietrich Jecklin
99b26fff77270da712161bb8d2ef505dcb825ccb.summary: There was a time when it was still customary for people to go about their business on high Charfreitag as on a weekday; a church service was indeed held, but afterward everyone was permitted to resume his work.

97e98e2875bd4254f0d970914d02c670327388ab.title: The Venediger
97e98e2875bd4254f0d970914d02c670327388ab.author: Josef Müller
97e98e2875bd4254f0d970914d02c670327388ab.summary: ‘In earlier times those Venediger used to travel about the country; they were fine, knowledgeable Mandli!’

3315416c02fa96258481916df09457dc642ccaa4.title: The Venediger in Glarus
3315416c02fa96258481916df09457dc642ccaa4.author: Theodor Vernaleken
3315416c02fa96258481916df09457dc642ccaa4.summary: In the Canton of Glarus, many stories are told about Fahrende Schüler who come from Venice to the Alps in a single night, fill a sack with stones, and return home just as quickly.

3400bf070f2919ebfcf5604c56d312d62cdb1d56.title: The Venediger in Sörenberg
3400bf070f2919ebfcf5604c56d312d62cdb1d56.author: Alois Lütolf
3400bf070f2919ebfcf5604c56d312d62cdb1d56.summary: Every year a Venediger appeared in Sörenberg at the sources of the Little Emme, which flows through the Entlebuch and is known to carry gold-bearing sand—for Venediger were found everywhere,

85ffe69f6c7328e88d913a4966b21fa50339845e.title: The Venediger in the Arni-Loch
85ffe69f6c7328e88d913a4966b21fa50339845e.author: Alois Lütolf
85ffe69f6c7328e88d913a4966b21fa50339845e.summary: a) In the middle of the Arni Alp above Engelberg lies the Arni-Loch, a cave.

febbe00167780c72972d234468a1b72490d3862f.title: The Venedigern on Casanna
febbe00167780c72972d234468a1b72490d3862f.author: Theodor Vernaleken
febbe00167780c72972d234468a1b72490d3862f.summary: On the Alp Casanna in the Prättigau, and in the area surrounding the Alp, the mountains contained much mineral wealth and especially veins of gold.

ba3eb7090c7370ad79a28d951d2034e50ad60914.title: The Venetian and the Man from Weisstannen
ba3eb7090c7370ad79a28d951d2034e50ad60914.author: C. Kohlrusch
ba3eb7090c7370ad79a28d951d2034e50ad60914.summary: At the time of the Milanese wars, a Venetian once entertained a young man from Weisstannen in the most splendid fashion.

9730480498b3016173dc97b95b5df627e42111b6.title: The Venetian and the Weisstanner
9730480498b3016173dc97b95b5df627e42111b6.author: Jakob Kuoni
9730480498b3016173dc97b95b5df627e42111b6.summary: During the Milanese wars, a Venetian once entertained a young Weisstanner with the finest food and drink.

f284259f2a62ab82c33cbac849eb9042a08dc89d.title: The Vengeful Beggar Woman
f284259f2a62ab82c33cbac849eb9042a08dc89d.author: Josef Müller
f284259f2a62ab82c33cbac849eb9042a08dc89d.summary: During the summer a Wybervölchli often came to Brunni and begged.

2eb4a90445992e00671bd9a64d5c67836b8f0804.title: The Verena Bath in the City of Baden
2eb4a90445992e00671bd9a64d5c67836b8f0804.author: Ernst L. Rochholz
2eb4a90445992e00671bd9a64d5c67836b8f0804.summary: A public bath in Baden serves people seeking relief, while a private ritual draws women hoping for a child. The collector follows the account with comparisons to other water legends.

bd097427923b8f173e8ac1740744e24e9c25ae69.title: The Viehrücken on the Alps
bd097427923b8f173e8ac1740744e24e9c25ae69.author: Jakob Kuoni
bd097427923b8f173e8ac1740744e24e9c25ae69.summary: Once the sixty or more cows of a Sente have been driven into the high-fenced and usually roofed Stofel, or milking place, the farmhands prepare to milk.

f44fe08a48704e08f28b8ad979ed9a8a74308194.title: The Village Beast in Suhr
f44fe08a48704e08f28b8ad979ed9a8a74308194.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
f44fe08a48704e08f28b8ad979ed9a8a74308194.summary: A young, merry shoemaker in Suhr owned a large glass bottle that lacked nothing but its bottom.

8e0bfa9e6074fa9a9265ccb37f3591299cecb017.title: The Village Calf of Auenstein
8e0bfa9e6074fa9a9265ccb37f3591299cecb017.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
8e0bfa9e6074fa9a9265ccb37f3591299cecb017.summary: One evening, the pastor of Auenstein and his wife were walking home from the village of Rupperswil.

8abea90a875e96cd12c891f50e8c5bfd20ddab1a.title: The Village Dog at Mägden
8abea90a875e96cd12c891f50e8c5bfd20ddab1a.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
8abea90a875e96cd12c891f50e8c5bfd20ddab1a.summary: From the village fountain known as the Schwefelbrunnen, the Obwasser formerly ran down a roadside ditch into the village brook flowing from Winterfingen.

a7506a0d714cbc780794b2a48958663fad29d31a.title: The Village Dog in Muri
a7506a0d714cbc780794b2a48958663fad29d31a.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
a7506a0d714cbc780794b2a48958663fad29d31a.summary: Muri-Langdorf is divided into Oberdorf, Mitteldorf, and Unterdorf—the upper, middle, and lower village districts.

92c23b1f7078839fe93000275ff4e960a2af868c.title: The Village of Hospental
92c23b1f7078839fe93000275ff4e960a2af868c.author: Josef Müller
92c23b1f7078839fe93000275ff4e960a2af868c.summary: The village of Hospental is said to have stood in ancient times on the other bank of the Reuss, at ‘Tendlen.’ From there, the pack trail climbed toward the Bätz and then descended through the Brigg forest.

22b070a4f30fa4ee1214df2a3dc21232ad85bcd7.title: The Village on the Theodul Plain
22b070a4f30fa4ee1214df2a3dc21232ad85bcd7.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen

e8d62cb36d6d1bf4820bf45a48c7df8c8cc0b4f2.title: The Village Pig
e8d62cb36d6d1bf4820bf45a48c7df8c8cc0b4f2.author: Jakob Kuoni
e8d62cb36d6d1bf4820bf45a48c7df8c8cc0b4f2.summary: The Stubetiknaben in particular have tales to tell of this creature.

d98da1600002280f5f0c32668155accf9e919951.title: The Village Poodle in Wettingen
d98da1600002280f5f0c32668155accf9e919951.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
d98da1600002280f5f0c32668155accf9e919951.summary: Herrengässli is the name given to that part of the village of Wettingen in which the monastic clergy of the nearby Wettingen Stift owned several houses.

f2d8013f9ea83e8a814b461b980b888e180c163d.title: The Vogeldürscht above the Schmiedwald
f2d8013f9ea83e8a814b461b980b888e180c163d.author: M. Sooder
f2d8013f9ea83e8a814b461b980b888e180c163d.summary: Once the Bammert in the Schmiedwald heard the Vogeldürscht; he looked up and saw it circling in the air.

c109ee2d1a0a74260a8a8d9ea5ff314f9902d9e7.title: The Voice from the Avalanche
c109ee2d1a0a74260a8a8d9ea5ff314f9902d9e7.author: Josef Müller
c109ee2d1a0a74260a8a8d9ea5ff314f9902d9e7.summary: When, about 50–60 years ago, the avalanche swept out over the house at Blüemlismatt during the night, a voice was heard crying: ‘Hinecht chumi-n-i und nah hundert Jahrä chumi-n-i wider’—‘Tonight I am coming, and after a hundred years I shall come again.’

eea5853c86bca94e68fbcfc14153eed343e76ef6.title: The Voracious Wolf
eea5853c86bca94e68fbcfc14153eed343e76ef6.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
eea5853c86bca94e68fbcfc14153eed343e76ef6.summary: Among many others, the following legend shows how far belief in witchcraft, when it was in full bloom, could climb into foolishness and absurdity:

5a95a7ff88eb31e52b22f9bb2666a0ea6a62a79b.title: The Vow
5a95a7ff88eb31e52b22f9bb2666a0ea6a62a79b.author: Josef Müller
5a95a7ff88eb31e52b22f9bb2666a0ea6a62a79b.summary: Below the Schweigacher at Unterschächen, a traveler was overtaken by a terrible earthquake.

33d55a9b73776a3debf10ee82988cdba5de9d169.title: The Vättnerbergers Learn to Fell Timber (Dialect)
33d55a9b73776a3debf10ee82988cdba5de9d169.author: Jakob Kuoni
33d55a9b73776a3debf10ee82988cdba5de9d169.summary: The wilda Mannli were much wiser than other people in many matters, and the Vättnerbergers learned a great deal from them, including how to fell timber.

42bc96822c3a7973fb617cab183d5ff13f6ab776.title: The Wachletä-Jumpfere Near Magden
42bc96822c3a7973fb617cab183d5ff13f6ab776.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
42bc96822c3a7973fb617cab183d5ff13f6ab776.summary: During those long famine years of the Swedish War, the Rhine region of Aargau suffered unspeakably.

447770607e2dcb39e541e39244f88eb79ee92f14.title: The Wager
447770607e2dcb39e541e39244f88eb79ee92f14.author: Jakob Kuoni
447770607e2dcb39e541e39244f88eb79ee92f14.summary: Late one evening, guests were still sitting together in a village inn, entertaining one another with ghost stories.

e98203364f5458f8e962d72825f523bfeeb6dbbf.title: The Wagon of the Wild Host
e98203364f5458f8e962d72825f523bfeeb6dbbf.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
e98203364f5458f8e962d72825f523bfeeb6dbbf.summary: Higher deities are imagined traveling in vehicles; even their riding is still understood by our dialect as a mere Fahrt, or vehicular journey, just as the older language called the two- and four-horse wagon reita and the driver reitweko.

5827d558095bca28b992bb7ff2956a127d4c08cc.title: The Wagon with Four Schimmel
5827d558095bca28b992bb7ff2956a127d4c08cc.author: Theodor Vernaleken
5827d558095bca28b992bb7ff2956a127d4c08cc.summary: About a quarter of an hour from Rohrbach, near Huttwil in the canton of Bern, there still stands the ruin of a former castle called the Old Castle.

82337f53097f499ea1de34270e23e45b09c0eceb.title: The Walchwil Dwarfs and the Pork
82337f53097f499ea1de34270e23e45b09c0eceb.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
82337f53097f499ea1de34270e23e45b09c0eceb.summary: In the rocks and crags of the Almende belonging to the little Zug village of Walchwil, the Bergmandli once lived.

1c27c4990315f779d4e0fe9864ef8e7de4161d64.title: The Waldbruder and Sorcerer in Getschwyler
1c27c4990315f779d4e0fe9864ef8e7de4161d64.author: Josef Müller
1c27c4990315f779d4e0fe9864ef8e7de4161d64.summary: In the “Espen,” a small patch of Allmend meadowland near the Getschwyler chapel in the municipality of Spiringen, forest hermits formerly lived.

ad077def8e8a214e0ce9c1adf4f5f39ecda69f13.title: The Waldbruder on Felliberg
ad077def8e8a214e0ce9c1adf4f5f39ecda69f13.author: Josef Müller
ad077def8e8a214e0ce9c1adf4f5f39ecda69f13.summary: In the Fellibergen, in the municipality of Gurtnellen, stands the Waldbruderchäppeli.

b3435372e7fc6d5a28530f7987242ce56a0deeef.title: The Waldfenka of Churwalden
b3435372e7fc6d5a28530f7987242ce56a0deeef.author: Theodor Vernaleken
b3435372e7fc6d5a28530f7987242ce56a0deeef.summary: The Bergleutlein, neither males nor females, have ever done anyone any harm unless they were provoked to the utmost and most sensitive degree.

fc3bdd5816246bb475d996cae7aeab16591fb9a6.title: The Wandelzeit
fc3bdd5816246bb475d996cae7aeab16591fb9a6.author: Alois Lütolf
fc3bdd5816246bb475d996cae7aeab16591fb9a6.summary: Anyone who dies a violent death must ‘wander’ as a spirit after death until the number of years that person would otherwise have lived is complete.

debc24312a6e65000d5349cb30947991f78811ec.title: The Wanderbotze
debc24312a6e65000d5349cb30947991f78811ec.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
debc24312a6e65000d5349cb30947991f78811ec.summary: In the Stockwald near Birgisch, parish of Naters, people tell of a Botzen (spirit) that is said often to have been seen and heard.

fdd65b465d701864416092e6542ee12c0cf1f5f1.title: The Wandering Human Skull
fdd65b465d701864416092e6542ee12c0cf1f5f1.author: Alois Lütolf
fdd65b465d701864416092e6542ee12c0cf1f5f1.summary: Since ancient times, three human skulls have been kept in the chapel at Gerligen, a small village between Ballwil and Eschenbach. They are said to be the skulls of three murderers who met their deaths there.

ec81af2b77dda8d93916b640023c2dad3d0fa3b1.title: The Wandering Image
ec81af2b77dda8d93916b640023c2dad3d0fa3b1.author: Alois Lütolf
ec81af2b77dda8d93916b640023c2dad3d0fa3b1.summary: A large male figure is painted on the wall of a house in Lungern. When the bells ring at three o'clock in the afternoon on Good Friday to mark the death of Jesus, this man goes to the church fountain to drink water.

b882fdfca0142da09f0caed20c131e5b54f65358.title: The Wandering Jew (Andwil, SG)
b882fdfca0142da09f0caed20c131e5b54f65358.author: Jakob Kuoni
b882fdfca0142da09f0caed20c131e5b54f65358.summary: In the municipalities of Andwil and Gaiserwald, the ewige Jude, or Wandering Jew, once appeared as a stone-old little man in torn clothing.

378eab0a5cf1e8d8c6609133fc144b2346f48f11.title: The Wandering Jew (Savien, GR)
378eab0a5cf1e8d8c6609133fc144b2346f48f11.author: Dietrich Jecklin
378eab0a5cf1e8d8c6609133fc144b2346f48f11.summary: A restless being, half man and half ghost, came one day, when it was raining terribly, to the Platz (Savien) and was hospitably invited into a house there.

5f51bf3fd5685688f0f23a8c3ff669c7cfaabd0c.title: The Wandering Jew on the Theodul Pass
5f51bf3fd5685688f0f23a8c3ff669c7cfaabd0c.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
5f51bf3fd5685688f0f23a8c3ff669c7cfaabd0c.summary: Between Monte Rosa and the Matterhorn lies a mighty glacier called the Augsttalgletscher, or Theodul Pass.

11983aad3e8e64eec4ff32f1805f579375e280ed.title: The Wandering Night Light
11983aad3e8e64eec4ff32f1805f579375e280ed.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
11983aad3e8e64eec4ff32f1805f579375e280ed.summary: "I am an old man," an elderly man in Törbel once told me.

c49be768017ac02b8d9f2f53696a6b09bbc442c9.title: The Wandering Rathsherren of Muri
c49be768017ac02b8d9f2f53696a6b09bbc442c9.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
c49be768017ac02b8d9f2f53696a6b09bbc442c9.summary: “Be quiet, the gentlemen are walking about!” was formerly a common saying throughout the country when one wished to call someone who spoke too suggestively to a more respectful tone. (Melch. Kirchhofer, Schweiz. Sprichw. No. 79.)

9b7b6b8f0ba7294461de277d857a09515712f162.title: The Wandering Scholar on Alpe Casana
9b7b6b8f0ba7294461de277d857a09515712f162.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9b7b6b8f0ba7294461de277d857a09515712f162.summary: Near Serneus stands an old, ruined house called the “Gmür” (masonry).

9080126276cef3af14543a194866f626e50e4996.title: The Wandering Scholar on Pa d’Aur
9080126276cef3af14543a194866f626e50e4996.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9080126276cef3af14543a194866f626e50e4996.summary: Just as the Venediger, or fahrende Schüler, roamed through most Alpine regions and by means of their art found and gathered treasures unknown to the inhabitants of the land, they also discovered in the mountains above Trimmis a spring of liquid gold.

7a330416b9830dc534780dbd4fad743361d5e7f4.title: The Wandering Scholars
7a330416b9830dc534780dbd4fad743361d5e7f4.author: Josef Müller
7a330416b9830dc534780dbd4fad743361d5e7f4.summary: The fahrenden Schüler were recognized by the fact that, when they walked along the road, they constantly twirled their hooked staffs in circles before them with their right hands.

3b6f3621f7e5cb8287fc6fc4f67017384c36dc80.title: The Wandering Scholar’s Apprentice
3b6f3621f7e5cb8287fc6fc4f67017384c36dc80.author: Josef Müller
3b6f3621f7e5cb8287fc6fc4f67017384c36dc80.summary: A man wanted to become a fahrender Schüler and said so to one who already was one.

f405b931cf425488ff0e5e09aace8fc4a7674d08.title: The Wandering Traitors
f405b931cf425488ff0e5e09aace8fc4a7674d08.author: Alois Lütolf
f405b931cf425488ff0e5e09aace8fc4a7674d08.summary: The hamlet of Deinikon in the Zug municipality of Baar is the place where, in 1531, peace was negotiated and concluded between the Reformed and the five old Catholic cantons.

01a55c77168856f58f213eb8f91133f5da099b72.title: The Wanzenschneider of Obermumpf
01a55c77168856f58f213eb8f91133f5da099b72.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
01a55c77168856f58f213eb8f91133f5da099b72.summary: The fields between Schupfart and Obermumpf, two neighboring Fricktal villages, are broad, rising hillside farms.

be32f25df6f07b733769c369be11f80fde9758a4.title: The War of the Bees
be32f25df6f07b733769c369be11f80fde9758a4.author: Josef Müller
be32f25df6f07b733769c369be11f80fde9758a4.summary: In one war, bees were loosed upon the enemy, and in this way the battle was won. That is why it is called the War of the Bees.

5bbee55583e7b1c2e29bf425a35410ac9cd3a92f.title: The Warning
5bbee55583e7b1c2e29bf425a35410ac9cd3a92f.author: Jakob Kuoni
5bbee55583e7b1c2e29bf425a35410ac9cd3a92f.summary: In the lower part of the Malun Alp spreads the beautiful Dreierwald.

58684e10736111f6ca830ce7bfde7b0d46c900fe.title: The Warning of the Erdmännchen
58684e10736111f6ca830ce7bfde7b0d46c900fe.author: C. Kohlrusch
58684e10736111f6ca830ce7bfde7b0d46c900fe.summary: Not far from Lake Thun, behind the Ralligen vineyard, lies the place called the Einöde.

44a61e9f3e70c0191fc9d6f60d596e65fc614fa8.title: The Washerwoman (Waldkirch, SG)
44a61e9f3e70c0191fc9d6f60d596e65fc614fa8.author: Jakob Kuoni
44a61e9f3e70c0191fc9d6f60d596e65fc614fa8.summary: In the Heldtobel, not far from Waldkirch toward Bernhardzell, where a path formerly crossed the brook, a young, slender washerwoman once washed and “flatterte” with desperate intensity whenever people passed by.

2d074398cb27933b05be9b67f6134563119e6f33.title: The Washerwoman (Walenstadt, St. Gallen)
2d074398cb27933b05be9b67f6134563119e6f33.author: Jakob Kuoni
2d074398cb27933b05be9b67f6134563119e6f33.summary: Between the now-abandoned footbridge that crossed the Alpbach — the path now runs much farther up into the alp — and the waterfall spraying farther above, an old woman sometimes does her washing with the most industrious activity on…

e339f72b850a3556d3d85528a66d7af5eed5dfe6.title: The Washerwoman (Wildhaus, St. Gallen)
e339f72b850a3556d3d85528a66d7af5eed5dfe6.author: Jakob Kuoni
e339f72b850a3556d3d85528a66d7af5eed5dfe6.summary: Near Lisighaus, a little white-clad woman could be seen at night washing at a fountain. Dr. Henne-Am Rhyn, Deutsche Volkssage.

9ac4738c0f4cf0e5b24aaf8e39d5a4e152addcce.title: The Washerwoman at the Frenkenbach
9ac4738c0f4cf0e5b24aaf8e39d5a4e152addcce.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
9ac4738c0f4cf0e5b24aaf8e39d5a4e152addcce.summary: At the first bridge over the Frenkenbach in the Reigoldswil valley of Basel-Landschaft lies a wooded hill. This is the place where, whenever the moon is full, a woman washes clothes throughout the night.

989505c234f2d8965e03d5ece6a8a2540566d2ce.title: The Wasserfrauen of the Troglosen
989505c234f2d8965e03d5ece6a8a2540566d2ce.author: Meinrad Lienert
989505c234f2d8965e03d5ece6a8a2540566d2ce.summary: It was after the Feast of the Assumption when a little farm boy from the village of Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz set out to make his way home to his remote little village of Untersyten.
