d298f7e36aaa4d563f565b73f30bc7685efc1a13.summary: It was in gray antiquity when a courageous rider wished to travel from the Bernese country across into Valais.

8b9c418748e88a7799692fca127b1f7089a21be0.title: The White Rider on the Längwäg
8b9c418748e88a7799692fca127b1f7089a21be0.author: M. Sooder
8b9c418748e88a7799692fca127b1f7089a21be0.summary: At night, a wisse Riter on a white horse sometimes gallops up through the Längwäg. He comes from near the Galgelöli and goes as far as Dorniggütsch. He has met many a person at night.

8fa616ce80160da92c3c904790db56feedd4dee2.title: The White Spirit
8fa616ce80160da92c3c904790db56feedd4dee2.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
8fa616ce80160da92c3c904790db56feedd4dee2.summary: In the Eisten near Stalden, on the eastern side of the valley, a laboriously and boldly constructed Wasserleite carries the water of the Vispa for well over one and a half hours to irrigate the meadows of Staldenried.

4dfead81a272e2d57867dbf759aebf5b5d3f7b0c.title: The White Witch
4dfead81a272e2d57867dbf759aebf5b5d3f7b0c.author: Dietrich Jecklin
4dfead81a272e2d57867dbf759aebf5b5d3f7b0c.summary: It was late one evening when the men of the village of Peist left the municipal assembly.

f344e813da68fbc863f085da1746ef44594fb2a4.title: The White Woman at Obersaxen
f344e813da68fbc863f085da1746ef44594fb2a4.author: Dietrich Jecklin
f344e813da68fbc863f085da1746ef44594fb2a4.summary: A poor man who was walking home from Mayerhof to St.

dbf0fa72d5954c4e00068b4f52a1cdf0545fce18.title: The White Woman at Ringgenberg Bridge
dbf0fa72d5954c4e00068b4f52a1cdf0545fce18.author: Dietrich Jecklin
dbf0fa72d5954c4e00068b4f52a1cdf0545fce18.summary: At Ringgenberg Bridge, on high festivals and holy days in the still early morning, a girl of almost unearthly beauty appears to children tending goats.

7c965a49bb407d2cb5bf4af3a48118d9e3fc1e11.title: The White Woman in Zurzach
7c965a49bb407d2cb5bf4af3a48118d9e3fc1e11.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
7c965a49bb407d2cb5bf4af3a48118d9e3fc1e11.summary: Almost in the middle of the little town of Zurzach stands a house called the weisse Rössli.

94a12b4562a00b3b48b12b6498a95c8efab97332.title: The White Woman of Leissigen
94a12b4562a00b3b48b12b6498a95c8efab97332.author: Hermann Hartmann
94a12b4562a00b3b48b12b6498a95c8efab97332.summary: In ancient times, a substantial city with walls, towers, and a lordly castle stood upon the Stoffelberg near Leissigen.

0d183e4003ab248eb0c5b711c7975d3e9b3b1209.title: The White Woman without a Nose
0d183e4003ab248eb0c5b711c7975d3e9b3b1209.author: Theodor Vernaleken
0d183e4003ab248eb0c5b711c7975d3e9b3b1209.summary: When one travels from the lonely, quiet Münster Valley over the Ofen Pass toward the Engadin, one must cover a six-hour journey and encounters only a single house.

9db9af61a33afb546fbb6e4c203bd3b9bd71e457.title: The White Woman — Frutigen
9db9af61a33afb546fbb6e4c203bd3b9bd71e457.author: Hermann Hartmann
9db9af61a33afb546fbb6e4c203bd3b9bd71e457.summary: At the far end of the valley floor of Frutigen, between Öschinen and the Breithorn, rises more than 11000 Fuss high the Frau, or White Woman, whose summit is covered with a mantle of eternal snow.

be9bb3b19ba74a5ceb299afc583a208117010b62.title: The White-Clad Avenging Spirit on Schwanau
be9bb3b19ba74a5ceb299afc583a208117010b62.author: Alois Lütolf
be9bb3b19ba74a5ceb299afc583a208117010b62.summary: As is well known, the ‘weisse Buch’ at Sarnen is among the earliest chronicles of central Switzerland and dates from the second half of the fifteenth century.

4e0913524208a86c9ab492959ce388109d9f89d0.title: The White-Fir Name
4e0913524208a86c9ab492959ce388109d9f89d0.author: Jakob Kuoni
4e0913524208a86c9ab492959ce388109d9f89d0.summary: A mighty Weisstanne is said to have stood upon the site where the village church now stands before its foundation stone was laid; hence the name of the village and valley.

6ee8ff0a0cf4251da77827eb5c949edfd1519d11.title: The White-Horse Knight of Liestal
6ee8ff0a0cf4251da77827eb5c949edfd1519d11.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
6ee8ff0a0cf4251da77827eb5c949edfd1519d11.summary: The high ridge between Arisdorf and Liestal is called the Scheuerhalde.

6c1d9c3c8ece5aed194c705003891811e915889f.title: The White-Horse Rider at Stein am Rhein
6c1d9c3c8ece5aed194c705003891811e915889f.author: Theodor Vernaleken
6c1d9c3c8ece5aed194c705003891811e915889f.summary: At Stein am Rhein, on stormy nights, one sometimes hears a rider on a white horse descend from Hohenklingen Castle, gallop onto the Rhine bridge, and from its middle plunge into the waters of the Rhine.

712ce65e1a372abbcf230b556cb1f3805561ec11.title: The White-Horse Treasure Wagon
712ce65e1a372abbcf230b556cb1f3805561ec11.author: Theodor Vernaleken
712ce65e1a372abbcf230b556cb1f3805561ec11.summary: Near the small Gerzensee between Thun and Bern lived a rich farmer who was very avaricious.

385e94a6a817b5974185ee93f2913e21a3ab6998.title: The Wicked Mother
385e94a6a817b5974185ee93f2913e21a3ab6998.author: C. Kohlrusch
385e94a6a817b5974185ee93f2913e21a3ab6998.summary: A man from Matt in the Sernft Valley had two boys by his first wife.

4adec86c7af5b7f6b84388d7526f8d74207b838e.title: The Wicked Mother and the Kind Büebli
4adec86c7af5b7f6b84388d7526f8d74207b838e.author: Otto Sutermeister
4adec86c7af5b7f6b84388d7526f8d74207b838e.summary: There was once a mother and a little boy living alone in a small house.

03fddd24da65160587a422603a4ca84f87f49f9a.title: The Wicked Senne
03fddd24da65160587a422603a4ca84f87f49f9a.author: Johannes Jegerlehner
03fddd24da65160587a422603a4ca84f87f49f9a.summary: High in the Nanzertal lies a small but beautiful Alp that is still counted among the best in the Vispertal.

ef648a0e5c0b5c0cb67462daf53602978f491ecc.title: The Wicked Stepmother
ef648a0e5c0b5c0cb67462daf53602978f491ecc.author: Walter Keller
ef648a0e5c0b5c0cb67462daf53602978f491ecc.summary: There was once a stepmother who had two daughters.

fa7eceb5b3edbbe8eaa75417da68fbb0c8f47c5c.title: The Widow's Bread and Butter
fa7eceb5b3edbbe8eaa75417da68fbb0c8f47c5c.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
fa7eceb5b3edbbe8eaa75417da68fbb0c8f47c5c.summary: Below Sins, Rüssegg Castle once stood on the Reuss.

5923dab8711fffa17738e5fbd4a76cf8db3780f3.title: The Wiggle (Tawny Owl)
5923dab8711fffa17738e5fbd4a76cf8db3780f3.author: Josef Müller
5923dab8711fffa17738e5fbd4a76cf8db3780f3.summary: Not very long ago in Erstfeld, several young men were making merry in the house of two strikingly pretty, young, perfectly healthy girls.

0abbaf26c8cf53d301975954250d2dff7f61d260.title: The Wild Bull at Schwarzsee
0abbaf26c8cf53d301975954250d2dff7f61d260.author: Jakob Kuoni
0abbaf26c8cf53d301975954250d2dff7f61d260.summary: When the people of Wangs repaired the alpine fence before the Alpfahrt to their Gamidaur pasture, an unknown but vigorous-looking man came to them and offered to perform the duties of a Senn during the coming summer without pay or complaint.

10459ea8b6ccf358ed8a6036497b3edd3fe83582.title: The Wild Cowherd
10459ea8b6ccf358ed8a6036497b3edd3fe83582.author: Dietrich Jecklin
10459ea8b6ccf358ed8a6036497b3edd3fe83582.summary: For many summers in succession, a Fänggenmannli tended the Heimkühe at Conters without ever accepting any reward.

bf95ef48b08b99aa523ba8775ce365e43de7c3f5.title: The Wild Host (H. Hartmann)
bf95ef48b08b99aa523ba8775ce365e43de7c3f5.author: Hermann Hartmann
bf95ef48b08b99aa523ba8775ce365e43de7c3f5.summary: On dark, stormy nights, a ghostly procession called the wildes Heer often passes through the valleys and over the heights of our land.

c940dbf277c1349c0e69715e2b3a33d82d30c6da.title: The Wild Host near Egliswil
c940dbf277c1349c0e69715e2b3a33d82d30c6da.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
c940dbf277c1349c0e69715e2b3a33d82d30c6da.summary: At the Stöckhof near Egliswil, the farmer lodged a Capuchin friar making his appointed begging rounds and was still chatting with him before bedtime when a distant din announced the Wildes Heer.

d376476143ec90231cc27d7d5ec00d6208bbe2aa.title: The Wild Host of Grandvillars
d376476143ec90231cc27d7d5ec00d6208bbe2aa.author: Theodor Vernaleken
d376476143ec90231cc27d7d5ec00d6208bbe2aa.summary: In the southern part of the canton of Fribourg, the Taunabach flows through a landscape of mountains and valleys that several hundred years ago was the haunt of a wild hunter who carried on his restless activity every Saturday…

0d70f7bc1d65c9066db8f571ca2692b4e43785d9.title: The Wild Hunt
0d70f7bc1d65c9066db8f571ca2692b4e43785d9.author: M. Sooder
0d70f7bc1d65c9066db8f571ca2692b4e43785d9.summary: Between Christmas and New Year, a roaring hunt passes through the countryside. The accompanying commentary connects the host with the storm.

a3b936abd2e2c7999400da015105f7fbec5603c4.title: The Wild Hunt around Zofingen and Brittnau
a3b936abd2e2c7999400da015105f7fbec5603c4.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
a3b936abd2e2c7999400da015105f7fbec5603c4.summary: Centuries ago, a hunter ranged the woods around Zofingen and Brittnau.

3d5d9bd604d0029a339f7fa189cf2c6830d6a288.title: The Wild Hunt by the Altburg
3d5d9bd604d0029a339f7fa189cf2c6830d6a288.author: M. Sooder
3d5d9bd604d0029a339f7fa189cf2c6830d6a288.summary: At an uncanny hour, a Bammert heard trees being felled and wood dragged in the Lohäule. He went back there, but everything was silent, and he saw nothing. So he returned and thought he must have heard incorrectly.

551c18fae1379d54a846cc727efd37df942da920.title: The Wild Hunt on the Fuhrebärg
551c18fae1379d54a846cc727efd37df942da920.author: M. Sooder
551c18fae1379d54a846cc727efd37df942da920.summary: In the Fuhrebärg, things were not always clean and peaceful.

3368682a77e7586d6581b01d6349a6824193673b.title: The Wild Hunt on the Schwendelberg
3368682a77e7586d6581b01d6349a6824193673b.author: J. J. Jakob
3368682a77e7586d6581b01d6349a6824193673b.summary: ‘Do you hear how it howls toward the Guggershorn?

a1520f5df4bf08f5ead85a649ec6141676f33238.title: The Wild Hunter in the Wigger Valley
a1520f5df4bf08f5ead85a649ec6141676f33238.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
a1520f5df4bf08f5ead85a649ec6141676f33238.summary: Near the town of Zofingen, a hill in the Finkenhard forest is called Schloss Finkenstein.

ba1238d3eb3e929d9b9c5608ff12e466d8873d4e.title: The Wild Hunter, or the Thürst
ba1238d3eb3e929d9b9c5608ff12e466d8873d4e.author: J. J. Jakob
ba1238d3eb3e929d9b9c5608ff12e466d8873d4e.summary: A farmer and miller in that vicinity once allowed one of his farmhands to go home to his family in the evening.

344b55a9df23bf2efb36fb7725c58178939f1cd8.title: The Wild Huntsman
344b55a9df23bf2efb36fb7725c58178939f1cd8.author: M. Sooder
344b55a9df23bf2efb36fb7725c58178939f1cd8.summary: In former times people always heard the Wild Huntsman as he hunted from Altburg over the Chaserebärg toward Chaschteler.

d141581622efd7d70ee1126974acf71e450c5f23.title: The Wild Huntsman on the Scheidegg
d141581622efd7d70ee1126974acf71e450c5f23.author: Hermann Hartmann
d141581622efd7d70ee1126974acf71e450c5f23.summary: In the mountains of Grindelwald, a strange call is often heard around midnight.

07e24241f4fa674a4db6be85a25043ada7782a1a.title: The Wild Huntsman Punishes a Horse Abuser
07e24241f4fa674a4db6be85a25043ada7782a1a.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
07e24241f4fa674a4db6be85a25043ada7782a1a.summary: Who could forget the road from Zurzach to Kaiserstuhl, the way it formerly went uphill and downhill as though from heaven into hell?

07163ddf40d96853faa165abd833949711af149b.title: The Wild Lake
07163ddf40d96853faa165abd833949711af149b.author: Jakob Kuoni
07163ddf40d96853faa165abd833949711af149b.summary: Above Vilters lies the Wild Lake. If stones are thrown into it, it begins to rage, and storms and severe thunderstorms arise.

2eba115142c274d795e65b70e556f5a3cd124024.title: The Wild Little Man Making Cheese
2eba115142c274d795e65b70e556f5a3cd124024.author: Theodor Vernaleken
2eba115142c274d795e65b70e556f5a3cd124024.summary: On an Alp, a wild little man lived on fairly familiar terms with the Senn and received from him many things that gave him pleasure; in return, he was very devoted to the Senn.

3b3bdbe232f8b83d0f55d5676704dee76c161acc.title: The Wild Mannli near Lüen
3b3bdbe232f8b83d0f55d5676704dee76c161acc.author: Dietrich Jecklin
3b3bdbe232f8b83d0f55d5676704dee76c161acc.summary: In the so-called Glassauer Forest there were once many wilde Lütli.

97777949cce1f4c7291cc74bd6b4716951907ab3.title: The Wild Mannli Outwitted
97777949cce1f4c7291cc74bd6b4716951907ab3.author: Dietrich Jecklin
97777949cce1f4c7291cc74bd6b4716951907ab3.summary: A man from Klosters had lost his newborn baby, and an ugly changeling had been laid in the cradle in its place.

88e1d52ccc579e502f8ae23b6330338279d53758.title: The Wild Männlein among the Woodcutters
88e1d52ccc579e502f8ae23b6330338279d53758.author: Theodor Vernaleken
88e1d52ccc579e502f8ae23b6330338279d53758.summary: In olden times, accidents often occurred throughout the land during tree felling.

84323aa895415ae147c667a97c10ed0072d7031f.title: The Wild Männlein of Safien
84323aa895415ae147c667a97c10ed0072d7031f.author: Theodor Vernaleken
84323aa895415ae147c667a97c10ed0072d7031f.summary: At the Houses, as the place is called, far back in the Safien valley, a woman was once making cheese.

8859f9660b2e236da871318d10fd0d4be8e1318e.title: The Wild Männlein's Gratitude
8859f9660b2e236da871318d10fd0d4be8e1318e.author: Theodor Vernaleken
8859f9660b2e236da871318d10fd0d4be8e1318e.summary: In Safien, people still know and point out the place where the wild Männlein lived with his wife.

35469bf7437af4f5fa9919769ab149b3f7e8ddfe.title: The Wild Passion for Hunting
35469bf7437af4f5fa9919769ab149b3f7e8ddfe.author: Theodor Vernaleken
35469bf7437af4f5fa9919769ab149b3f7e8ddfe.summary: Another legend from this region—the southern part of Fribourg—relates:

2b773b0a1326183f7a76cfb92fd0031cde4b40bf.title: The Wild-Mannli’s Advice
2b773b0a1326183f7a76cfb92fd0031cde4b40bf.author: Dietrich Jecklin
2b773b0a1326183f7a76cfb92fd0031cde4b40bf.summary: At the time when dear simplicity was still customary in our country, it once happened that the sworn official Val. Suter of Tenna caught a most remarkable animal in his garden.

39f59f5445be599d62c13479e67ba7e0bbcd443f.title: The Wild-Mannli’s Tree-Felling
39f59f5445be599d62c13479e67ba7e0bbcd443f.author: Dietrich Jecklin
39f59f5445be599d62c13479e67ba7e0bbcd443f.summary: Just as people learned from the Fänggen how to bore Teuchel, they learned many other useful methods and practical tricks from them as well.

c1bede04783cf0a382a51a577eaf9949d0027756.title: The Wilden of Sassalbo
c1bede04783cf0a382a51a577eaf9949d0027756.author: Dietrich Jecklin
c1bede04783cf0a382a51a577eaf9949d0027756.summary: East of the small town of Puschlav rises the gigantic Sassalbo. At its foot, deep caves penetrate the mountain’s interior, and these were formerly inhabited by “Wilden.”

e8d916fd9dae7dbc457d8deac3bbb5da86eb6d43.title: The Wildi-Küfer in Oberflachs
e8d916fd9dae7dbc457d8deac3bbb5da86eb6d43.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
e8d916fd9dae7dbc457d8deac3bbb5da86eb6d43.summary: About thirty years ago, a man lived in Oberflachs who, because he knew very well how to handle wine, was given supervision of the municipality’s Zehntenkeller and was therefore called the Wildi-Küfer.

cd135490b12065c2c8c127010eccac146993528d.title: The Wildmannli
cd135490b12065c2c8c127010eccac146993528d.author: Theodor Vernaleken
cd135490b12065c2c8c127010eccac146993528d.summary: On the southeastern side of the great Windgälle rises a strange mass of rock that, seen from some distance, resembles a man standing upright.

8fc0564634646cd1dd894018c7e6ed503e104643.title: The Will-o'-the-Wisp at the Rad-kappeli
8fc0564634646cd1dd894018c7e6ed503e104643.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
8fc0564634646cd1dd894018c7e6ed503e104643.summary: Near the two ponds outside the city of Baden, directly opposite the brickworks there, a chapel called the Rad-kappeli stood on the Bandstrasse several decades ago.

6a32d3455632a9b741592be7003959be3d9b9177.title: The Will-o’-the-Wisp under a Roof
6a32d3455632a9b741592be7003959be3d9b9177.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
6a32d3455632a9b741592be7003959be3d9b9177.summary: Will-o’-the-wisps appear most often at the time of the new moon, when the weather tends to change, and so the farmer regards them as good prophets of the weather.

74f29646acb06e8bf3752ff1a3daa36dc5e570cd.title: The Wine Adulteress
74f29646acb06e8bf3752ff1a3daa36dc5e570cd.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
74f29646acb06e8bf3752ff1a3daa36dc5e570cd.summary: A girl from Zermatt who had grown up at Aroleid found that region altogether too wild, so she wandered down the valley and through the country.

8262a509081d5ada9623f21a2dfd6bac4a53b905.title: The Wine Bottle That Never Became Empty
8262a509081d5ada9623f21a2dfd6bac4a53b905.author: Theodor Vernaleken
8262a509081d5ada9623f21a2dfd6bac4a53b905.summary: One evening, a man fetched wine from the inn for his wife, who had just given birth.

8e050832c073d32530cfa328ba1b81e3de51728e.title: The Wine Sale
8e050832c073d32530cfa328ba1b81e3de51728e.author: Dietrich Jecklin
8e050832c073d32530cfa328ba1b81e3de51728e.summary: In Zizers there still lives a peaceable married couple—he is called Hans, she Uschi (Ursula)—who in the year 1874 had “already sold,” that is, promised, the wine still in the Bütte (wine vat).

0e7dbb2015f827a4dc1167395688a3d06e96e35c.title: The Winon Maiden
0e7dbb2015f827a4dc1167395688a3d06e96e35c.author: Alois Lütolf
0e7dbb2015f827a4dc1167395688a3d06e96e35c.summary: The little Winon River near Beromünster—perhaps an ancient Vienna—rises near Neudorf and flows through a valley covered with firs, the Winonholz, toward the Lucerne border near Maihausen.

47fc8266e2115ac09729f7d3335b76ae8ec3a549.title: The Wirtletier
47fc8266e2115ac09729f7d3335b76ae8ec3a549.author: Alois Lütolf
47fc8266e2115ac09729f7d3335b76ae8ec3a549.summary: Wirtle is the name of the hill between Ballwil and Hochdorf over which the valley road has passed for centuries.

9d6934b65be5a91b4dbf9b2906723f1853228ff6.title: The Wise Fänggenmannli
9d6934b65be5a91b4dbf9b2906723f1853228ff6.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9d6934b65be5a91b4dbf9b2906723f1853228ff6.summary: The inhabitants of the municipality of Tenna caught a large bear that had done great harm to their herds.

b8e47cb9e010cc8ea55dcaba42f3f4fe10060ca2.title: The Wishing Cave near Arosa
b8e47cb9e010cc8ea55dcaba42f3f4fe10060ca2.author: Dietrich Jecklin
b8e47cb9e010cc8ea55dcaba42f3f4fe10060ca2.summary: Far back in the Schanfigg Valley, above the little village of Arosa and lovely Schwellisee, an old Ziernüßlibaum stands alone.

ddd8f8c9e8cceb2f2f91cf6b6962c2da7dae1963.title: The Wissle Hate Whistling
ddd8f8c9e8cceb2f2f91cf6b6962c2da7dae1963.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
ddd8f8c9e8cceb2f2f91cf6b6962c2da7dae1963.summary: It is an old Zellata (legend) that the Wissle, or Herumjini, cannot bear whistling.

3464a199aafbfe7db4330888f94b4d2f4d4473f5.title: The Wißmaidli Fir on Schenkenberg near Oberflachs
3464a199aafbfe7db4330888f94b4d2f4d4473f5.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
3464a199aafbfe7db4330888f94b4d2f4d4473f5.summary: The Wißmaidli fir was an old tree near Oberflachs, now felled; the Wißmaidli spring is nearby.

5c47da2ee110564c73693c08380ffd58901ff8b7.title: The Witch (Oberuzwil, SG)
5c47da2ee110564c73693c08380ffd58901ff8b7.author: Jakob Kuoni
5c47da2ee110564c73693c08380ffd58901ff8b7.summary: In a house in Oberuzwil, whenever milk was boiled, it “separated.” Someone advised that the next time milk was boiled and began to rise, it should be stirred with a birch switch until it settled again.

91f3b46f2da589e3590e504b6d6c9d9993fa3622.title: The Witch (Waldkirch, St. Gallen)
91f3b46f2da589e3590e504b6d6c9d9993fa3622.author: Jakob Kuoni
91f3b46f2da589e3590e504b6d6c9d9993fa3622.summary: In the Haslenholz toward Lehn, a woman wrapped in ragged clothes teased passersby, especially women.

a8025588ba6c5730a263af912f00d26eeb382910.title: The Witch and Child-Murderer
a8025588ba6c5730a263af912f00d26eeb382910.author: Josef Müller
a8025588ba6c5730a263af912f00d26eeb382910.summary: In one region, newborn children were always being killed, and when they were examined, a little wound like one made by a Gufen was found on their heads.

15d6aa2d4b225e024831fd5acd47195b644ba467.title: The Witch and Her Husband
15d6aa2d4b225e024831fd5acd47195b644ba467.author: Josef Müller
15d6aa2d4b225e024831fd5acd47195b644ba467.summary: There was once a husband whose wife often went dancing at night.

a7ba99f01d95b3d8f3ef598104d0fe74f8766e11.title: The Witch and the Bell
a7ba99f01d95b3d8f3ef598104d0fe74f8766e11.author: Josef Müller
a7ba99f01d95b3d8f3ef598104d0fe74f8766e11.summary: When the people of Schattdorf were trying to hang the new great bell in the church tower, they could not manage it at all; the bell simply would not go in.

8c61c71b0c2372a2e2216a9ccdd6f90399154542.title: The Witch and the Boulder in Isental
8c61c71b0c2372a2e2216a9ccdd6f90399154542.author: Josef Müller
8c61c71b0c2372a2e2216a9ccdd6f90399154542.summary: In former times Isental was called Wiesental, old Furggälä-Vreni always said, and the ravines and Rübi valleys on the north side of the valley did not yet exist.

b28933c3f69808335edf3deca58f524632cbbb44.title: The Witch and the Grain Field
b28933c3f69808335edf3deca58f524632cbbb44.author: Alois Lütolf
b28933c3f69808335edf3deca58f524632cbbb44.summary: A farmer sent his servant several hours away on business.

99f09d0ec5a8f6e186f309ac6fdcc4cdeab3aa02.title: The Witch and the Three Bells
99f09d0ec5a8f6e186f309ac6fdcc4cdeab3aa02.author: Josef Müller

b273479531e2b4f71d93d8d217f251e3d65048bc.title: The Witch as a Fly
b273479531e2b4f71d93d8d217f251e3d65048bc.author: Jakob Kuoni
b273479531e2b4f71d93d8d217f251e3d65048bc.summary: A young man from Grabs left his beloved and accepted enlistment money for Dutch service.

5555c138a10e91ac9d5c479fc48b961ac1903e1a.title: The Witch at Fetan
5555c138a10e91ac9d5c479fc48b961ac1903e1a.author: Dietrich Jecklin
5555c138a10e91ac9d5c479fc48b961ac1903e1a.summary: Several young men traveling at midnight from Klein-Fetan to Gross-Fetan saw, by the favor of the moonlight, a human body lying on the ground in a meadow beside the road.

c423e718651c3a8774415756859271379f63c3ea.title: The Witch at Hegdorn
c423e718651c3a8774415756859271379f63c3ea.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
c423e718651c3a8774415756859271379f63c3ea.summary: At Hegdorn on the Naters mountain, it is said, there once lived a witch married to an honest man.

c6505ecb6fe7880f48cfd54090e9c1b8ff383faa.title: The Witch at the Stafel
c6505ecb6fe7880f48cfd54090e9c1b8ff383faa.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
c6505ecb6fe7880f48cfd54090e9c1b8ff383faa.summary: At the time when there was still much talk of witches and Strideln and their mischief, the community of Zermatt held a Gemeintrunk.

8b5a3a3c5560ca6f53c8da0af095ba39384c3815.title: The Witch at the Window
8b5a3a3c5560ca6f53c8da0af095ba39384c3815.author: Jakob Kuoni
8b5a3a3c5560ca6f53c8da0af095ba39384c3815.summary: A young man told me that he was not at all superstitious, but that late one night he had nevertheless seen something that struck him as strange.

3dec1cf1055f097eb5899fcaa6b91e04693084d1.title: The Witch Catherine Repond, or Catillon la Toascha
3dec1cf1055f097eb5899fcaa6b91e04693084d1.author: C. Kohlrusch
3dec1cf1055f097eb5899fcaa6b91e04693084d1.summary: This witch was actually named Catherine Repond, but when people wanted to anger her, they also called her Catillon la Toascha, or Hunchback Kate.

68578590d2c31d6e319a5de23e220f3e96222f44.title: The Witch Heaps on the Diedenberg
68578590d2c31d6e319a5de23e220f3e96222f44.author: Josef Müller

781a130d5719fc34435ef30d0edde710c420b5fb.title: The Witch in Gulatsch
781a130d5719fc34435ef30d0edde710c420b5fb.author: Dietrich Jecklin
781a130d5719fc34435ef30d0edde710c420b5fb.summary: It is now eight years since a great, withered fir stood in the forest behind the village of Ruis, beside the Schmuor—the water that comes from the Panixer mountain—on the road leading to Andest.

9c92bbbc12866c8ddb134d38a938416c452543fb.title: The Witch in Langwies
9c92bbbc12866c8ddb134d38a938416c452543fb.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9c92bbbc12866c8ddb134d38a938416c452543fb.summary: In former times a house stood in the “Bizirüti” near Langwies, inhabited by a man and his wife.

fac66ff3f9b45ba8b94c41a31fd30446d8f2befb.title: The Witch in Sapün
fac66ff3f9b45ba8b94c41a31fd30446d8f2befb.author: Dietrich Jecklin
fac66ff3f9b45ba8b94c41a31fd30446d8f2befb.summary: A man once walked uphill through Sapün-Dörfli above Langwies with one of his finest cattle when a little old woman came pattering up to him, looked at the animal, and stroked its back with her right hand while saying, “Das ist doch…

f17d54203af1b48dfb6a82fccbf4cc7ba667ffdf.title: The Witch in Scheid
f17d54203af1b48dfb6a82fccbf4cc7ba667ffdf.author: Dietrich Jecklin
f17d54203af1b48dfb6a82fccbf4cc7ba667ffdf.summary: An old but very skilled hunter in Scheid related that in his youth he once had to tend the cattle during winter in the stable of his somewhat remote Maiensäss.

1f2ee8341c421906d05c91feb290a3d0f83350e6.title: The Witch in the Blüemlismatt
1f2ee8341c421906d05c91feb290a3d0f83350e6.author: Josef Müller
1f2ee8341c421906d05c91feb290a3d0f83350e6.summary: a) Opposite Silenen, in the ancient Tatschihaus in the Blüemlismatt, lived an old witch.

4478e8787d591a8aba316d419ef7322e570d35da.title: The Witch in the Burned Juppe
4478e8787d591a8aba316d419ef7322e570d35da.author: Dietrich Jecklin
4478e8787d591a8aba316d419ef7322e570d35da.summary: A housewife in Montbiel had a flock of hens that laid eggs every day and thereby gave her great pleasure.

9e15088ec0d19d98e694677da711b9a3a0a982be.title: The Witch in the Bächen
9e15088ec0d19d98e694677da711b9a3a0a982be.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
9e15088ec0d19d98e694677da711b9a3a0a982be.summary: Many amusing legends are still told of so-called witches and Strideln: how, for example, they harmed people and made fools of them in many ways, continuing these roguish tricks until at last they had to pay for them at the stake.

7af309a74d8764aeca3aa084f6d0f1c8ee53d0fe.title: The Witch in the Castle Pond of Sulzberg
7af309a74d8764aeca3aa084f6d0f1c8ee53d0fe.author: C. Kohlrusch
7af309a74d8764aeca3aa084f6d0f1c8ee53d0fe.summary: In the castle pond of Sulzberg Castle lived a witch in the form of a toad. She had been granted the power to commit every possible mischief as far as the boundaries of the castle's possessions extended.

adc2fc1d4149bbf908246a4e531ad48396b1f459.title: The Witch in the Seelisberg Seeli
adc2fc1d4149bbf908246a4e531ad48396b1f459.author: Josef Müller
adc2fc1d4149bbf908246a4e531ad48396b1f459.summary: An old witch on the Kulm rolled a great stone down the slope.

0ee1fd7d2d764290f6e14d00035d815980fc92fe.title: The Witch in the Tiejen
0ee1fd7d2d764290f6e14d00035d815980fc92fe.author: Dietrich Jecklin
0ee1fd7d2d764290f6e14d00035d815980fc92fe.summary: A very long time ago, an old little man named Ciprian lived in the Tiejen, an Alp above Langwies. His household up there was solitary and simple, and he knew no great wants.

d68688cd31e6a314a88872c0e1434acceb4d1dc6.title: The Witch in Wolf Form
d68688cd31e6a314a88872c0e1434acceb4d1dc6.author: Dietrich Jecklin
d68688cd31e6a314a88872c0e1434acceb4d1dc6.summary: In the area around Luzein, a wolf once terrified herd and herdsmen and harassed the country people in many ways.

92e37c2390b92e034f926d284e6bcad55a956fa0.title: The Witch Maidens of Habkeren
92e37c2390b92e034f926d284e6bcad55a956fa0.author: Hermann Hartmann
92e37c2390b92e034f926d284e6bcad55a956fa0.summary: Long ago—no one knows how long—two boys from Habkeren used to visit two maidens about whom the people could not say who they were or where they had come from into the mountain valley.

190f9b6165fda0fa53f74d5363d7420b85db322d.title: The Witch near Strahlegg
190f9b6165fda0fa53f74d5363d7420b85db322d.author: Dietrich Jecklin
190f9b6165fda0fa53f74d5363d7420b85db322d.summary: At midnight, a young man from Jenatz was walking toward Strahlegg “z’hengert”—to go courting.

3e1ca2db8274b042c05c61c43831fb37f5c35f5d.title: The Witch of Andermatt
3e1ca2db8274b042c05c61c43831fb37f5c35f5d.author: Josef Müller
3e1ca2db8274b042c05c61c43831fb37f5c35f5d.summary: As late as the fifties of the preceding century, an old witch lived in Andermatt.

e8ced098ea7d7f19ce94898d7f5b72b1d56dd503.title: The Witch of Dallenwil
e8ced098ea7d7f19ce94898d7f5b72b1d56dd503.author: Alois Lütolf
e8ced098ea7d7f19ce94898d7f5b72b1d56dd503.summary: The witch of Dallenwil practiced weather-making.

92a1acaeace45854fbe1d9b55bcbce47ed5522f0.title: The Witch of Lauterbrunnen
92a1acaeace45854fbe1d9b55bcbce47ed5522f0.author: Hermann Hartmann
92a1acaeace45854fbe1d9b55bcbce47ed5522f0.summary: Many years ago, a woman in Lauterbrunnen was suspected of witchcraft.

7964e975f1ed4dd889971549c93751a492e4c546.title: The Witch on Her Deathbed
7964e975f1ed4dd889971549c93751a492e4c546.author: Alois Lütolf
7964e975f1ed4dd889971549c93751a492e4c546.summary: There was a witch who made hailstorms.

09e8e292fb995989df13117a1fbf3a6dee79b7e8.title: The Witch on the Avalanche
09e8e292fb995989df13117a1fbf3a6dee79b7e8.author: Josef Müller
09e8e292fb995989df13117a1fbf3a6dee79b7e8.summary: The people of Erstfeld often saw a woman walk from Bürtschen through the village as far as Wyler.

61db95e862412ee11056a808730284e6f8fd7537.title: The Witch on the First
61db95e862412ee11056a808730284e6f8fd7537.author: Dietrich Jecklin
61db95e862412ee11056a808730284e6f8fd7537.summary: On the First in Sapün near Langwies lived a witch who could transform herself into all manner of shapes.

4748777f5288232b9a55bfe2c45213516fef8bd8.title: The Witch on the Lorisboden
4748777f5288232b9a55bfe2c45213516fef8bd8.author: Dietrich Jecklin
4748777f5288232b9a55bfe2c45213516fef8bd8.summary: Not far from the Mayerhof in Obersaxen is a meadowland called the Lorisboden, upon which several barns stand.

cfd899e6f4ee28313f5898768344ae540c9e49d5.title: The Witch Stone
cfd899e6f4ee28313f5898768344ae540c9e49d5.author: Josef Müller
cfd899e6f4ee28313f5898768344ae540c9e49d5.summary: The witch stone in the Grossplangg above the Dieden at Wassen bears an oblong, rounded Tuolä on its surface; old witches are said to have pressed it out.

6e4c26ac30afe67c98fa8ea3c67c5ea612008c26.title: The Witch Stones
6e4c26ac30afe67c98fa8ea3c67c5ea612008c26.author: Alois Lütolf
6e4c26ac30afe67c98fa8ea3c67c5ea612008c26.summary: In former times, when witches still held their regular gatherings, they marked the places where these occurred with strange signs.

5c2084691a396dcf316ae744a2f6726fbccbe04a.title: The Witch Who Comes Every Altjohrobe
5c2084691a396dcf316ae744a2f6726fbccbe04a.author: M. Sooder
5c2084691a396dcf316ae744a2f6726fbccbe04a.summary: The year was seventeen hundred and ninety-eight, a time when the French devastated everything around here.

b3fa77e4aba501d3f97b6e83b70b967cf4db1549.title: The Witch with the Red Half-Stockings
b3fa77e4aba501d3f97b6e83b70b967cf4db1549.author: Josef Müller
b3fa77e4aba501d3f97b6e83b70b967cf4db1549.summary: ‘My grandfather,’ relates a 70-year-old woman originally from Meien, ‘was a Geissbub in Wassen in his youth.

115c8ac1082c17662e681ef7ee55014183bdec4c.title: The Witch with Two Kinds of Stockings
115c8ac1082c17662e681ef7ee55014183bdec4c.author: Josef Müller
115c8ac1082c17662e681ef7ee55014183bdec4c.summary: In the autumn of 1808, a strange little woman came to Bürglen wearing a red stocking on one leg and a black one on the other.

fd78e6fecb028e2dc104acf956547168be93d4e2.title: The Witch's Wishes
fd78e6fecb028e2dc104acf956547168be93d4e2.author: Josef Müller
fd78e6fecb028e2dc104acf956547168be93d4e2.summary: a) An old witch was being led to the stake.

bbb9d00fb6713df6e1152a35625638195cbcc335.title: The Witchcraft at Obersaxen
bbb9d00fb6713df6e1152a35625638195cbcc335.author: Dietrich Jecklin
bbb9d00fb6713df6e1152a35625638195cbcc335.summary: On a magnificent morning the shepherd drove out his animals as usual, but that morning he felt very strange.

31d4eb4b6ac0b55d927cc9513a99447ba27091a2.title: The Witches in Pardenn
31d4eb4b6ac0b55d927cc9513a99447ba27091a2.author: Dietrich Jecklin
31d4eb4b6ac0b55d927cc9513a99447ba27091a2.summary: Many years ago, the cows on Alp Pardenn (Closters) were often heard running about during the night.

562da34c4ad8e13061ce01dfe4653a36bc08c1e2.title: The Witches in the Foferenwald
562da34c4ad8e13061ce01dfe4653a36bc08c1e2.author: C. Kohlrusch
562da34c4ad8e13061ce01dfe4653a36bc08c1e2.summary: Not far from the village of Tschugg, upon the southern slope of the Jolimont, lies a forest called the Foferenwald.

9a2450b790353307ef5b3039e6acea4f1590630f.title: The Witches in the Krinnen
9a2450b790353307ef5b3039e6acea4f1590630f.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9a2450b790353307ef5b3039e6acea4f1590630f.summary: In the “Krinnen,” a Heuberg in Sapün above Langwies, there was a gathering place for witches, and the “Hexen-Bödeli” where it stood is still pointed out today.

9cfe74bf53b4d69c50737a191266c4f0ff3fae13.title: The Witches of Pardenn
9cfe74bf53b4d69c50737a191266c4f0ff3fae13.author: Theodor Vernaleken
9cfe74bf53b4d69c50737a191266c4f0ff3fae13.summary: Behind the farmstead of Monbiel, which belongs to Klosters, at the far end of the Prättigau, lies the beautiful Alp Pardenn.

18955e6fb98f0302773a1c40710a706e36441396.title: The Witches of Trins
18955e6fb98f0302773a1c40710a706e36441396.author: Dietrich Jecklin
18955e6fb98f0302773a1c40710a706e36441396.summary: The carter Wellinger of Schleuis once reached the “Stutze” before the village of Trins with a load when one of the wagon’s front wheels suddenly flew off as though blown away.

0a4a4c3cef8114734babe5fb0d127a82c85dc743.title: The Witches on the Rübi at Silenen
0a4a4c3cef8114734babe5fb0d127a82c85dc743.author: Josef Müller
0a4a4c3cef8114734babe5fb0d127a82c85dc743.summary: a) Once, the terrified people of Silenen watched helplessly as the Rübi burst from the steep Kilchtal with uncanny force, threatening death and destruction.

9b71741912d46257e8bdb9c6f723c83cb5923940.title: The Witches on the Vierschröt
9b71741912d46257e8bdb9c6f723c83cb5923940.author: Josef Müller
9b71741912d46257e8bdb9c6f723c83cb5923940.summary: a) The Vierschröt is an enormous, almost perfectly rectangular, tilted rock guarding the narrow entrance to the Riedertal, a valley so rich in myths and legends.

cbcd97d44e38c2800b3decaec1bcd19956e3e693.title: The Witches on Urden
cbcd97d44e38c2800b3decaec1bcd19956e3e693.author: Dietrich Jecklin
cbcd97d44e38c2800b3decaec1bcd19956e3e693.summary: It was one autumn when the people of Maladers had left their Alp below Urden early because of bad weather.

9e4a9e9f13cbe22f9f2b8c01503cc728ab7351d9.title: The Witches' Dance
9e4a9e9f13cbe22f9f2b8c01503cc728ab7351d9.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9e4a9e9f13cbe22f9f2b8c01503cc728ab7351d9.summary: Above the little village of Cavreisen lies a level meadow.

c8af861d49af53df9704f27425d3d6db5be1c0c5.title: The Witches' Dance in the Ried-Loch
c8af861d49af53df9704f27425d3d6db5be1c0c5.author: Dietrich Jecklin
c8af861d49af53df9704f27425d3d6db5be1c0c5.summary: Once two men from Closters were returning home from the Davos market. Night had long since fallen when they reached the so-called Ried-Loch, beside the path that descends from the so-called Black Lake and joins the road.

7c35a5c46c5a6c73149a392d9002321a8708a020.title: The Witches' Ride
7c35a5c46c5a6c73149a392d9002321a8708a020.author: Dietrich Jecklin
7c35a5c46c5a6c73149a392d9002321a8708a020.summary: A girl served as a maid on a farm in Fanas and noticed that her mistress often left the house in the evening, disappearing from the kitchen in an inexplicable way.

10914122f93ef95085934861bd40e510776e6502.title: The Witches' Tower in Uznach
10914122f93ef95085934861bd40e510776e6502.author: Jakob Kuoni
10914122f93ef95085934861bd40e510776e6502.summary: On the place known as the Burg, above the little town of Uznach, there formerly stood—until 1867—a very massive, fairly tall, square tower called the Herenturm.

fc04b9ee2fb34be3adc2774eb21a3ce18de230fe.title: The Witches’ Dance at Fetan
fc04b9ee2fb34be3adc2774eb21a3ce18de230fe.author: Dietrich Jecklin
fc04b9ee2fb34be3adc2774eb21a3ce18de230fe.summary: There were once two girls in Fetan who were inseparable friends.

22f4645bc40d830a3247cf8905eaa9e1fe6d941c.title: The Witches’ Dance at Schuders
22f4645bc40d830a3247cf8905eaa9e1fe6d941c.author: Dietrich Jecklin
22f4645bc40d830a3247cf8905eaa9e1fe6d941c.summary: In Schuders there was once a boy whose parents, being miserly people, never wished to let him join the company of other young people.

bc131d70789d4c4b77f03df03a89a84d93f9d6f9.title: The Witches’ Dance in the Ried-Loche
bc131d70789d4c4b77f03df03a89a84d93f9d6f9.author: Dietrich Jecklin
bc131d70789d4c4b77f03df03a89a84d93f9d6f9.summary: One evening a doctor and another man were walking from Davos-Laret to Closters-Äuja.

10743d6d3799e617238600d5292f9581edbcb1cb.title: The Witches’ Dance on Gafarrabühl
10743d6d3799e617238600d5292f9581edbcb1cb.author: Jakob Kuoni
10743d6d3799e617238600d5292f9581edbcb1cb.summary: Surrounded on every side by lush herbs, up here there is a level little spot where nothing ever grows green or blossoms, because in former times witches and evil spirits held their nocturnal gatherings there.

1097cec806b07f4b0d5f118d7d91ce6523591b90.title: The Witches’ Dancing Places in Tumleschg
1097cec806b07f4b0d5f118d7d91ce6523591b90.author: Dietrich Jecklin
1097cec806b07f4b0d5f118d7d91ce6523591b90.summary: On the right side of the Almenser-Tobel is a sparse meadow near a mill.

617dd2957fe0cc04b1b80ed355f2897b241eb8b4.title: The Witches’ Fight
617dd2957fe0cc04b1b80ed355f2897b241eb8b4.author: Dietrich Jecklin
617dd2957fe0cc04b1b80ed355f2897b241eb8b4.summary: A Schierser who had his cattle at Rahl, a “Gadenstatt” above Fanas, for the “Vor-Winterung” and was feeding them there heard dreadful screaming in the yard before the stalls for a long time one night.

f91edbc3583668945dbf1bd8a5cbc1f6b12e1e3e.title: The Witches’ House
f91edbc3583668945dbf1bd8a5cbc1f6b12e1e3e.author: Dietrich Jecklin
f91edbc3583668945dbf1bd8a5cbc1f6b12e1e3e.summary: Among the ruined houses at Alto near Puschlav, surely none has acquired as much significance in folk tradition as the one popularly called the “Witches’ House.” In this house, a very long time ago, a widow lived with her son.

551fba69bff52184e00cf2a503e99baf732a2374.title: The Witches’ Place near Laupen
551fba69bff52184e00cf2a503e99baf732a2374.author: Jakob Kuoni
551fba69bff52184e00cf2a503e99baf732a2374.summary: Near the hamlet of Laupen in the municipality of Zuzwil, a round place lies in a small wood, overgrown with marsh grass and a few stunted pines.

45fd8c00e4df19774307d85a1aca546f4d8f1c96.title: The Witches’ Stone near Kerns
45fd8c00e4df19774307d85a1aca546f4d8f1c96.author: Alois Lütolf
45fd8c00e4df19774307d85a1aca546f4d8f1c96.summary: On the meadow of a common pasture at Kerns lies a stone called the ‘Witches’ Stone.’ Its square surface may measure about twelve Klafter, lies at a slight angle, and is otherwise perfectly even.

9139d32cd71524aa60bf0ff16210c95fcff7ae2b.title: The Witch’s Children
9139d32cd71524aa60bf0ff16210c95fcff7ae2b.author: Josef Müller
9139d32cd71524aa60bf0ff16210c95fcff7ae2b.summary: A witch had four children, two of whom went to school.

711d5f824905afd84ebd2bdf99fd591d25b47696.title: The Witch’s Granite Block
711d5f824905afd84ebd2bdf99fd591d25b47696.author: C. Kohlrusch
711d5f824905afd84ebd2bdf99fd591d25b47696.summary: Not far from Thusis lies the scattered municipality of Tschappina. Beside its last houses is a small meadow on which a great granite block rises.

f6bf831085846a0f2f1d75460abfcb6b9a587c62.title: The Wolf in Distress
f6bf831085846a0f2f1d75460abfcb6b9a587c62.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
f6bf831085846a0f2f1d75460abfcb6b9a587c62.summary: At Z'en Grächten in the Leukergrund one stormy evening, a wolf looked miserably and hungrily through an open stable door where a young fellow was tending the livestock.

190a781872422954be68c69fedba0ecaac26eb2d.title: The Wolf in the Grieskumme
190a781872422954be68c69fedba0ecaac26eb2d.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
190a781872422954be68c69fedba0ecaac26eb2d.summary: The Grieskumme is a high alpine pasture that can feed dry cattle during the summer and a great many sheep in autumn.

6f651f6119a74e4013220a2fbc32c9f7455edb44.title: The Wolf of Obervaz
6f651f6119a74e4013220a2fbc32c9f7455edb44.author: Dietrich Jecklin
6f651f6119a74e4013220a2fbc32c9f7455edb44.summary: A large wolf once roamed around Obervaz and tore apart one of the farmers' sheep every day.

b893f3e50e8afed80f0ead25b140edcea8074d3a.title: The Wolf on the Lenzer-Haide
b893f3e50e8afed80f0ead25b140edcea8074d3a.author: Dietrich Jecklin
b893f3e50e8afed80f0ead25b140edcea8074d3a.summary: One evening a man traveled the road from Lenz across the Lenzer-Haide and led a goat with him on a rope.

0e5f95a6dff68bc18641cb1b1f40382734771935.title: The Woman Hermit of Wallenstadt
0e5f95a6dff68bc18641cb1b1f40382734771935.author: Jakob Kuoni
0e5f95a6dff68bc18641cb1b1f40382734771935.summary: Women hermits, forest sisters, or Beguines once lived on the high rock that bears the very unusual pilgrimage chapel of Saint George near Bärschis, probably built on the ruins of a Roman fortress.

fda567ae6aa240181ac10c63c3dabfccbe7add94.title: The Woman in Childbed
fda567ae6aa240181ac10c63c3dabfccbe7add94.author: M. Sooder
fda567ae6aa240181ac10c63c3dabfccbe7add94.summary: In a farmhouse, a Chimpettere died, and she was carried to the cemetery. The very next night, she came back. She sighed and groaned outside the windows and looked sadly into the sitting room. This went on for a long time.

ff2d919cb696d0f84c0a66e2b5e9bdb8407878d9.title: The Woman in the Wild Host: The Billy Goat
ff2d919cb696d0f84c0a66e2b5e9bdb8407878d9.author: Alois Lütolf
ff2d919cb696d0f84c0a66e2b5e9bdb8407878d9.summary: At Schwarzenberg in Schorried near Alpnach, people know that an extraordinarily large billy goat appears there with a catlike animal sitting between its horns.

ed3a5a39d2842f2c74c05200c78fac462ea540bd.title: The Woman in the Wild Host: The Sled Ride
ed3a5a39d2842f2c74c05200c78fac462ea540bd.author: Alois Lütolf
ed3a5a39d2842f2c74c05200c78fac462ea540bd.summary: Very often in the wild hunt of the gods, a woman has either a co-leading or dominant rank, or else a suffering part. Her name is Streggelen, Grosskellerin, or Pfaffengälere.

0ee1a2614896b90c555fe3cf846ebd3a132d0076.title: The Woman in the Wild Host: The Wagon
0ee1a2614896b90c555fe3cf846ebd3a132d0076.author: Alois Lütolf
0ee1a2614896b90c555fe3cf846ebd3a132d0076.summary: At Ennetmoos near Stans, "a dreadful and pitiful screaming" is often heard up and down the Pfaffenkellergraben.

aef918aa9334158060b641d546151a88e409931a.title: The Woman in the Wild Host: Various Tales of the Streggelen
aef918aa9334158060b641d546151a88e409931a.author: Alois Lütolf
aef918aa9334158060b641d546151a88e409931a.summary: On the Galgenbächlein between Sarnen and Sachseln, the wild spirit-woman rides over hill and dale on a “hellish monster,” screaming so loudly that she can be heard for miles around.

104b8f19daaf7f99796c726c2ae4e08f6c867054.title: The Woman in the Wild Hunt: Schöpferschmied-Anneli
104b8f19daaf7f99796c726c2ae4e08f6c867054.author: Alois Lütolf
104b8f19daaf7f99796c726c2ae4e08f6c867054.summary: On the Hostris—that is to say, Hochgesträss, because the ancient road once ran here along the Wigger—lie several Jucharten of farmland called the Holderacker.

31e11bfe3b91df251b4a7ed9dc546d331927b053.title: The Woman in the Wild Hunt: The Captured Streggelen
31e11bfe3b91df251b4a7ed9dc546d331927b053.author: Alois Lütolf
31e11bfe3b91df251b4a7ed9dc546d331927b053.summary: On Streggelnnacht, men from Triengen went into the Oelerhölzli, the beechwood above the village, to hunt and capture the Streggeln.

c0dcdb631f47bd1cd2686bf6f8f1c9894963118e.title: The Woman of the Schafloch
c0dcdb631f47bd1cd2686bf6f8f1c9894963118e.author: Hermann Hartmann
c0dcdb631f47bd1cd2686bf6f8f1c9894963118e.summary: On one of the Alpen on the Sigriswil Rothorn, a thriving boy once slept beside his herd.

d036881ed41d567adc77cf8f5af18996bc29d8c3.title: The Women's Battle on the Langermatt
d036881ed41d567adc77cf8f5af18996bc29d8c3.author: Georg Küffer
d036881ed41d567adc77cf8f5af18996bc29d8c3.summary: In former times, the dark-haired Walliser very often came over the Rawil to the Lenk fair with their mules.

50178bbdd4784a833b0393ece66dd8756ce3e8bd.title: The Women’s Footbridge
50178bbdd4784a833b0393ece66dd8756ce3e8bd.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
50178bbdd4784a833b0393ece66dd8756ce3e8bd.summary: Between Endingen and Degerfelden is a bridge that is dangerous to cross at night; a ghost is said to block the way.

e357bb9dc0f1d50ebb60f7907cb453c7145c24cb.title: The Wondrous Church
e357bb9dc0f1d50ebb60f7907cb453c7145c24cb.author: C. Kohlrusch
e357bb9dc0f1d50ebb60f7907cb453c7145c24cb.summary: High in the ice fields of the Bernese Oberland, in the midst of a glacier, is a wondrous vault of ice that perfectly resembles the interior of a church.

7b0e0f53562206567ede0da1235d365f1f9fd3de.title: The Wondrous Little Bird in the Bruderholz
7b0e0f53562206567ede0da1235d365f1f9fd3de.author: C. Kohlrusch
7b0e0f53562206567ede0da1235d365f1f9fd3de.summary: During the Council at Basel, several clergymen walked out beyond the city into a little wood called the Bruderholz so that they might discuss some disputed points.

caebf2d19524f080d38f0e3a89307420aa83a511.title: The Wondrous Mirror
caebf2d19524f080d38f0e3a89307420aa83a511.author: C. Kohlrusch
caebf2d19524f080d38f0e3a89307420aa83a511.summary: A poor woodcutter working not far from the ruins of Bischofsstein Castle once saw something sparkling and shining among the old masonry like gold, silver, or precious stone.

4a90d54b596e4b479babcd4687c352c87406e29a.title: The Wood-Splitter at Walenhütten
4a90d54b596e4b479babcd4687c352c87406e29a.author: J. J. Jakob
4a90d54b596e4b479babcd4687c352c87406e29a.summary: In the Walenhütten Vorsass, an Alpine herdsman is said to have lived long ago who liked the herding life so well that he once declared that if he could remain on the mountain forever, he had no wish to enter heaven.

5f937545c282a22049bf332721a4ada72ac55845.title: The World’s Gratitude
5f937545c282a22049bf332721a4ada72ac55845.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
5f937545c282a22049bf332721a4ada72ac55845.summary: Slander has been inventive in every age.

8510327697ff5ec5ded908c3fa8b04f841abb593.title: The Wuetihee
8510327697ff5ec5ded908c3fa8b04f841abb593.author: Jakob Kuoni
8510327697ff5ec5ded908c3fa8b04f841abb593.summary: High in the forest is a pond from which the village stream flows.

d6743b5009c11c22057830ed053dc36e2364de8f.title: The Wunderkräutlein
d6743b5009c11c22057830ed053dc36e2364de8f.author: Jakob Kuoni
d6743b5009c11c22057830ed053dc36e2364de8f.summary: A barn once stood in the Zelg below Rieden. Its owner kept his livestock there to feed and tend them. He did so with much pain, for he had an ‘open’ leg wound that would not heal.

6f5df64da9d1c251c7b1a27ac54629c6c6456bf7.title: The Wuotië
6f5df64da9d1c251c7b1a27ac54629c6c6456bf7.author: Jakob Kuoni
6f5df64da9d1c251c7b1a27ac54629c6c6456bf7.summary: At Christmas one hears the Wuotië high in the air, a wild outcry coming from the southeast. Anyone who opens the window to hear it better or even to look for it will unfailingly come away with a swollen face. S. Walt

fa327849e067994e943d76dc91dcb7dc05daec84.title: The Wälder and Rhima near Kaiserstuhl
fa327849e067994e943d76dc91dcb7dc05daec84.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
fa327849e067994e943d76dc91dcb7dc05daec84.summary: The Stadtthier in Kaiserstuhl bears the names above.

05e93e3723247cb6aecfc6a037009700c9755317.title: The Wäscherli near Birri
05e93e3723247cb6aecfc6a037009700c9755317.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
05e93e3723247cb6aecfc6a037009700c9755317.summary: The Wäschebach rises in a wooded upland meadow belonging to the village of Birri in the Freiamt, waters the meadows of Aristau, and, after a short course, empties into the Reuss.

8705162b8defccad7c05eba3567f8a81302f2bfb.title: The Wässermann in Seengen
8705162b8defccad7c05eba3567f8a81302f2bfb.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
8705162b8defccad7c05eba3567f8a81302f2bfb.summary: The Wässermann once cheated his neighbors over water rights and has wandered ever since.

56875e68e7f452267f0101b6ea8a388ea0452723.title: The Wättermanndli in the Pörtlialp
56875e68e7f452267f0101b6ea8a388ea0452723.author: Josef Müller
56875e68e7f452267f0101b6ea8a388ea0452723.summary: 1. Whenever people heard a Jauchzer coming from the Beerdli, those at the Ronastutz and in Fellenen would say, “Aha! The Wättermanndli has given another Jauchzer in the Beerdli; the weather will turn foul.”

a1e1c48154485a2353cf737e37ba168645fa3533.title: The Wütisheer (C. Kohlrusch)
a1e1c48154485a2353cf737e37ba168645fa3533.author: C. Kohlrusch
a1e1c48154485a2353cf737e37ba168645fa3533.summary: From the Rotental between Hasli and Grindelwald and across the Scheidegg, one often hears the roaring of the raging host, or Wütisheer, as it is called here.

c8b20a4e2a7887e20e0d7cd2c589dd74a5a14464.title: The Wütisheer (H. Hartmann)
c8b20a4e2a7887e20e0d7cd2c589dd74a5a14464.author: Hermann Hartmann
c8b20a4e2a7887e20e0d7cd2c589dd74a5a14464.summary: Between Hasli and Grindelwald, one often hears from the direction of the Rotental the roaring of the gray Talherren or of the Wütisheer.

b2a210b7c39fc0cdc923d8335cc92fc9c7a395c5.title: The Young Duke

b2a210b7c39fc0cdc923d8335cc92fc9c7a395c5.summary: Once there was a young duke who was so devout and God-fearing that he would have preferred to die at once and journey to Heaven.

fb2d3a61ce6bb73fb98833eb2603ae3949d0261a.author: C. Kohlrusch
fb2d3a61ce6bb73fb98833eb2603ae3949d0261a.summary: Another time, around midnight, a thoroughly tipsy young man from Plaffeien made his way through the lane toward Plasselb.

b4793f185a30028fb4c44b364e82afb6a4b0d210.author: Otto Sutermeister
b4793f185a30028fb4c44b364e82afb6a4b0d210.summary: A king had a young noble retainer called Junker Prahlhans because he always promised much and delivered little. But a jester also lived at the king's court, and he wanted to reform Prahlhans. It happened in the following way:

0ee401823635e41baee0b1f8e15491284bea2cab.title: The Young Treasure Hunters
0ee401823635e41baee0b1f8e15491284bea2cab.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
0ee401823635e41baee0b1f8e15491284bea2cab.summary: Two boys were talking with each other about treasure hunting: "The Devil has the treasures in his power."—"Then he must bring us money."—"Yes, but the person to whom the Jaggi must bring money must not be very good."—"God be praised, that would be me."

2e2ef21d429c0453a4539afecf4768e44c0e0b13.title: The Zermatt Man’s Marflu

2e2ef21d429c0453a4539afecf4768e44c0e0b13.summary: Even now, people in the mountains believe in certain places that the Marflu of the marmots comes from their eating a particular herb before hibernation.

154000cd9dde10ef6a17c01da92aadb7a1f7cb7d.title: The Ziberlisturm
154000cd9dde10ef6a17c01da92aadb7a1f7cb7d.author: M. Sooder
154000cd9dde10ef6a17c01da92aadb7a1f7cb7d.summary: The Nachtlütli were very small, only about this high; they scarcely reached above a person’s knee.

3f8dd17e24a88c3548ce66dca309e34486204990.title: The Ziprion
3f8dd17e24a88c3548ce66dca309e34486204990.author: Dietrich Jecklin
3f8dd17e24a88c3548ce66dca309e34486204990.summary: There, as far as the sky was blue,

9c2ca77025353d8a7c791752083e1bd46c73c153.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9c2ca77025353d8a7c791752083e1bd46c73c153.summary: Years ago, a Senne, a Zu-Senne, and the Schreiber stayed on the Tamins-Grossalp.

8b1c762171eb578393e9f1a89d4e65ea58a34336.title: The Zwingherr
8b1c762171eb578393e9f1a89d4e65ea58a34336.author: Meinrad Lienert
8b1c762171eb578393e9f1a89d4e65ea58a34336.summary: In those dark times when individuals even in Switzerland still presumed to exercise unlimited dominion over the bodies and souls of their fellow human beings, a Hagheer, or Zwingherr, lived in the region near Wald.

5a1f930633fecb9d80bbb33c7a2ac206014131bd.title: The Zwingherr of Wartenstein in the Emmental
5a1f930633fecb9d80bbb33c7a2ac206014131bd.author: Theodor Vernaleken
5a1f930633fecb9d80bbb33c7a2ac206014131bd.summary: Zwingherren or Twingherren are said to have inhabited most castles in the Canton of Bern.

98148238dba70486925516ab33e5a7175b13d473.author: Alois Lütolf
98148238dba70486925516ab33e5a7175b13d473.summary: There was once a Zwingburg in Wolhusen.

bb022ebb911222b057f57a451bd123490ecbefa7.title: The Zwingnagel
bb022ebb911222b057f57a451bd123490ecbefa7.author: Jakob Kuoni
bb022ebb911222b057f57a451bd123490ecbefa7.summary: One afternoon on the Flums Alp called Fursch, the cattle and dairying equipment had been moved down from the upper Säss to the lower one.

844ff15171682e2dc626bffb8a0063027a7aa240.title: The Zyprion
844ff15171682e2dc626bffb8a0063027a7aa240.author: Theodor Vernaleken
844ff15171682e2dc626bffb8a0063027a7aa240.summary: High above the left bank of the Rhine in Graubünden rises the Calanda mountain chain.

97cb887ff47833d8b8ef33d889ee359c58f0b954.title: The Zössler (Ganterschwil, St. Gallen)
97cb887ff47833d8b8ef33d889ee359c58f0b954.author: Jakob Kuoni
97cb887ff47833d8b8ef33d889ee359c58f0b954.summary: In former times there were many Zössler in the fields; they formed entire chains and leapt after one another. Dr. Henne-Am Rhyn, Deutsche Volkssage.

28207ce46221cacb132ebeefee13933f7e5d59fe.title: The Zössler (Jonschwil, St. Gallen)
28207ce46221cacb132ebeefee13933f7e5d59fe.author: Jakob Kuoni
28207ce46221cacb132ebeefee13933f7e5d59fe.summary: On the holy night, someone saw two ‘Zössler’ walking across the bridge in the Töbeli. Both were headless and had with them a dog that had one fiery eye. Dr. Henne-Am Rhyn, German Folk Legend.

8e549a29464f7d9f96ff1531f3532acfb0eff10b.title: The Züriheiri of Zurzach
8e549a29464f7d9f96ff1531f3532acfb0eff10b.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
8e549a29464f7d9f96ff1531f3532acfb0eff10b.summary: Many centuries ago, a poor boy once came running from the Zurich countryside to Zurzach and begged outside the Ox Inn.

0fdbb8cab8240f2fae812a9cd346c35e14def4a1.title: The Züsler (Benken, St. Gallen)
0fdbb8cab8240f2fae812a9cd346c35e14def4a1.author: Jakob Kuoni
0fdbb8cab8240f2fae812a9cd346c35e14def4a1.summary: Old Spörri, who died at the beginning of the 19th century, had a Reckzug—five horses used to haul ships upward from Lake Zürich through the Linth into Lake Walen—and could therefore feed his horses only at night.

f6083394b5285af37e18eaec96fa5973c7566cd0.title: The Züsler (Kappel, SG)
f6083394b5285af37e18eaec96fa5973c7566cd0.author: Jakob Kuoni
f6083394b5285af37e18eaec96fa5973c7566cd0.summary: In former times, a Züsler made the road across the Bendelhöhe unsafe.

c050bee449cdb40c61bccb8fbe992f437a26b11a.title: The Züsler (Rieden, SG)
c050bee449cdb40c61bccb8fbe992f437a26b11a.author: Jakob Kuoni
c050bee449cdb40c61bccb8fbe992f437a26b11a.summary: In a deep ravine near Rieden, a timber thief atones for his crimes as a Züsler.

1a9897c935ead035bb78753b4f2928db3573a72a.title: The z’Roten Tower in Emd
1a9897c935ead035bb78753b4f2928db3573a72a.author: Moritz Tscheinen and Peter Joseph Ruppen
1a9897c935ead035bb78753b4f2928db3573a72a.summary: Near the so-called "little village," below the parish church in Emd, a large, solidly built, tower-like house with several rooms, halls, and spacious living quarters stood at the edge of a rock.

60b958e60d949cc53c8277fc4d829a040bb815a5.author: C. Kohlrusch
60b958e60d949cc53c8277fc4d829a040bb815a5.summary: Directly before Wartburg, magnificently situated on the Töss and reduced to ruin by the vindictiveness of Queen Agnes of Hungary, rises the no-longer-existing castle of Pfungen, an ancient structure that, if the chronicle can be…

f10bc14e2272ea7b647a18e5c91bd5112707bb2b.title: The Äulihund
f10bc14e2272ea7b647a18e5c91bd5112707bb2b.author: Jakob Kuoni
f10bc14e2272ea7b647a18e5c91bd5112707bb2b.summary: Beside the deep bed of the Thur between Kengelbach and Loretto lies the Äuli, a solitary farmstead.

0b7717c7aa4f074c296f26035644df9d76be7182.title: The Äuliwibli
0b7717c7aa4f074c296f26035644df9d76be7182.author: Jakob Kuoni
0b7717c7aa4f074c296f26035644df9d76be7182.summary: Not far from Flums, by the little chapel above the Seez, the "Äuliwibli" wanders about in shirtsleeves. Whoever catches sight of it suddenly becomes swollen. Dr. Henne-Am Rhyn, Deutsche Volkssage.

72d47057e187fc48cd33e5df64be654319b0e33a.title: The Örkentier
72d47057e187fc48cd33e5df64be654319b0e33a.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz

2a1900651af92198c1662ba2f3843af34b27a18b.title: The ‘Stilled’ Goats
2a1900651af92198c1662ba2f3843af34b27a18b.author: Jakob Kuoni
2a1900651af92198c1662ba2f3843af34b27a18b.summary: When Mühli-Leart, or Mill-Leonhard, who died many years ago, was still young and nosed around the house in the manner of boys, he found a worm-eaten book in an old trough on the upper floor.

1aca1056d30d2efbeec2cf5d51a72ccbccf3ff59.title: The ‘White Mountain Farms’ in Attinghausen
1aca1056d30d2efbeec2cf5d51a72ccbccf3ff59.author: Josef Müller
1aca1056d30d2efbeec2cf5d51a72ccbccf3ff59.summary: I have always heard this told too: In Attinghausen, from Heeräzwy to Regliberg, there was in olden times a broad, beautiful stretch of level land with magnificent farms, and above it there were fine mountain farms reaching up toward Seewli.

87f31e7e49bee72dafb18e97f8e3ed615b4877c4.title: The “Prince’s” Alp
87f31e7e49bee72dafb18e97f8e3ed615b4877c4.author: Dietrich Jecklin
87f31e7e49bee72dafb18e97f8e3ed615b4877c4.summary: A spirit in the “Fürstenalpe” above Trimis, which has belonged to the Bishop of Chur since ancient times, had commanded each successive group of Sennen to say a formula over the herds entrusted to them every evening before going to…

5f5a6c70130445a2ec946f5c002c0d84207db6a4.title: Then Run to the Evil One

9278047db78f2798a121b7f92c4d0901d7fa4a9a.title: Theophrasius Paracelsus
9278047db78f2798a121b7f92c4d0901d7fa4a9a.author: Alois Lütolf

9254084a0154650f0d02d8ee5eeeffbb5fd534fb.summary: On Angereesenacht, a young woman or young man can learn whom he or she will marry.

cb67b07f377e002c8f5f573ccff6c1b725c0bda1.author: Jakob Kuoni
cb67b07f377e002c8f5f573ccff6c1b725c0bda1.summary: According to popular belief, will-o'-the-wisps performed their nocturnal dance as ‘fürige Manne’ because during their lifetimes, they had moved boundary stones and thereby robbed their neighbors.

86873dc5442f823519660a365562515db826ffaf.title: Will-o'-the-Wisps I
86873dc5442f823519660a365562515db826ffaf.author: Jakob Kuoni
86873dc5442f823519660a365562515db826ffaf.summary: The road between Sonnental (Tscherlach) and Bärschis is also said not always to be entirely safe.

dd65a9bfce4880e32a1d85b9ed5b1e2e7a61989c.title: Willading

dd65a9bfce4880e32a1d85b9ed5b1e2e7a61989c.summary: It must surely have been long ago when a lord lived at Thunstetten Castle; his name was Willading.

d6f9180e83886a45cc58238908d28c1931981c23.author: Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Grimm
d6f9180e83886a45cc58238908d28c1931981c23.summary: Grimm recounts Tell’s confrontation with the hat on the pole, the apple shot, and his escape across the lake.

109df4445f70b8906ab5cb77d8e6687e66f75223.title: William Tell (Uri)
109df4445f70b8906ab5cb77d8e6687e66f75223.author: Josef Müller
109df4445f70b8906ab5cb77d8e6687e66f75223.summary: A short oral recollection adds a family visit above Sisikon to William Tell’s journey toward Küssnacht.

6aa29c0ca1a690bc01637ce76fec6a4888ca1cce.author: M. Sooder
6aa29c0ca1a690bc01637ce76fec6a4888ca1cce.summary: a. Whenever there was a Windspiel somewhere, our grandfather used to thrust a pitchfork into it; then it collapsed. But once a man thrust a pitchfork into one and is said to have had a bad leg from that time onward.

f86606137666c27a1847328ce11772dd2dda448f.title: Windspiel (Whirlwind)—Nesselnbach
f86606137666c27a1847328ce11772dd2dda448f.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
f86606137666c27a1847328ce11772dd2dda448f.summary: If a Windspiel can arise beneath a wagon already fully loaded with sheaves, it lifts the wagon into the air and then scatters the entire load in every direction.

7dae94bab5f0749699207855ef04285395f7fae1.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
7dae94bab5f0749699207855ef04285395f7fae1.summary: A young Bernese man near Langenthal in Upper Aargau did not believe in the spectral nature of the Windsbraut.

f9f798ab9957d517a4d397fc4023207697dbd7c0.title: Wine Magic

f9f798ab9957d517a4d397fc4023207697dbd7c0.summary: During the thirties of the 19th century, while workers near Intschi were engaged in building the new Gotthard road, they saw many a Lagel of the finest Italian wine being carried down the old Ried road on the opposite side of the narrow Reuss Valley.

731b712ef2d4e02ec547aadf0e5e826a584cce1e.summary: There is said to have been a vineyard in Gumpisch beyond the Tällä in former times.

671861335139ccd3524bc9118270be340a2c6126.summary: In the municipality of Beinwil on the Hallwilersee, a large field on the mountainside bears the name Wingart, meaning vineyard.

dcad97791df562616187389924cdfa244f0d6000.summary: At the time when people began to clear and clean the forests of Switzerland, a hideous serpent and dreadful dragon, called a Lindwurm in the Swiss annals, was found in the land of Unterwalden.

ea4ca2dfa1886c57dd1082afd4aca13a1a293643.title: Wise Women around Kienberg
ea4ca2dfa1886c57dd1082afd4aca13a1a293643.author: Ernst Ludwig Rochholz
ea4ca2dfa1886c57dd1082afd4aca13a1a293643.summary: On the Frauenhalde, situated toward the woods by the little village of Kienberg in the Frickthale, there still live Erdweibchen regarded as wise and holy women.

2928ac0faafc4ce1883dae4f9ece0efe03019592.summary: A boy went on Stubeten visits to two girls in the little land of Uri who were no longer very young.

975569f8bd1f91dd3597e7590ed0226b1fb9aace.summary: a) Two farmhands belonging to Prosper Bär of Schattdorf—a wealthy farmer who also owned a field in the neighboring municipality of Bürglen—had spent an evening visiting three girls in Bürglen.

6b49109a9bb0762c7b4d3a1ef73be323896dce4c.title: Witch Story

8c74836805d8f8a27c4f9221e17fb81515c65b2b.summary: Toward evening, a woman from Wassen went to Silenen to see Doctor Lussmann on behalf of a gravely ill neighbor.

298ffbb0d40cc2e0f666a142b7f221895f5a4cf2.title: Women's Cunning (Uri)

46b5790de80ee2d8c377a8e46eecac3588cee293.author: H. Hartmann

3fbd6ed0ab214e4b6a1fa2c6b512cca9196c0305.title: Work at Pentecost

9b82d0100ac1785e931faea2a099bef54bb241c4.author: Dietrich Jecklin
9b82d0100ac1785e931faea2a099bef54bb241c4.summary: At the beginning of the hay and Emd harvest, late in the evening one not infrequently hears “dängeln” (sharpening scythes) in several hamlets or farmsteads of the Puschlav valley.

ff030093140ea94dc2c6a4676201f2dd23c4d68b.title: Working Longer, an Uberträttig
ff030093140ea94dc2c6a4676201f2dd23c4d68b.author: M. Sooder
ff030093140ea94dc2c6a4676201f2dd23c4d68b.summary: I was still a little schoolgirl when I had to spin throughout the whole evening.

f3832bbbdae44d52950beed116d6aa3b180ff58a.title: Wuatahee and Klagweh
f3832bbbdae44d52950beed116d6aa3b180ff58a.author: Jakob Kuoni
f3832bbbdae44d52950beed116d6aa3b180ff58a.summary: In the Rhine valley, Wotan’s raging host is called “Wuatahee” or “Wuatihee.” The “Klagweh” is distinguished from it.

80ba00c3dfe6e4198fb0b88f2c166e3a9ebbe4d6.title: Wüetihö

b6a9867e0a574264e773fd1cee9f05e34ef2f09d.title: Yes, Yes! If You Had Not Been Blessed!
b6a9867e0a574264e773fd1cee9f05e34ef2f09d.author: Josef Müller
b6a9867e0a574264e773fd1cee9f05e34ef2f09d.summary: Above Eisten in Meien, the small children were alone at home one day in an old black cottage while their parents worked on a remote property.

9c0e53e31c7d396a28edf4e7c9dfa89053f39a35.title: You Shouldn’t Have Said That!
9c0e53e31c7d396a28edf4e7c9dfa89053f39a35.author: Josef Müller
9c0e53e31c7d396a28edf4e7c9dfa89053f39a35.summary: One night a Senn at Gufern could find no peace at all in his hut; something kept waking him from sleep.

0cdbdabad7af81d0b5214060fc0f16bc747d646d.title: Zarèra
0cdbdabad7af81d0b5214060fc0f16bc747d646d.author: Dietrich Jecklin
0cdbdabad7af81d0b5214060fc0f16bc747d646d.summary: Above Pisciadella is a place containing nothing but the ruins of buildings, and to this day that place is called la Rovina (“the ruin”).

279bfcd31a29f4326f31f9c482a452ad2124f262.title: Zigeuner on St. Gotthard
279bfcd31a29f4326f31f9c482a452ad2124f262.author: Josef Müller
279bfcd31a29f4326f31f9c482a452ad2124f262.summary: A weary, heavily burdened little old woman who wanted to sit down and rest was threatened with Verlochen by a band of Zigeuner to which she belonged. This is what the Zigeuner do: they bury old people whom they deem no longer useful.

eef6eb23d507cd972ce2106ad52647b4d13848a3.title: Zwingli's Giant Leap
eef6eb23d507cd972ce2106ad52647b4d13848a3.author: Alois Lütolf
eef6eb23d507cd972ce2106ad52647b4d13848a3.summary: As is well known, the Reformer Ulrich Zwingli was a preacher in Einsiedeln between 1516 - 1518.

26651ba7c274ec6c390129666773795fbc16bcbb.title: Züsler (Oberuzwil, St. Gallen)
26651ba7c274ec6c390129666773795fbc16bcbb.author: Jakob Kuoni
26651ba7c274ec6c390129666773795fbc16bcbb.summary: Züsler—fiery men and movers of boundary markers—were often seen here.

a30a60626182c1ddf9a0989e43575c887c798ba0.title: ‘Did You Help with the Hunt…’
a30a60626182c1ddf9a0989e43575c887c798ba0.author: M. Sooder
a30a60626182c1ddf9a0989e43575c887c798ba0.summary: In the Sigerist house, Grossätti related, a small group used to gather between Christmas and New Year.

e082ba267d1e25f8cb5fb7922f23830b64bd8d48.title: ‘Guide It, Guide It’
e082ba267d1e25f8cb5fb7922f23830b64bd8d48.author: Josef Müller
e082ba267d1e25f8cb5fb7922f23830b64bd8d48.summary: One summer, a Bettlermandli went about the mountains of Bürglen and the Schächen Valley, but the people gave him too little, and he said he would yet play them a Schwirren.

34260c03927ec83f80a09f1806aa8204e85adf2a.title: “If I Had a Red Stocking.”
34260c03927ec83f80a09f1806aa8204e85adf2a.author: Josef Müller
34260c03927ec83f80a09f1806aa8204e85adf2a.summary: A dreadful storm poured down over Bürglen.

glossary.description: A high seasonal pasture and its working landscape, including huts, livestock and dairy work. It does not simply mean a mountain peak.
An Alpine dairyman responsible for the herd, milk processing and cheesemaking. Other workers and occupations appear beside the Senn in these tales.
A warm downslope wind in the Alps, sometimes described in the stories as violent or dangerous.
Literally a little mountain man: a supernatural mountain dweller. Its appearance and role depend on the particular telling.
glossary.example_title: A Bergmännchen Knows of a Treasure

glossary.description: A regional name often associated with a nightmare or pressure spirit. Local accounts do not always describe the same form.
glossary.example_title: In the Meien Valley (The Shadow Spirit)

glossary.description: A binding, prohibition or spell. In some tales it holds a person in place; its meaning should be read in context.
A horned mountain mammal adapted to steep, rocky terrain in the European Alps.
One of Switzerland’s constituent states. Place names such as Aargau may name a whole canton, rather than a single village.
